title: ECB Consumer Expectations Survey results – September 2026
body:
ECB Consumer Expectations Survey results – September 2026 Skip to: Skip to navigation Skip to content Skip to footer EN Български Čeština Dansk Deutsch Eλληνικά English Español Eesti keel Suomi Français Gaeilge Hrvatski Magyar Italiano Lietuvių Latviešu Malti Nederlands Polski Português Română Slovenčina Slovenščina Svenska Menu Search Menu ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Search Options Image Preview Sort by ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Suggestions Home Media Explainers Research & Publications Statistics Monetary Policy The €uro Payments & Markets Careers Suggestions Sort by Relevance Date PRESS RELEASE ECB Consumer Expectations Survey results – September 2026 23 October 2026 Compared with August 2026: median consumer perceptions of inflation over the past 12 months and expectations for inflation over the next 12 months increased slightly, while median expectations for inflation three years and five years ahead were unchanged; expectations for nominal income growth over the next 12 months increased, as did expectations for spending growth over the next 12 months; expectations for economic growth over the next 12 months decreased, while the expected unemployment rate in 12 months’ time increased; expectations for growth in the price of homes over the next 12 months increased, while expectations for mortgage interest rates in 12 months’ time remained unchanged Inflation In September the median rate of perceived inflation over the previous 12 months increased to 3.6% from 3.5% in August. Median expectations for inflation over the next 12 months also increased, to 3.1% from 3.0%. Median expectations for inflation three years ahead and median expectations for inflation five years ahead were unchanged at 2.9% and 2.5% respectively. Uncertainty about expectations for inflation over the next 12 months increased slightly, remaining higher than the level prior to the start of the conflict in the Middle East. Respondents in the bottom income quintile continued to report higher inflation perceptions and expectations, on average, than those in the top quintile. Younger respondents (aged 18-34) continued to report lower inflation perceptions and expectations than older respondents (aged 35-54 and 55-70). Inflation results Income and consumption Consumers’ expectations for nominal income growth over the next 12 months increased to 1.1% in September from 1.0% in August. As in previous months expectations were, on average, higher in the bottom income quintile (1.5%) than in the top quintile (1.2%). Perceived nominal spending growth over the previous 12 months increased to 5.3% from 5.2%, while expected nominal spending growth over the next 12 months increased to 3.7% from 3.6%. Income and consumption results Economic growth and labour market Expectations for economic growth over the next 12 months decreased in September to -1.5%, from -1.2% in August. Expectations for the unemployment rate 12 months ahead increased to 11.3%, from 11.0%. As observed in previous months, households in the bottom income quintile expected the highest unemployment rate 12 months ahead (13.6%), while households in the top income quintile expected the lowest rate (9.7%). Consumers continued to expect the future unemployment rate to be only slightly higher than the perceived current unemployment rate (10.6%), suggesting a broadly stable labour market outlook. Economic growth and labour market results Housing and credit access Consumers expected the price of their home to increase by 3.5% over the next 12 months, higher than in August (3.4%). As in previous months expectations for home price growth over the next 12 months remained, on average, higher in the lowest income quintile (4.0%) than in the highest income quintile (3.2%). Expectations for mortgage interest rates in 12 months’ time remained unchanged from July, at 4.9%. As in previous months, households in the top income quintile expected the lowest mortgage interest rates 12 months ahead (4.4%), while those in the bottom quintile expected the highest rates (5.7%). The net percentage of households reporting a tightening (relative to those reporting an easing) of access to credit over the previous 12 months increased compared with August, as did the net percentage of households expecting tighter credit conditions over the next 12 months (relative to those expecting an easing). Housing and credit access results The microdata underlying the aggregate results are available in the Data and methodological information section of the ECB Consumer Expectations Survey (CES) web page. The release of the CES results for October is scheduled for 27 November 2026. For media queries, please contact: Benoit Deeg , tel.: +49 172 1683704. Notes The fieldwork for the latest CES wave was carried out between 27 August and 28 September 2026. The main aggregate results for individual countries and the euro area are published on the ECB Data Portal and on the ECB’s website every month. Unless otherwise indicated, the statistics presented in this press release refer to the 2% winsorised mean. For further details, see ECB Consumer Expectations Survey – Guide to the computation of aggregate statistics . The CES is a monthly online survey of, currently, around 19,000 adult consumers (i.e. aged 18 or over) from 11 euro area countries: Belgium, Germany, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Austria, Portugal and Finland. The results are used for policy analysis and complement other data sources used by the ECB. Further information about the survey and the data collected is available on the CES web page . Detailed information can also be found in the following two publications: Bańkowska, K. et al., “ ECB Consumer Expectations Survey: an overview and first evaluation ”, Occasional Paper Series , No 287, ECB, Frankfurt am Main, December 2021; and Georgarakos, D. and Kenny, G., “ Household spending and fiscal support during the COVID-19 pandemic: Insights from a new consumer survey ”, Journal of Monetary Economics , Vol. 129, Supplement, July 2022, pp. S1-S14. The survey results do not represent the views of the ECB’s decision-making bodies or staff. title: Kazakhstan Expands Compute for Its AI Future
body: Kazakhstan’s AI ecosystem is moving from infrastructure plans to deployment. The shift is visible across the full AI stack — from infrastructure to models to applications. The announcements below — coinciding with a visit to Astana by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang — point to the nation’s increasing supply of accelerated computing, along with its growing demand for what comes next. On Friday, Oct. 23, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang visited Astana, meeting with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev at the Akorda Presidential Palace and joining Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiyev — Kazakhstan’s minister of AI and digital development — for a public fireside chat at the Alem.AI program. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Jensen Huang and Kazakhstan’s AI Minister Speak at Alem.AI In their fireside chat at Alem.AI, Kazakhstan’s international center for artificial intelligence, Madiyev and Huang discussed the country’s push to become an AI nation — building the energy and computing infrastructure to support homegrown AI and applying it across the economy. Madiyev said Kazakhstan wants AI that reflects its language and culture. “We want AI that understands and speaks Kazakh and captures cultural contexts and cultural specifics,” he said, describing the country’s work on Kazakh-language models. Huang said Kazakhstan could turn its energy resources into a foundation for AI production — and a new kind of export. “Instead of just exporting energy, in the future, you could transform energy into intelligence and export intelligence,” he said. He also argued that local data is central to that ambition: it embodies a country’s culture, history and values. “Your country’s data is your natural resource. It belongs to you.” The conversation also turned to physical AI. Madiyev pointed to Kazakhstan’s factories, mines, agriculture, transport and logistics as potential areas for development, asking how the country could become a hub for training models for robots and other physical systems. Huang called the idea “fantastic,” saying physical AI could transform industries from mining and mineral processing to agriculture. Huang said AI and robotics can help people do more, but ambition will shape how fully they seize that opportunity. He applied the idea to Kazakhstan, saying AI could help lift the country and its people. “If you have ambition, and I believe you do, AI will lift your nation,” Huang said. “AI will lift your people.” Huang also praised the founders of Higgsfield AI, the Kazakhstan-founded startup, and it was announced NVIDIA is making an investment into the startup during the event. “The first thing and the last thing is you invest in people, not companies,” he said, describing the founders as visionary and pointing to their effort to compete globally. Asked about AI security, Huang said the technology must be developed and deployed responsibly. He described NVIDIA’s OpenShell as a way to contain AI agents by limiting their access to files and tools and monitoring their activity. For young people entering a fast-changing field, Huang recommended learning how AI works — not just how to use it. He said aspiring AI programmers should understand the technology’s principles, strengths and weaknesses, combining technical knowledge with the ability to work effectively with AI. “I envy being 18 years old today… because the world is changing so rapidly, and there’s a complete reset because of technology.” The Infrastructure Layer Is Scaling The visits coincided with a signing ceremony marking Firebird’s investment agreement with the government of Kazakhstan, held at the presidential palace. Building on its first AI factory in Armenia, Firebird is expanding into Kazakhstan, where it has secured a U.S. export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs. The first phase is under construction with Kazakhtelecom at Data Center Valley, targeting commercial launch in the third quarter of 2027. A planned second phase would bring Firebird’s total potential AI infrastructure capacity in Kazakhstan to approximately 500 megawatts. Firebird also plans to establish Firebird Labs Kazakhstan to support local AI startups, research and talent development through funding, access to compute and research partnerships. Firebird cofounder and CEO Razmig Hovaghimian attended the signing ceremony at the Akorda Presidential Palace alongside government officials. “What began as a seed of an idea 180 days ago has grown into a major investment in Kazakhstan’s AI future,” said Razmig Hovaghimian, co-Founder and CEO of Firebird. “President Tokayev’s vision gave us the confidence to think bigger about what we can build together. With Jensen Huang here today, that ambition feels more tangible than ever. We’re building the infrastructure for Kazakhstan’s talent and ideas to reach the world.” Kazakhtelecom , the nation’s largest telecommunications company, has already deployed 400 NVIDIA H200 and 480 NVIDIA B300 GPUs in Astana and Almaty. Next year, the company plans to deploy more than 1,000 GPUs in the Data Center Valley, along with more than 1,000 NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs in the Ekibastuz region, serving diverse workloads with infrastructure that enterprises, developers and institutions can use at scale. AI-Native Companies Scale With Compute The nation’s AI-native companies are also building out their compute capacity — and the applications that run atop them. Higgsfield is expanding its AI infrastructure with NVIDIA Vera Rubin running on cloud service providers, giving the company additional capacity as models, products and customer demand for its generative media applications grow. More local capacity gives developers and companies room to train, fine-tune and serve increasingly capable models. Successful applications, in turn, create demand for more compute. Kazakhstan’s AI opportunity isn’t defined by GPU counts alone. Connecting that infrastructure with developers, universities, startups and industries can turn accelerated computing into useful applications. Today’s announcements represent different layers of that stack — infrastructure deployment, access to compute and AI-native product development — where the AI foundation is reaching new scale. Watch the fireside chat between Jensen Huang and Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiyev, streamed live from Alem.AI in Astana . Watch NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s GTC Berlin keynote in replay . Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements

title: Treasury Issues Proposed Rule to Implement Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act
body: October 22, 2026 WASHINGTON– The U.S. Department of the Treasury (Treasury) today issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) to propose updates to the Outbound Investment Security Program (OISP) based on direction from Congress in the Comprehensive Outbound Investment Security (COINS) Act, passed as part of the Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act.  The COINS Act codifies the U.S. Government’s approach to regulating certain outbound investments by U.S. persons and builds upon Treasury’s existing OISP. In passing the COINS Act, Congress made clear that restricting certain U.S. outbound investments into dual-use strategic technologies that benefit a foreign adversary’s military modernization efforts, surveillance states, and human rights abuses is necessary to prevent harm to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. President Trump is committed to protecting our national security and the implementation of the COINS Act is consistent with maintaining a strong, open investment environment that benefits our economy and supports our national security interests. The COINS Act directs the Secretary of the Treasury (the Secretary) to issue regulations that (1) require United States persons to provide notification to Treasury regarding certain transactions involving covered foreign persons that are engaged in notifiable technologies, and (2) prohibit United States persons from engaging in certain other transactions involving covered foreign persons that are engaged in prohibited technologies.  The COINS Act authorizes the Secretary to prescribe regulations with technical parameters for “prohibited technology” and “notifiable technology” in five technology sectors: semiconductor technologies and microelectronics; artificial intelligence systems; quantum information technologies; high-performance computing and supercomputing; and hypersonic systems.  The COINS Act also authorizes the Secretary—in consultation with the appropriate congressional committees and subject to notice and comment rulemaking—to add and define technologies beyond those specifically listed in the law that enable the military, intelligence, surveillance, or cyber-enabled capabilities of a country of concern.  Accordingly, the Secretary has added biotechnology to the proposed regulations. “Under President Trump’s leadership, we are committed to putting America’s national security first,” said Secretary Scott Bessent .  “The proposed regulations would strengthen the existing Outbound Investment Security Program to prevent our adversaries from using U.S. investment to develop critical technologies that threaten U.S. national security.  This important step also helps promote our commitment to an open investment environment by providing clarity to U.S. and foreign investors as well as an opportunity for them to provide feedback on the proposed regulations.” “The proposed regulations are designed to address risks that can arise when foreign adversaries try to benefit from U.S. investment in key technology sectors,” said Assistant Secretary of the Treasury for Investment Security Christopher Pilkerton.  Pilkerton added, “It will enhance the Outbound Investment Security Program and our efforts to protect U.S. national security.” The NPRM issued today provides details on key concepts and aspects of the program’s proposed implementation, including: Requirements applicable to a U.S. person (including any controlled foreign entities); Categories of covered national security transactions; Definitions; The scope of covered foreign persons; Excepted transactions; Technical specifications to inform the scope of covered national security transactions based on certain technologies and products in the areas of semiconductor technology and microelectronics, quantum information technologies, super intelligence systems, hypersonic systems, high-performance computing and supercomputing, and biotechnology; Information that a U.S. person is required to provide to Treasury as part of a notification; The process of requesting non-binding feedback and submitting confidential information; The knowledge standard and expectations for a U.S. person to conduct a reasonable and diligent inquiry prior to undertaking a transaction; and Conduct that would be treated as a violation of the proposed rule and applicable penalties for such conduct. Treasury invites comments from a wide range of stakeholders on all aspects of the NPRM including feedback on the scope of a covered national security transaction, definitions of key terms, the notification requirements, and the penalty and enforcement processes for violations, among other aspects.  Treasury will carefully consider this input before issuing the final implementing regulations. Written comments may be submitted by the deadline in the official NPRM, available at https://www.regulations.gov .  The NPRM will be followed at a later date by final implementing regulations, which will set an effective date for the program. The NPRM, fact sheet, and additional information are available at: https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/international/outbound-investment-program .

title: AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available
body: AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available Today, we’re announcing the general availability of AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities . AWS Continuum is a security service that finds and validates code vulnerabilities, then delivers fixes as patches you can automate or as pull requests in your repositories. AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities confirms which findings are exploitable in your environment, ranks the resulting issues by business impact, and proposes a fix for each one. Every remediation starts in a mode where Continuum proposes the fix and a person approves it before it ships. In the future, you will be able to decide which actions Continuum can take on its own, within the guardrails you define. Using frontier artificial intelligence (AI) models, threat actors can turn a vulnerability disclosure into working exploit code in minutes, and the same tools that speed up development also increase the volume of findings your teams must process. If your organization runs a large application estate, your scanners likely produce thousands of findings a day, and many of them need no action. A finding can be unreachable, unexploitable, or already mitigated by a runtime control. Generic severity scores don’t tell you which resources a threat actor can actually reach, so a critical score on a dev-only utility looks the same as a medium score on a service one step away from a payments database. Previously, confirming whether a finding was exploitable took hours of manual investigation, and shipping a fix with confidence took days of coordination across security, infrastructure, and application teams, because the blast radius of a change is hard to assess without business context. To close that gap, Continuum proves which findings are exploitable and bounds the risk of each fix it proposes. Continuum builds a context graph from two primary sources: your code repositories and your AWS environment. For AWS, you set up a collector in the account and Region where your code runs. The collector gathers resource details such as AWS Config resources and network configuration so Continuum can judge whether a vulnerability is reachable over the network and what a threat actor could reach from it. From this graph, Continuum learns which systems are business-critical, who owns them, how services depend on one another, and which data each one touches. It uses that picture to identify your highest-value systems, such as customer data stores, payment pipelines, and authentication services, and then ranks each resulting issue by how close its attack path runs to those systems. Continuum analyzes each finding against your code and its environment context and assigns an evidence level, such as a verdict proven by static analysis of the vulnerable code path. For findings it can reproduce, Continuum runs the exploit in an isolated sandbox and attaches proof-of-concept code with the reproduction steps. It produces the attack path, the supporting source analysis, and a blast radius assessment instead of a risk score alone. It also evaluates whether your existing defenses would detect and stop the validated path. For each confirmed issue, Continuum generates a fix (a code patch, a dependency upgrade, or a configuration change) and opens it as a pull request in your connected repository, ready to review. Every fix requires human approval: you review and merge the pull request, so the final decision stays with your team. In the future, you will be able to build confidence in specific remediation classes and let Continuum apply those fixes automatically once its confidence gates pass, such as test coverage, scope bounds, and historical success rate. AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities in action To show how this works, I open AWS Continuum in the console and go to Code vulnerabilities . Before I can review issues, I set up an environment. I connect a code source, either a GitHub integration or an Amazon S3 bucket, and then create an environment that scans it on a schedule I choose. An Amazon S3 source has a couple of prerequisites: the bucket sits in the same account and AWS Region where I turn on AWS Continuum, and I grant access through an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role that AWS Continuum assumes. I can optionally add AWS infrastructure context by setting up an AWS Continuum collector in the account and Region where my code runs and authorizing my environment to use it. For the full requirements and steps, see the AWS Continuum User Guide . The Overview page brings these pieces together in one place, showing my Code integrations , the Environments built on them, and the status of any AWS collector that supplies AWS resource context. I open one of my environments. The Issues tab lists validated, prioritized issues rather than raw scanner output, each with a severity, a status, and the time it was created. I choose one of the issues. The Overview rates it High severity, with the status Completed and the remediation already Delivered to GitHub. The Risk assessment explains why. Continuum rates its Exploitability as Exploitable , with an evidence level of Static proven and a validation run status of Completed . Likelihood is High , since the service is reachable from an attacker, requires no authentication, and needs no user interaction. Impact is Moderate , which means an attacker gains the ability to modify business data, with a blast radius reaching other users in the same tenant. A Proof section includes the source analysis behind the verdict. The Remediation section shows a fix already delivered as a pull request in GitHub, changing four files, with 50 lines added and 24 removed across the cart service. Continuum opens the fix as a pull request titled Continuum fix , and I choose View pull request to open it in GitHub. The console is explicit that a generated patch does not mean the issue is fixed. I still review and merge it, which keeps the final decision with my team. A Contributing findings section lists the specific scanner finding this issue was built from. The pull request description carries the same risk assessment, remediation summary, and proof from the console, so whoever reviews it in GitHub sees the evidence without leaving their workflow. The Findings tab lists the raw scanner findings across the environment, the evidence that issues are built from. The Scans tab shows the history of each scan with its status, origin, and request and completion times, and I use Configure scan frequency to change the cadence or Queue scan to run one on demand. The Configuration tab is where I manage the environment: the code and context sources it reads from, its code integrations, environment settings such as whether Continuum creates remediation patches, and the AWS collectors it uses for AWS context. In a single workflow, I work through the validated issues in priority order with each scan, reviewing the evidence and scope behind each one before I approve and merge the fixes I trust. Every fix waits for my approval, so the backlog keeps shrinking while my team keeps control of what ships. Now available AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is available today in US East (N. Virginia) and US West (Oregon) Regions. For pricing, visit the pricing page . To learn more, visit the AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities product page and the User Guide . Give it a try in the AWS Continuum console today, and send us feedback through your usual AWS Support contacts. — Esra

title: Regulators unveil plans to simplify Senior Manager and Certification Regime
body:
Regulators unveil plans to simplify Senior Manager and Certification Regime | Bank of England – the UK's central bank Our use of cookies We use necessary cookies to make our site work. We’d also like to use some non-essential cookies (including third-party cookies) to help us improve the site. By clicking ‘Accept recommended settings’ on this banner, you accept our use of analytics cookies.   For more information on how these cookies work please see our Cookie policy . Accept recommended cookies Proceed with necessary cookies only Skip to main content Regulators unveil plans to simplify Senior Manager and Certification Regime The number of financial services roles required to face enhanced checks from regulators will fall significantly under proposals that will support growth. Published on  
        22 October 2026 News release The number of financial services roles required to face enhanced checks from regulators will fall significantly under proposals that will support growth. The changes are expected to save firms around £2 billion over a 10-year period. The Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) and Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) have today announced parallel consultations on proposals to significantly streamline the Senior Managers and Certification regime (SM&CR). The SM&CR was introduced 10 years ago to instil a culture of accountability among senior decision-makers in regulated firms. Under the proposals, unnecessary burdens will be removed while high standards of individual accountability and conduct will remain unchanged, including the regulators’ commitment to ensuring that individuals are accountable for misconduct that affects society as well as their employers. The changes will allow firms to focus more resources to ensure good customer and market outcomes, recruit and appoint talent, and prioritise innovation and investment, all supporting UK growth and competitiveness. The key changes to the regime include: Regulator pre-approval will be removed for a range of regulatory functions, including Chief Actuaries and Chairs of Risk and Audit Committees. Firms will instead notify regulators of these appointments directly, gaining speed and flexibility while remaining responsible for ensuring candidates are fit and proper. Removing the Certification Regime and associated administrative requirements for around 139,000 individuals below senior manager level to be subject to annual certification checks and appear on the Financial Services Register. Raising the conduct rule breach reporting threshold for most staff below senior manager level and streamlining Conduct Rule training requirements. This enables firms to better target more serious misconduct. Certain Senior Manager roles, such as CEOs, CFOs and Chairs, will continue to require regulator pre-approval, including fit and proper tests, before appointment. Regulators will also be able to require pre-approval for otherwise notified roles in high-risk cases. Firms will remain responsible for ensuring their employees remain competent, suitable and meet appropriate standards of conduct, and those no longer requiring pre-approval will continue to be held to the same level of accountability as before. Katharine Braddick, Deputy Governor for Prudential Regulation and Chief Executive Officer of the PRA, said: “The Senior Managers Regime is an essential part of the UK’s regulatory framework. These proposals keep checks in place for the most important roles, meaning individuals are accountable for their actions, but reduce the administrative burden where it isn’t needed, giving firms more time to invest in growth-focused activities and greater flexibility in onboarding senior talent.” Sarah Pritchard, Deputy CEO, said: “SM&CR has delivered significant improvements in accountability and governance across financial services. We remain committed to ensuring individual accountability and good standards of behaviour across financial services. But we can achieve the same impact with a more streamlined regime, supporting our aim to be a smarter regulator.” Some of the proposed reforms require legislative change. By consulting now, the FCA and PRA will be ready to implement reforms quickly once legislation is passed. The consultations are now open until 22 January, seeking views on how the regime can be made more proportionate while maintaining high standards of individual accountability and conduct. The consultations invite feedback on all aspects of the proposals with policy expected to follow in 2027. This was announced as part of Mansion House speeches delivered by Katharine Braddick and Nikhil Rathi. In her speech, Katharine unveiled a five-year strategy for the PRA designed to transform the regulator, focusing on the resilience of the financial sector, the regulator’s growth and competitiveness objective, innovating with data and technology and boosting transparency. Notes to editors Read and engage with the PRA’s consultation . Read and respond to the FCA's consultation , and review the accompanying cost-benefit analysis. These consultations are the second and most significant phase of SM&CR reform. They build on changes in April 2026 , including longer timelines for senior manager applications following unexpected or temporary changes, removal of duplicate certification requirements for overlapping functions, and a 30% increase in enhanced firm thresholds for larger firms. The reforms are expected to reduce PRA SM&CR pre-approvals by 43% and halve the overall burden of the PRA regime. For FCA Enhanced solo-regulated firms where fewer SMFs apply, around 15% of applications would move to notification and 2 SMF roles would be removed, saving a further 19%. The PRA’s latest quarterly data shows that 98% of applications were determined within the proposed new two-month statutory deadline, compared with 98.3% in the FCA’s most recent quarterly metrics. The proposals build on wider PRA and FCA initiatives to support growth and competitiveness, including reforms to the ring-fencing regime to enable more flexible sharing of operational resources, proposals to index over 100 PRA thresholds to nominal GDP growth, and FCA reforms to strengthen the attractiveness of UK capital markets and support investment, and joint PRA/FCA initiatives to help innovative firms start up, scale up and compete internationally. title: Minutes of the Securities Lending Committee meeting – September 2026
body:
Minutes of the Securities Lending Committee meeting – September 2026 | Bank of England – the UK's central bank Our use of cookies We use necessary cookies to make our site work. We’d also like to use some non-essential cookies (including third-party cookies) to help us improve the site. By clicking ‘Accept recommended settings’ on this banner, you accept our use of analytics cookies.   For more information on how these cookies work please see our Cookie policy . Accept recommended cookies Proceed with necessary cookies only Skip to main content Minutes of the Securities Lending Committee meeting – September 2026 The Securities Lending Committee is a forum for market participants and authorities to discuss the UK securities lending market. Published on  
        22 October 2026 Date: 15 September 2026 Time: 2.30pm – 4.30pm | Location: Bank of England, 20 Moorgate, London EC2R 6DA Minutes Item 1: Welcome and introductory remarks The Chair opened the meeting and welcomed the members and observers. Item 2: Diversity, Equity & Inclusion The Committee discussed the developing strategies for attracting and retaining early career talent in the securities finance industry. Development and retainment strategies aimed to provide early career staff with opportunities to diversify knowledge and experience across firms. Other initiatives included firm-wide roll out of leadership programmes driving alignment across the workforce. Item 3: SLC Tax & Regs Update The SLC Tax & Regulations sub-committee provided an update noting increased operational challenges created by holding-period rules and record date requirements across national tax regimes. Implementation of T+1 accelerated settlement could amplify existing issues, should firms fail to adapt. The group noted the need for greater tax harmonisation and monitoring tax-related risk across jurisdictions. Item 4: T+1 Update Industry participants are broadly on track for implementation in October 2027 but there are significant differences in readiness between firms. Operational challenges around securities lending recalls, collateral sourcing, funding, settlement timing, partial settlements and agent lender capabilities persist. Future competitiveness may depend on collateral agility, automation, real-time processing and the ability to support same-day operational workflows. The group noted that T+1 readiness extends beyond compliance and requires scalable operating models capable of supporting future market changes. Item 5: Market update The Committee made observations on business growth, capital optimisation and market evolution and discussed increased use of central counterparties, collateral efficiency mechanisms and smart collateral structures. Members highlighted growth opportunities in newer markets and the growing importance of digital asset initiatives, including the rise of tokenisation programmes. Digital collateral discussions centred on how infrastructure projects could eventually reshape financing markets. Upcoming regulatory developments, mandatory clearing requirements and operational changes could affect lenders, borrowers and investment funds over the coming years. Item 6: Changes in the Digital Landscape The group discussed digital assets and market infrastructure noting regulatory developments supporting tokenisation, digital securities, collateral usage, and digital market infrastructure programmes. There are multiple industry working groups examining repo, collateral mobility, payments, legal frameworks and digital securities issuance. Practical use cases remain the critical challenge. The group discussed a legal case involving the potential re-characterisation of a securities financing transaction as a secured loan, where the outcome could have significant implications for repos, securities lending and contractual certainty. Members noted the pace of development in artificial intelligence and characterised current adoption as primarily efficiency-driven rather than fully autonomous decision-making. Use cases have tended to centre on administrative tasks, information retrieval, data aggregation, recall processing and enhanced transparency across funding and collateral books. The group discussed evolution of AI use from individual productivity tools into strategic infrastructure with the potential to influence trading activity, client selection, collateral mobility and decision-making. Concerns remain around use of AI in governance, resilience, vendor oversight and data security, particularly if AI systems gained access to sensitive operational data. Item 7: AOB No further business. title: NVIDIA Unveils Minerva to Bring End-to-End Observability for AI Factories
body: NVIDIA Unveils Minerva to Bring End-to-End Observability for AI Factories New AIOps platform connects infrastructure and workload telemetry to help operators increase uptime and maximize AI factory yield. October 22, 2026 by Brian Sparks 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Launched today, NVIDIA Minerva is an AIOps platform built to help teams find problems earlier and keep AI factories productive. It brings together telemetry from infrastructure and AI workloads, then applies purpose-built AI models to turn that data into timely, actionable insight. AI factories are among the most complex operations in the world, with vast numbers of GPUs working across high-speed networks to train models and serve AI applications. At that scale, a single degraded component can slow an entire job. The warning signs may be easy to miss, such as a GPU running hotter than its peers or an NVMe drive losing performance under load. The platform focuses on AI factory yield, a measure of the useful work infrastructure produces through GPU hours, goodput, cluster uptime and token production. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Delivering a Dynamic View of an AI Factory Traditional monitoring tools often divide the data center into separate views. Networking, compute, site reliability and machine learning teams each see a different part of the operation. Minerva connects those signals across NVIDIA GPUs, networking, storage, schedulers and workloads. With these signals, Minerva builds a dynamic knowledge graph that logically maps the infrastructure — GPUs, SuperNICs, switches and cables — and the jobs running on it. This context helps operators trace a slow training job to the component affecting it, even across a factory with hundreds of thousands of GPUs. It analyzes billions of data points per hour using supervised and unsupervised machine learning. It learns normal behavior, detects previously unseen anomalies, predicts emerging failures and correlates related events based on the factory’s topology. Instead of sending every symptom to an operator, it can group an event storm into a focused incident with a likely root cause. Minerva comes with a native AI assistant and connects to external agentic AI tools. This adds a natural-language interface grounded in live telemetry. Operators can investigate cluster health and receive recommended remediation through conversation. Teams can keep a person in the loop to manually implement fixes or connect Minerva to automation through infrastructure application programming interfaces and external systems. Results That Maximize AI Factory Yield The ability to correlate workload and infrastructure issues along with its agentic AI capabilities help simplify AI factory operations. Instead of dealing with a blizzard of alerts, Minerva aggregates related problems into a single actionable item. This allows AIOps teams to move from reactive to proactive maintenance. And all of this helps AI factories maximize GPU uptime. Minerva delivers value for the key metrics AI factories focus on: Longer time between interruptions : Minerva spots trouble before it happens, so jobs run longer without incident. Faster time to repair : When an incident does happen, Minerva pinpoints the problem, leading to a significantly quicker resolution. Greater insight : Modern AI infrastructure generates a flood of data; Minerva filters it out, leaving only the handful of alerts that actually matter. IREN is among the NVIDIA partners using Minerva to optimize its AI factories. “As we scale our AI factories, the key to providing the best service for our customers is maximizing the productivity of our GPUs,” said Denis Skrinnikoff, chief technology officer of IREN. “NVIDIA Minerva gives our operations team one view across the network, the GPUs and the jobs running on them, so we focus more on proactive maintenance rather than troubleshooting. That visibility strengthens our operating model for the infrastructure we’re building next.” Joining IREN , Aolani , Bitdeer AI , IBM , Jio, Lambda , Quake AI and Tesla plan to deploy Minerva. In addition to Dell Technologies , Lenovo and Supermicro will offer Minerva as part of their AI factory operations portfolios. Learn more about NVIDIA Minerva . See notice regarding software product information. body: Cloud Deployment Incoming: ‘Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’ Arrives on GeForce NOW Get memberships through Amazon on Fire TV, rally a party in ‘FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE’ and explore Season Two of ‘The Elder Scrolls Online.’ October 22, 2026 by GeForce NOW Community 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Lock in and load out this GFN Thursday. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 arrives on GeForce NOW at launch, bringing a new campaign, multiplayer action and DMZ, high-stakes extraction mode to supported devices . The campaign also gets an enhanced look: GeForce RTX 5080-class performance arrives for Ultimate members, bringing support for ray-tracing features in the cloud. There’s a new way to join the cloud, too: Existing supported Fire TV Stick users can now purchase one-month Performance or Ultimate memberships directly through Amazon, making it easier to sign up and start streaming on the big screen. Plus, Square Enix’s FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE brings cinematic pixel art and strategic battles to the cloud, and The Elder Scrolls Online’s Echoes of Skyrim Season adds the entire Greymoor Chapter free for all ESO Standard Edition owners. It’s all part of six games joining the GeForce NOW library this week. Deployment Without the Downloads Squad up and answer the call on the cloud. Activision and Infinity Ward’s Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches today on GeForce NOW. Members can drop into the trenches in Korea, close-quarter combat in New York, high-octane chases through Paris, night raids in Mumbai and city-wide engagements to reclaim occupied territory. Fight as Private Park, a young South Korean soldier facing live combat for the first time alongside his squad as a routine patrol turns into a desperate fight for survival. Beyond the front lines, operator-turned-outlaw Captain Price is operating outside the system he once served, pursuing revenge through covert missions as the conflict spreads. Multiplayer pairs precise combat with fluid movement, a dozen core 6v6 maps from around the world and battlegrounds that are shaped by the campaign’s global conflict. The DMZ extraction mode sends players into contested territory to recover valuable technology, weigh objectives and decide when to get out. Loot, fight, negotiate, betray and extract — it’s all fair in the cloud and battleground. Ultimate members can now experience the campaign with ray tracing, powered by newly added GeForce RTX 5080-class performance across PCs, Macs, handhelds, mobile devices, browsers, supported TVs and more. With game downloads and installs handled by GeForce NOW, members can spend less time preparing a local rig and more time preparing the next loadout. A New Way to Play A new way to join GeForce NOW on Fire TV. GeForce NOW in-app purchase is rolling out to existing supported Fire TV Stick users, making it possible to purchase a membership directly through Amazon using an existing account. Transactions are processed through Amazon’s billing system, creating a more seamless path from setup to gameplay. GeForce NOW transforms Fire TV into a powerful PC gaming rig in the cloud. Members can stream supported PC games they already own or purchase new titles from digital stores including Steam, Epic Games Store, Ubisoft Connect, Xbox PC Game Pass, GOG and EA. The library includes thousands of ready-to-play games, including many of the world’s most-played titles and more than 100 free-to-play games. No downloads, installs, patches or updates stand between a new game and playtime. An Amazon Fire TV Stick, the GeForce NOW app and an Ultimate membership are all it takes to level up the living room with GeForce RTX 5080-powered gaming. A Pixel-Perfect Fantasy Classic roots. A new adventure. Square Enix’s FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE launches today on GeForce NOW, bringing the series’ classic roots into a cinematic pixel-art world. Travel with companions bound by fate and uncover the truth behind a force threatening to bring everything to ruin. Strengthen the party with Visions of beloved FINAL FANTASY characters, each bringing unique skills and abilities to battle. Dynamic camera angles and pixelized 3D models give familiar fantasy a fresh perspective. Exploit enemy weaknesses to stagger foes, break their defenses and seize extra turns before finishing the bonus phase with powerful Resonance attacks. Airships, crystals, espers and moogles bring familiar series favorites to a world filled with secrets to discover. GeForce NOW handles the game’s downloads and storage in the cloud, leaving more space on supported devices for everyday essentials. Save the inventory management for potions and Phoenix Downs. Step Into a New Season in Tamriel Familiar lands. Fresh reasons to return. The Elder Scrolls Online ’s second season , Echoes of Skyrim , launched Wednesday, Oct. 21, free for all ESO players and ready to stream through GeForce NOW. Season Two gives everyone who owns ESO Standard Edition access to its Skyrim content and the Antiquities treasure-hunting system. The Markarth downloadable content follows Monday, Nov. 9, rounding out the additions with two classic zones to explore. The Season also introduces Solo Dungeons, reimagining challenges previously designed for groups. Moon Hunter Keep and March of Sacrifices have been redesigned and rebalanced for players ready to tackle their dangers alone. Earn new rewards and take on new challenges at your own pace without needing to find a group. A new Tamriel Tome also launched Oct. 21, offering both free and premium battle pass reward tracks. In addition, members can look for the following titles joining the GeForce NOW library this week: We Were Here Tomorrow (New release on Steam , Oct. 20) FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE (New release on Steam , Oct. 22) Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 (New release on Oct 23, available in the Call of Duty app) CONTROL Resonant ( Epic Game Store ) Crimson Desert ( Epic Games Store ) Planet Zoo 2 ( Xbox app , supports XBOX Play Anywhere) Dates listed above reflect when games are released on their respective stores. GeForce NOW availability may vary, as games are onboarded after release and added throughout the week. Keep an eye on GeForce NOW channels and GFN Thursdays for availability updates on announced titles. Gamers who want to test out high-performance GeForce NOW cloud gaming can start with a day pass to try premium cloud gaming before committing to a membership. Better yet, the cost of the day pass can be applied toward a first monthly membership — making it easy to try GeForce RTX-powered cloud gaming with the latest releases, then level up for more. What’s on the mission board this weekend? Let us know on X or in the comments below. title: The Trump Administration is Making Homeownership More Affordable
body: October 22, 2026 Proposed Rules Implement the ROAD to Housing Act and Support Affordable Homeownership in America WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury issued proposed regulations to make homeownership more affordable for hardworking Americans. The proposed regulations implement Section 1001 of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (ROAD to Housing Act), which restricts large institutional investors from purchasing single-family homes, codifying key requirements of President Trump’s Executive Order 14376 , Stopping Wall Street from Competing with Main Street Homebuyers . “Under President Trump, this Administration continues to restore the path to affordable homeownership for millions of young and working families,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent . “Treasury is working to ensure American families and workers have a fair shot at purchasing homes in their communities by increasing housing supply and limiting large institutional investors’ role in the market, while supporting a strong, stable housing market and avoiding unnecessary disruption.” RESTORING THE AMERICAN DREAM OF HOMEOWNERSHIP Beginning on January 7, 2027, a large institutional investor generally may not purchase, or enter into a contract to purchase, a single-family home unless the purchase qualifies as an “excepted purchase” under the ROAD to Housing Act. The ROAD to Housing Act defines a large institutional investor by reference to, among other things, whether an entity is engaged in the business of investing in, owning, renting, managing, or holding single-family homes and has direct or indirect investment control over at least 350 such homes. The ROAD to Housing Act permits several categories of excepted purchases, including purchases made pursuant to build-to-rent programs, renovate-to-rent programs, homeownership programs, and programs to boost homeownership. Today’s NPRM sets forth Treasury’s proposed framework to: Establish standards for purchases made pursuant to build-to-rent programs that promote continued investment in new housing; Provide a safe harbor for purchases made pursuant to renovate-to-rent programs that bring neglected homes back into the housing supply and up to code; Clarify the requirements for homeownership programs and programs to boost homeownership, including providing safe harbors for large institutional investors that provide meaningful financial support towards their renters’ purchase of a home; Clarify that an entity is engaged “in the business of” investing in , owning, renting, managing, or holding single-family homes when it does so for the purpose of receiving income or financial gain, and not incidentally to a different business; Define when an entity may qualify as a passive investor in another entity that owns a home because it does not share directors or officers with the other entity and does not have a property control right over the underlying homes; Clarify certain purchases involving debts previously contracted, loss mitigation, and transfers between large institutional investors that protect the liquidity of the housing market; and Clarify the calculation of the maximum civil penalty where a single prohibited purchase involves more than one large institutional investor. The proposed rule would provide non-exclusive safe harbors for several statutory requirements. These include standards for determining whether a home has been substantially rehabilitated under a renovate-to-rent program, whether a renter has received meaningful financial support under certain homeownership programs, and whether a renter has received a right of first refusal and 30-day first-look period. Treasury’s proposed approach recognizes that housing-market participants use a variety of ownership, investment, construction, servicing, and property-management structures and seeks to provide clarity without unnecessary disruption to housing supply, homebuilding, rehabilitation activity, or capital formation. Members of the public should submit comments in response to the NPRM within 30 days after publication in the Federal Register. The proposed regulations are available here . ###

title: Jury finds two Missoula men guilty of trafficking meth as part of multistate drug ring
body: Press Release Jury finds two Missoula men guilty of trafficking meth as part of multistate drug ring Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Montana MISSOULA – Two Missoula men who were accused of trafficking methamphetamine as part of a multistate drug ring were found guilty by a federal jury today, First Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark Steger Smith said. Following a four-day trial, Arthur Ray Peoples, 69, and Joseph Frederick Ployhar, 45, were found guilty of conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine, possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine, and distribution of methamphetamine. The two men each face 15 years to life of prison, a $20 million fine and at least 10 years of supervised release. Their mandatory minimum sentences are increased because each has a prior conviction for a serious drug felony. U.S. District Judge William W. Mercer presided and will determine a sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. Peoples and Ployhar were detained pending further proceedings. The government alleged in court documents and at trial that an investigation of a multistate drug ring identified Peoples as one of multiple meth dealers in Montana. Law enforcement used a confidential informant who bought roughly 27 grams of meth from Peoples on Jan. 28, 2025. Following the buy, investigators put Peoples under surveillance and then pulled him over when they suspected a drug deal was about to happen. In his vehicle, officers found several small baggies containing meth. From there, they searched his motel room and found more meth, digital scales, baggies, and ledgers. Ployhar was similarly identified through the course of the drug ring investigation. He was pulled over returning from Washington with another defendant, Jamie Maki . Investigators searched the vehicle and found roughly two and a half pounds of meth. Maki pleaded guilty earlier this year to drug trafficking charges and will be sentenced on Feb. 4, 2027. The U.S. Attorney’s Office prosecuted the case. The Missoula Drug Task Force conducted the investigation. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. Contact Keri Leggett Acting Public Affairs Officer keri.leggett@usdoj.gov Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Project Safe Neighborhoods Component USAO - Montana Press Release Number: 26-274
retained_feed_body: A pair of Missoula men who were accused of trafficking methamphetamine as part of a multistate drug ring were found guilty by a federal jury today.

title: Convicted Firearms Trafficker Indicted for Possessing Firearms and Ammunition
body: Press Release Convicted Firearms Trafficker Indicted for Possessing Firearms and Ammunition Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts Defendant committed the alleged criminal conduct weeks after being released from federal prison BOSTON – A convicted firearms trafficker from Revere has been indicted by a federal grand jury for being a felon in possession of firearms. Cory Daigle, 31, of Revere, was indicted on charges of being a felon in possession of firearms and ammunition. The defendant will be arraigned at a later date. In August 2024 , Daigle was convicted of unlawfully trafficking in firearms, possessing a machinegun, receiving or possessing an unregistered firearm and additional firearms-related offenses. Daigle was sentenced to approximately two years in prison in that case and, according to court documents, had only been released from Bureau of Prisons custody a few weeks before he was allegedly found to possess 11 firearms, more than 100 rounds of ammunition and additional firearm components during a search of his residence on June 25, 2026. The charge of being a felon in possession of firearms and ammunition provides for a sentence of up to 15 years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Jeff Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England; and Justin Page, Acting Inspector in Charge of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service’s Boston Division made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives, Boston Field Division and the Revere and Boston Police Departments. Assistant U.S. Attorney Julissa Walsh of the Major Crimes Unit is prosecuting the case. The details contained in the charging document are allegations. The defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in the court of law. Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: High‑Speed Pursuit, Crash into Police Cruiser, Unlawful Possession of Loaded Glock, Yield a 28-Month Sentence for D.C. Felon
body: Press Release High‑Speed Pursuit, Crash into Police Cruiser, Unlawful Possession of Loaded Glock, Yield a 28-Month Sentence for D.C. Felon Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia WASHINGTON - Trevon Troxler, 31, a previously convicted felon residing in the District, was sentenced today in U.S. District Court to 28 months incarceration in connection with a high‑speed flight from law enforcement that resulted in a collision with a federal police cruiser and the recovery of a loaded Glock 29 pistol, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. Troxler pleaded guilty on May 13, 2026, before U.S. District Judge Amy Berman Jackson to unlawful possession of a firearm and ammunition by a felon, and to destruction of federal property. In addition to the 28‑month prison term, Judge Berman Jackson ordered Troxler to serve three years of supervised release. Federal prosecutors had requested a 33‑month prison term. According to court documents, on Oct. 12, 2025, about 8:20 p.m., Troxler fled from law enforcement after officers attempted to stop the white Honda Accord he was driving in the 3500 block of Ames Street NE. Troxler led MPD officers and a Diplomatic Security Service agent through multiple sections of the city at high speed, striking a federal police cruiser and an uninvolved Hyundai. The collision with the Hyundai sent the car off the roadway and into a residence on the 1600 block of Eastern Avenue NE. After the collision, Troxler continued to flee in the Honda, traveling northbound on I-295, where he swerved in and out of traffic at a high rate of speed. As Troxler entered the ramp to Route 50, the Honda hit the federal police cruiser again. The Honda approached 33rd Place Northeast, and it struck a median in the roadway and stopped. Troxler opened the vehicle door, exited the vehicle, and fled on foot. Police quickly apprehended him at 2300 South Dakota Ave. NE. Officers recovered a loaded firearm from the driver’s side of Troxler’s vehicle. The weapon was a Glock 29 equipped with a laser attachment and loaded with one round in the chamber and 26 rounds in a high‑capacity magazine. Troxler caused more than $4,000 in damage to the federal police cruiser, which was property of the United States. Troxler has a previous conviction for unauthorized use of a vehicle and receiving stolen property, and another felony conviction for attempted assault with a dangerous weapon and unlawful possession of a firearm (crime of violence). The investigation was conducted by the Metropolitan Police Department, the Diplomatic Security Service, and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives - Washington Field Office. The matter was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Emory V. Cole of the Federal Major Crimes Section under the President’s Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful Again initiative, which targets violent crime by prioritizing federal prosecution of armed repeat offenders and removing illegal firearms from District neighborhoods. 25cr242 Follow us on X , Instagram , and YouTube Or at https://www.justice.gov/usao-dc Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - District of Columbia

title: Gang Member Pleads Guilty to Federal Gun and Drug Charges
body: Press Release Gang Member Pleads Guilty to Federal Gun and Drug Charges Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts Defendant manufactured and sold firearms, silencers and machinegun conversion devices; distributed controlled substances; and committed an armed home invasion while on state parole for armed robberies BOSTON – A Vice Lord gang member from Athol, Mass. has pleaded guilty in federal court in Boston to gun and drug charges. At the time of the offenses the defendant was on parole following multiple six- to 10-year concurrent state prison sentences. Keith Harlow, a/k/a “Lord Savage,” 40, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to distribute controlled substances; being a felon in possession of firearm and ammunition; conspiracy to interfere with commerce by robbery; and engaging in the business of manufacturing and dealing in firearms without a license. U.S. District Court Judge Indira Talwani scheduled sentencing for Jan. 12, 2027. Harlow was charged in May 2025, however he remained a fugitive until his arrest in August 2025 . Harlow is a member of a Vice Lords chapter known as the Four Corner Hustlers. Known by his street name “Lord Savage,” Harlow has been convicted of multiple prior armed robberies and, at the time of the offenses, was on parole following multiple six to 10-year concurrent state prison sentences. In 2025, while on state parole, Harlow sent numerous text messages and was captured in photographs and video recordings in possession of firearms, a suppressor and machinegun conversion device, commonly known as a selector “switch.” In numerous text messages, Harlow discussed the manufacturing of firearms and selector switches and the sale of numerous firearms he had in his possession. One of the firearms seized during the investigation was purchased by co-conspirator Andrew Poor and given to Harlow. Further investigation of Poor revealed his involvement in a January 2025 home invasion of a residence in Athol. Dante Machuca was also identified as participating in the home invasion, along with Harlow and Poor. According to the charging documents, Harlow, Poor and Machuca, entered into the residence of a suspected drug dealer armed with firearms in order to rob the dealer of drugs and proceeds. Harlow engaged in a struggle with the dealer and fired his weapon to demonstrate its authenticity, before putting the hot barrel of the firearm against the victim’s abdomen. At the time of this home invasion, Harlow was on parole for multiple state prison terms. During a search of Harlow’s residence on May 29, 2025, multiple firearm receivers, suspected firearm suppressors, machinegun conversion devices, 3D printers and firearm manufacturing supplies were recovered. Approximately 100 grams of suspected cocaine was also found in the residence. A review of Perry’s cellphone seized during his arrest on state charges on May 29, 2025, revealed that Harlow and Perry worked together to distribute controlled substances and sell firearms throughout Massachusetts. In text message communications, Harlow and Perry discussed committing multiple robberies and using firearms to shoot at various individuals. At the time of the offenses, Harlow and Perry were prohibited from possessing firearms due to numerous prior felony convictions, including Perry’s youthful offender conviction of manslaughter. At the time of all the messages, Harlow was on parole following multiple concurrent state prison sentences for multiple armed robberies and Perry was on probation for a domestic violence offense. Perry was sentenced in September 2026 to 97 months in prison, to be followed by three years of supervised release. The charge of being a felon in possession of a firearm provides for a sentence of up to 15 years in prison, up to three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. The charge of conspiring to distribute controlled substances provides for a sentence of up to 20 years, at least three years and up to a lifetime of supervised release and a fine of up to $1 million. The charge of unlicensed manufacturing and dealing in firearms provides for a sentence of up to five years in prison, up to three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. The charge of conspiracy to interfere with commerce by robbery provides for a sentence of up to 20 years in prison, up to three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Boston Division; David E. Sullivan, Northwestern District Attorney; and Athol Police Chief Craig Lundgren made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the United States Marshal Service in Massachusetts; the U.S. Marshal’s Service in the Northern District of Georgia; United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia; the Massachusetts State Police; the Franklin County House of Correction; and the Massachusetts Department of Correction. Assistant U.S. Attorney Philip A. Mallard of the Organized Crime & Gang Unit is prosecuting the case. Updated October 22, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Violent Crime Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: Federal Awards Bring Nearly $1.5 Million to Jefferson County During Domestic Violence Awareness Month
body: Press Release Federal Awards Bring Nearly $1.5 Million to Jefferson County During Domestic Violence Awareness Month Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Alabama BIRMINGHAM, Ala. – As the Department of Justice and communities across the country observe Domestic Violence Awareness Month this October, new federal awards totaling nearly $1.5 million are coming to two of Jefferson County’s key partners in the fight against domestic violence: the Jefferson County District Attorney’s Office and One Place Metro Alabama Family Justice Center. The Department of Justice’s Office on Violence Against Women (OVW) has awarded $750,000 through its Improving Criminal Justice Responses program to Jefferson County, on behalf of the Jefferson County District Attorney’s Office. Authorized by the Violence Against Women Act (VAWA), the program supports partnerships among governments, courts, and victim-service providers to treat domestic violence as the serious crime it is and to seek safety and autonomy for victims. The funding will expand and strengthen the investigation and prosecution of domestic violence cases, while providing additional support to victims seeking protection and justice. The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), through the Administration for Children and Families’ Family and Youth Services Bureau, has awarded $358,333 to One Place Metro Alabama Family Justice Center for the first year of a two-year project beginning September 30, 2026, with the same amount anticipated for the second year, for a total of $716,666. Funded through the Family Violence Prevention and Services Act, the award will support counseling and advocacy for survivors and their children, and growth of One Place’s work through Camp HOPE America. Camp HOPE is a national, year-round program for children ages 7 to 17 affected by domestic and family violence. One Place hosts Alabama’s only Camp HOPE America site. “Domestic violence is not an issue of anger management. It is an issue of power and control, and many of its deaths are predictable and preventable when a community responds together,” said Rebecca McWilliams, Executive Director of One Place Metro Alabama Family Justice Center. “Thanks to the Violence Against Women Act and the partnerships we have built with local and federal law enforcement, we have come a long way, and we still have a long way to go. This support from the Department of Health and Human Services will help us walk alongside survivors and make sure children who have witnessed violence have somewhere to belong.” The new resources build on results already visible in Jefferson County. In 2023, the county recorded 25 statutory domestic violence homicides. As of mid-September 2026, it has recorded two, and Birmingham has recorded none. “October is Domestic Violence Awareness Month, and the message from this office is simple: domestic violence is a violent crime, and it will not be tolerated in the Northern District of Alabama,” said U.S. Attorney Phillip W. Williams Jr. “Victims deserve safety, dignity, and justice. These awards put real resources behind the prosecutors who hold abusers accountable and the advocates who walk beside survivors and their children. When we stand together, from the streets to the courtroom, offenders are held accountable and families get the help they need. This is a united front, and my office will keep championing our partners’ work in Washington.” The awards also support Operation Safe Families, the U.S. Attorney’s Office initiative that brings together federal law enforcement, state and local law enforcement, prosecutors, and victim-service providers. Because abusers with access to firearms pose a significant and often deadly risk, the U.S. Attorney’s Office is committed to prosecuting federal cases against abusers who are prohibited from possessing firearms. Operation Safe Families is part of the office’s Project Safe Neighborhoods strategy, because offenders who terrorize their intimate partners often go on to commit other violent crimes and pose extreme risks to law enforcement officers. Nearly one-half of all offenders federally prosecuted by the Northern District of Alabama for violent offenses have a history of domestic violence. Since 2024, the Northern District of Alabama has indicted 62 domestic violence offenders across fourteen counties for various federal offenses. “Domestic violence is one of the clearest warning signs for deadly violence in our community. Roughly 70% of identified homicide offenders in Jefferson County have a history of it, and our office prosecutes more of these cases than homicides, attempted murders, and robberies combined,” said District Attorney Danny Carr. “When police, prosecutors, courts, and advocates work together before a crisis turns fatal, lives are saved. These resources help us sustain that work, and our goal must be zero. I appreciate our federal partners for standing with us.” To learn more about One Place Metro Alabama Family Justice Center or Camp HOPE, please visit One Place Metro Alabama Family Justice Center . title: Meriden Tax Preparer Charged with Tax Fraud Offenses
body: Press Release Meriden Tax Preparer Charged with Tax Fraud Offenses Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Connecticut David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, and Thomas Demeo, Special Agent in Charge of IRS Criminal Investigation in New England, today announced that YURIDIA TRUJILLO, 43, of Meriden, has been charged by indictment with preparing numerous false income tax returns. As alleged in the indictment, Trujillo operated as a tax return preparer under the business name Yuri’s LLC.  For the 2017 through 2024 tax years, Trujillo prepared at least 4,335 tax returns for clients.  On many of her clients’ tax returns, Trujillo made materially false entries, including false deductions for Individual Retirement Account (“IRA”) contributions and child and dependent care expenses; fabricated businesses and business deductions; fictitious losses for the buying and selling of stocks and cryptocurrency that clients never owned; and fabricated rental properties that would report little to no rental income, but significant deductible rental expenses. The indictment further alleges that in association with preparing and filing Forms 1040 for clients, Trujillo also filed Forms 8888, entitled “Allocation of Refund,” which allow taxpayers to elect to have a portion of a direct deposit tax refund deposited into up to three different bank accounts.  Trujillo filed false Forms 8888 in connection with client tax returns that included the bank account and routing numbers of her own bank account and the bank account of an associate, thereby diverting a portion of client refunds to herself. On October 7, 2026, a grand jury in New Haven returned an indictment charging Trujillo with 19 counts of aiding and assisting in the preparation and presentation of a false income tax return, an offense that carries a maximum term of imprisonment of three years on each count. Trujillo was arrested on October 9, 2026, and is released on a $50,000 bond pending trial. U.S. Attorney Sullivan stressed that an indictment is not evidence of guilt.  Charges are only allegations, and a defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. This investigation is being conducted by the Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigation Division.  The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Paul A. Riley. Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Tax Component USAO - Connecticut
