title: THIRD ALABAMA MAN PLEADS GUILTY TO MULTISTATE PHARMACY BURGLARY CONSPIRACY
body: Press Release THIRD ALABAMA MAN PLEADS GUILTY TO MULTISTATE PHARMACY BURGLARY CONSPIRACY Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Mississippi Gulfport, MS – A Northport, Alabama man pleaded guilty today to conspiracy to commit pharmacy burglaries throughout the Southeastern United States. According to documents and information presented to the court, Demirus White, 25, and his coconspirators, Kendrell Cross and Xavier Jennings, conspired to burglarize numerous pharmacies in Mississippi, including pharmacies located in Petal, Florence, Flora, Mathiston, Starkville, Belzoni, and Wiggins.  In addition, they conspired to burglarize pharmacies located in Tennessee, Florida, and Alabama. Law enforcement officers were able to identify White and his coconspirators through phone records that placed them near the locations of the pharmacy burglaries at or near the time of the burglaries, data recovered from the extractions of their phones, plus the recovery of one of Cross’s DNA from a pharmacy that was burglarized. Law enforcement officers also learned that the burglary ring used stolen high-performance vehicles to commit the burglaries and subsequently flee from law enforcement. Cross was ultimately arrested after stealing such a vehicle from a dealership in Laurel, Mississippi and fleeing from police. Cross was previously sentenced to 41 months imprisonment and ordered to pay restitution of $116,008.11.  Xavier Jennings is scheduled to be sentenced on November 5, 2026. Demirus White’s sentencing is scheduled for March 2, 2027.  Both Jennings and White face a statutory maximum sentence of ten years imprisonment. U.S. Attorney Baxter Kruger for the Southern District of Mississippi and Acting Assistant Special Agent in Charge Warner “Brooks” Benson of the Drug Enforcement Administration made the announcement. The Drug Enforcement Administration and the Mississippi Bureau of Narcotics investigated the case with assistance from state and local law enforcement agencies throughout Mississippi, Tennessee, Alabama, and Florida. Assistant U.S. Attorney Jonathan Buckner is prosecuting the case. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. Contact Tara McDaniel Public Affairs Officer Tara.McDaniel@usdoj.gov Updated October 22, 2026 Components Department of Justice USAO - Mississippi, Southern

title: Six Aliens Charged for Falsely Claiming United States’ Citizenship to Vote and/or Illegally Voting in 2022 and 2024 Elections
body: Press Release Six Aliens Charged for Falsely Claiming United States’ Citizenship to Vote and/or Illegally Voting in 2022 and 2024 Elections Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Ocala, Florida – United States Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe announces the filing of federal charges involving six aliens, all lawful permanent residents, for falsely claiming United States’ citizenship to vote and/or illegally voting in 2022 and 2024 elections. Jamie Orlando Sosa Sardina, 60, a Cuban national, Martha Haydee Desantis, 81, an Ecuadorian national, and Lise Marie Johnson, 69, a Canadian national, have each been charged by indictment with making a false statement claiming United States’ citizenship to vote and illegal voting by an alien. If convicted, each faces a maximum penalty of five years in federal prison on the false statement charge and up to one year imprisonment for the illegal voting offense. According to the indictments, Sardina registered to vote in 2022 and voted in the 2022 and 2024 federal general elections; Desantis re-registered to vote in 2024 and voted in the 2022 and 2024 federal general elections; and Johnson registered to vote in 2021 and voted in the 2022 federal general election. All voted despite knowing that they were not citizens of the United States. Luis Manuel Perez, 72, a Cuban national, Diane Wendy Curley, 55, a Canadian national, and Pedro Igor A. Franco, 37, a Brazilian national, all lawful permanent residents, were charged by information with illegal voting by an alien. If convicted, each faces a maximum penalty of up to one year in federal prison. According to the informations, Perez and Curley voted in the 2022 and 2024 federal general elections; Franco voted in the 2024 federal general election. Indictments and informations are merely formal charging documents alleging that a defendant has committed one or more violations of federal criminal law. Every defendant is presumed innocent unless, and until proven guilty. These cases were investigated by Homeland Security Investigations, the Florida Department of State - Office of Election Crimes, and the Hernando County Supervisor of Elections. They are being prosecuted by Special Assistant United States Attorney Jerry M. Harre. Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Component USAO - Florida, Middle

title: U.S. Attorney Moore Capito Joins with Law Enforcement Partners to Promote the DEA’s 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day on Saturday, October 24, 2026
body: Press Release U.S. Attorney Moore Capito Joins with Law Enforcement Partners to Promote the DEA’s 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day on Saturday, October 24, 2026 Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of West Virginia CHARLESTON, W.Va. – United States Attorney Moore Capito is encouraging West Virginians to safely dispose of unwanted medications on Saturday, October 24, 2026, the Drug Enforcement Administration’s 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day. From 10 a.m. to 2 p.m ., DEA and law enforcement partners will collect tablets, capsules, patches, and other solid forms of prescription drugs at more than 65 sites throughout the state, including more than three dozen locations in the Southern District of West Virginia. A collection site locator is available at www.DEATakeBack.com . All sites will accept old, unwanted, and expired prescription medications for free and anonymous disposal. “Drug Take Back Day is a critical opportunity to anonymously remove dangerous, unused prescription drugs from our homes before they end up in the wrong hands,” Capito said. “Law enforcement is sounding the alarm: every pill not turned in is a risk to our community. By acting now, we can stop misuse before it starts and keep these drugs off our streets. Your quick, anonymous action today can help save lives.” Collection sites will not accept syringes, sharps, and illicit drugs. Liquid products, such as cough syrup, should remain sealed in their original container. The cap must be tightly sealed to prevent leakage. In partnership with local law enforcement, Take Back Day has removed more than 20.4 million pounds (10,200 tons) of medication from circulation since its inception. The total includes 149,901 pounds collected in West Virginia, with 4,063 pounds of that disposed of during the previous Take Back Day on April 25, 2026. More information is available at www.DEATakeBack.com . A copy of this press release is located on the website of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of West Virginia. ### Updated October 22, 2026 Topics Community Outreach Prescription Drugs Component USAO - West Virginia, Southern

title: Oklahoma City Man Sentenced to Federal Prison for Possessing Machinegun Conversion Device
body: Press Release Oklahoma City Man Sentenced to Federal Prison for Possessing Machinegun Conversion Device Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Oklahoma OKLAHOMA CITY – XZHAVIER LEE WALTON , 21, of Oklahoma City, has been sentenced to serve 18 months in federal prison for unlawful possession of a machinegun, announced U.S. Attorney Robert J. Troester. According to public records, on February 19, 2026, officers with the Oklahoma City Police Department stopped a vehicle as part of an investigation into a robbery that had occurred earlier that day. During the traffic stop, officers detected the odor of marijuana and detained all occupants, including Walton, who was seated in the rear passenger area behind the driver’s seat. Underneath the driver’s seat, directly in front of Walton, officers recovered a handgun fitted with a machinegun conversion device (MCD), commonly known as a “switch.” When installed, MCDs convert semiautomatic weapons into fully automatic machineguns, and possession of MCDs violates federal law. Through their investigation, law enforcement determined that the handgun belonged to Walton. On March 3, 2026, a federal Grand Jury charged Walton with unlawful possession of a machinegun. Walton pleaded guilty on July 15, 2026, and admitted he knowingly possessed a handgun modified with an MCD. At a sentencing hearing on October 21, 2026, U.S. District Judge Charles Goodwin sentenced Walton to serve 18 months in federal prison, followed by three years of supervised release. This case is the result of an investigation by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and the Oklahoma City Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney David Nichols, Jr., prosecuted the case. This case is part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative to reduce violent crime through coordinated federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement partnerships. PSN is a key component of Operation Take Back America (OTBA), the Department’s nationwide effort to combat violent crime and other threats to public safety. This case is also part of “Project Switch Off,” the Western District of Oklahoma’s implementation of OTBA. “Project Switch Off” targets illegal machinegun conversion devices to address the significant danger these illegal devices present and to remove them from our streets. Reference is made to public filings for additional information. Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Oklahoma, Western

title: Montco Man, 20, Pleads Guilty to 2024 Carjacking in Which He Shot and Seriously Wounded the Victim
body: Press Release Montco Man, 20, Pleads Guilty to 2024 Carjacking in Which He Shot and Seriously Wounded the Victim Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Pennsylvania PHILADELPHIA – United States Attorney David Metcalf announced that Niyaz Burgess, 20, of Elkins Park, Pennsylvania, entered a plea of guilty today before United States District Judge Kai N. Scott to carjacking and using, carrying, and discharging a firearm during and in relation to a crime of violence. The defendant was charged by indictment in August of last year. As detailed in court filings and statements, on July 14, 2024, shortly before three in the morning, Burgess carjacked and shot a man on the 6600 block of Limekiln Pike in Philadelphia, driving away in the victim’s vehicle. The victim suffered two gunshot wounds to the abdomen and one to the arm, resulting in significant internal injuries. On July 15, 2024, around 4:30 a.m., Pennsylvania State Troopers found the victim’s crashed and abandoned car on I-95 South in Tinicum Township. They secured the vehicle and transferred it to the custody of the Philadelphia Police Department. Forensic testing subsequently revealed Burgess’s fingerprints and palm print on the stolen vehicle. The defendant is scheduled to be sentenced on February 15 and faces a maximum possible term of life imprisonment, five years of supervised release, and a fine of $500,000, with a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years in prison. This case was investigated by the FBI Philadelphia Violent Crimes Task Force and the Philadelphia Police Department, with assistance from the Pennsylvania State Police, and is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Sandra Urban. title: Delaware Real-Estate Agent Agrees to Pay $80,000 to Resolve False-Claims-Act Allegations Involving HUD Home Purchase
body: Press Release Delaware Real-Estate Agent Agrees to Pay $80,000 to Resolve False-Claims-Act Allegations Involving HUD Home Purchase Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Delaware Nick.Young@usdoj.gov WILMINGTON, Del. – Lauren Janes, a licensed real-estate agent residing in Delaware, has agreed to pay $80,000 to resolve allegations that she violated the False Claims Act by falsely certifying to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) that she would live in a home she bought from the agency. HUD sells homes it acquires in foreclosure after homeowners default on Federal Housing Administration (FHA) loans. To expand affordable homeownership for low- and moderate-income buyers, HUD first offers these homes exclusively to owner-occupants, who must agree to live in the property as their primary residence for at least one year. Investors may bid only if no owner-occupant buyer comes forward. According to the settlement, Janes bid on a HUD-owned home on Bonwood Road in Wilmington, Delaware, during the owner-occupant period in December 2021. On December 15, 2021, she signed a HUD sales contract to buy the property for $110,000, checking the box identifying herself as an owner-occupant rather than an investor. In a purchase addendum, she certified that she would live in the home as her primary residence for at least 12 months. Janes never lived at the property. After taking ownership on January 14, 2022, she renovated the home and, less than six months later, agreed to sell it for $202,000. The sale closed on July 22, 2022. Under the agreement, Janes will pay $80,000 and has agreed to a 48-month voluntary exclusion from participating in federal procurement and non-procurement transactions, including any other purchases of HUD-owned properties. “Lauren Janes made false statements to HUD to skip the line and purchase a HUD-owned home before other investors could bid on it,” said U.S. Attorney Benjamin L. Wallace.  “My Office and its law-enforcement partners will not allow anyone to cheat federal programs, especially affordable-housing programs meant to protect American families.” “Lauren Janes used her mortgage industry expertise to exploit the FHA program, misrepresenting her home’s occupancy to secure more favorable financing for herself,” said Special Agent in Charge Shawn Rice with the U.S Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), Office of Inspector General (OIG). “As a licensed professional, she understood the program’s requirements yet chose personal gain over professional integrity. HUD OIG remains committed to working with our law-enforcement and prosecutorial partners to hold accountable those who abuse HUD programs and put taxpayer resources at risk.” Janes admitted the facts set out in the statement of facts attached to the settlement agreement at the end of this release. The matter was investigated by HUD Office of Inspector General.  The settlement was handled by Assistant U.S. Attorney Claudia L. Pare. The claims resolved by this settlement are allegations only, and there has been no determination of liability. janes_settlement_agreement.pdf Updated October 22, 2026 Component USAO - Delaware

title: Texas Mexican Mafia Member Sentenced to Over 20 Years in Federal Prison
body: Press Release Texas Mexican Mafia Member Sentenced to Over 20 Years in Federal Prison Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Texas SAN ANTONIO – A member of the Texas Mexican Mafia was sentenced in San Antonio today to 250 months in federal prison for drug trafficking and firearm offenses, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas. According to court documents, David Cortez Jr. aka “Tazmanian” aka “Taz,” 35, of San Antonio, was a sergeant in the Texas Mexican Mafia. Through an investigation led by the Drug Enforcement Administration, Cortez was caught discussing the collection of narcotics proceeds for the Texas Mexican Mafia to make another multi-kilogram purchase of methamphetamine. Due to the investigation, agents were able to seize the narcotics before they could be distributed in the community. Cortez was arrested in October 2020 and was found in possession of heroin and a loaded handgun. He was indicted with 11 co-defendants on Sept. 30, 2020. With the exception of Rudy Arreola, who was indicted separately in 2021, all defendants in this case have been sentenced. Arreola is scheduled to be sentenced on Dec. 10. Donald Trevino, who served as the “free world” General of the Texas Mexican Mafia, was sentenced to 300 months in federal prison in October 2022. “As a ranking officer in one of the most notorious gangs in San Antonio, David Cortez Jr. and his many co-conspirators flooded our community with narcotics,” said U.S. Attorney Simmons. “I extend my gratitude to the DEA along with the FBI and our partners at the San Antonio Police Department for their efforts in safeguarding our community and protecting Americans. This office remains committed to dismantling the violent criminal organizations that interfere with our God-given rights to live our lives, enjoy liberty, and pursue happiness.” “Through aggressive and proactive investigative collaborations, DEA San Antonio Division saved lives by staying one step ahead of David Cortez Jr., dismantling his efforts to profit from the destruction of our communities,” said DEA Special Agent in Charge for the San Antonio Division, Miguel A. Madrigal. “His criminal enterprise has been brought to a halt, and he will now face the consequences of his actions for years to come.” “The FBI is committed to keeping dangerous, illegal drugs out of the communities we serve,” said FBI San Antonio Special Agent in Charge Daniel Faith. “This considerable sentencing puts those who would seek to harm others for their own gain on notice that justice will find you. Cortez will no longer pose a threat to the citizens of San Antonio because of our strong partnerships with DEA, SAPD and the U.S. Attorney's Office.” The DEA, FBI and San Antonio Police Department investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Eric Yuen prosecuted the case. This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. ### Contact USATXW.MediaInquiry@usdoj.gov Updated October 22, 2026 Topics Operation Take Back America Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Components Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Texas, Western

title: Justice Department’s Civil Division and the Department of Health & Human Services Announce Anti-Fraud Healthcare Self-Disclosure Pilot Program
body: Press Release Justice Department’s Civil Division and the Department of Health & Human Services Announce Anti-Fraud Healthcare Self-Disclosure Pilot Program Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs The Six-Month Pilot Program Provides a Pathway for Legitimate Healthcare Companies to Resolve Potential False Claims Act Violations The Department of Justice Civil Division has partnered with the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to launch a Healthcare False Claims Act Self-Disclosure Pilot Program (FCA SDPP), which is designed to give healthcare companies a way to quickly resolve past misconduct by self-disclosing potential violations of the federal False Claims Act (FCA) and to prioritize the government’s resources toward recalcitrant actors. This civil pilot program builds on longstanding Department principles, discussed further here and here , to promote predictable and efficient resolution of corporate misconduct while recovering damages and penalties for taxpayers. [1] “Voluntary self-disclosure is a powerful indicator of a company’s commitment to compliance and accountability,” said Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the Justice Department’s Civil Division. “This pilot program offers a favorable resolution framework to companies that want to take responsibility for past conduct while allowing the Department to concentrate resources on those who deliberately exploit our healthcare system. But for companies unwilling to take accountability, the Civil Division, in partnership with whistleblowers, will root out the fraud.” “By providing predictable and clear incentives for self-disclosure, this pilot program offers responsible companies an opportunity to move forward as stronger partners to federal healthcare programs,” said Deputy Assistant Attorney General Brenna Jenny of the Justice Department’s Civil Division. “When companies identify misconduct and take meaningful steps to fix the problem and repay the government plus penalties, the Department will take those actions into account in determining appropriate resolutions.” Participants must describe all relevant details relating to the disclosing company’s conduct that potentially violates the federal FCA and produce documents sufficient to fully reflect the nature, terms, and operation of the disclosed potential FCA violations. Self-disclosing companies must describe the remedial actions they have taken and make a financial repayment with a 1.25–1.6 multiplier. The multiplier applied will vary based on factors such as the timeliness of the self-disclosure, the duration and scope of the misconduct, the involvement of senior leadership, the financial benefit to the disclosing company, and whether the disclosing company has successor liability for the misconduct but promptly remediated. In exchange, companies will receive a coordinated civil release from liability under the federal False Claims Act and certain HHS administrative authorities. Companies may submit self-disclosures electronically to FCA-SDPP@usdoj.gov. The FCA SDPP will accept submissions through April 22, 2027. Late and incomplete submissions will not be reviewed. Note : A copy of the FCA SDPP protocol is available here . [1] The FCA SDPP is a pilot program available for conduct that potentially violates civil laws. A company seeking to self-disclose potential criminal conduct related to health care must disclose that conduct to the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division pursuant to the National Fraud Enforcement Division and HHS-OIG Policy on Coordination of Voluntary Self-Disclosure in Health Care Fraud Matters. A company that makes a voluntary self-disclosure of criminal matters to the Fraud Division within the meaning of the CEP need not make a duplicative submission to FCA-SDPP@usdoj.gov. Where a company also seeks a civil FCA release through the FCA SDPP, supplementation of its Fraud Division disclosure will be requested only to the extent necessary. Updated October 22, 2026 Topics False Claims Act Fraud Component Civil Division Press Release Number: 26-1218

title: Former Eminem Employee Pleads Guilty to Criminal Infringement of Copyright
body: Press Release Former Eminem Employee Pleads Guilty to Criminal Infringement of Copyright Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Michigan DETROIT — Joseph Strange, 48, of Holly, Michigan, who was formerly employed by the artist and musician Marshall Mathers (also known as Eminem), pleaded guilty in the Eastern District of Michigan to a charge related to his role in the reproduction and sale of unreleased music created by Eminem. “Our republic is built on the right to property,” said U.S. Attorney Jerome F. Gorgon Jr. for the Eastern District of Michigan. “We will protect that right by punishing criminals who steal the physical or intellectual property of Americans.” “Joseph Strange abused a position of trust to unlawfully copy and sell unreleased music belonging to Eminem, profiting from works that were not yet authorized for public distribution,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “His conduct undermined both legal and artistic rights. The Criminal Division remains committed to protecting intellectual property, holding accountable those who seek to profit from theft of creative content, and working with our law enforcement partners to deter and disrupt these crimes.” “Detroit has always been a city where creativity thrives, and no one has the right to steal or profit from another artist’s work without their permission,” said Special Agent in Charge Jennifer Runyan of the FBI Detroit Field Office. “Today’s guilty plea reinforces a simple principle: accountability follows those who compromise the integrity of another person’s creative labor. I want to commend the outstanding work of our FBI Oakland County Resident Agency and the entire investigative team, whose persistence and professionalism drove this case forward. We also appreciate the cooperation of Mathers Music Studio throughout the investigation. Protecting intellectual property means protecting the time, talent, and livelihoods behind it, and we will continue to treat these violations with the seriousness they deserve.” According to court documents, Strange was an employee of Mathers from approximately 2007 until 2021. During Strange’s employment, he worked at a studio in Ferndale, Michigan that Mathers used to create and develop music for future sale and distribution. During his employment, Strange helped set up and operate a computer system that stored music created by Mathers. Strange had access to password-protected hard drives that contained music in the process of being developed by Mathers and that was not yet meant to be released to the public. At some point Strange — without authority — copied 10 or more audio files of music and material in various stages of development from one or more of these drives. Between July and August of 2024, Strange sold and transmitted 10 or more of these music files to purchasers via the internet for a total of approximately $50,000. Strange did so without Mathers’s knowledge or authorization. Audio files sold by Strange were ultimately released online and made available on various public streaming platforms, without the permission or prior knowledge of Mathers. According to facts alleged by the government, while no commercial release of the music or material within these files was imminent or even certain, professional efforts had been made to prepare some of the music for possible commercial release, in some cases including studio mastering. Data provided by several streaming providers evidenced that, as of November 2025, infringing audio files identified by the government had been accessed more than eight million times. The infringement amount of the stolen files is estimated to be at least $750,000. Strange pleaded guilty to criminal infringement of a copyright. He is scheduled to be sentenced on Jan. 27, 2027, and faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. The FBI is investigating the case. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Timothy Wyse and Alyse Wu for the Eastern District of Michigan and Senior Counsel Vasantha Rao of the Criminal Division’s Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section (CCIPS) are prosecuting the case. CCIPS investigates and prosecutes cybercrime and intellectual property (IP) crime in coordination with domestic and international law enforcement agencies, often with assistance from the private sector. Since 2020, CCIPS has secured the conviction of over 180 cyber and IP criminals, and court orders for the return of over $350 million in victim funds. Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Intellectual Property Component USAO - Michigan, Eastern

title: Federal Jury Convicts Monahans Man of Three Counts After He Sexually Abused a Child for Over Five Years
body: Press Release Federal Jury Convicts Monahans Man of Three Counts After He Sexually Abused a Child for Over Five Years Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Texas ALPINE, Texas – A federal jury in Pecos convicted a Monahans man for two counts of aggravated sexual abuse of a child under 12 and one count of committing a sexual offense while being required to register as a sex offender, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas. According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Michael Scott Nichols, 55, groomed and sexually abused a minor female from around the age of six years old until she was 11 years old. On Sept. 23, 2024, the Ward County Sheriff's Department responded to a home in Monahans, where a woman reported that her daughter had been molested by Nichols. Nichols is a registered sex offender due to convictions for sexual assault of a child in 1995 and in 1997. He was sentenced to 15 years in a Texas State Prison for the 1997 offense. During this investigation, it was discovered that Nichols, who owned a trucking company, had abused the minor victim in the Western District of Texas and also transported her across state lines and further abused the victim in other states. Nichols was arrested on April 15, 2025. A third superseding indictment filed in August 2026 charged him with two counts of aggravated sexual abuse of a child and one count of penalties for registered sex offenders. A federal jury found Nichols guilty on all three counts on Wednesday, concluding a three-day trial held before U.S. District Judge David Counts. Immigration and Customs Enforcement Homeland Security Investigations and the Ward County Sheriff's Department investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kevin Cayton and Heather Haywood are prosecuting the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC . ### Contact USATXW.MediaInquiry@usdoj.gov Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Texas, Western

title: Convicted Felon Sentenced to Prison for Leaving a Residential Re-Entry Center
body: Press Release Convicted Felon Sentenced to Prison for Leaving a Residential Re-Entry Center Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts BOSTON – A Boston man was sentenced on Oct. 15, 2026 in federal court in Boston for leaving a residential re-entry center where he was serving the remainder of his federal sentence after being convicted of being a felon in possession of ammunition. Tyreek Hall, 24, was sentenced by U.S. Senior District Court Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV to one year in prison, to be followed by three years of supervised release. In July 2026 , Hall pleaded guilty to escape after being charged in February 2026 . In May 2024 , Hall was sentenced in the District of Massachusetts to 46 months in prison for illegally possessing ammunition while on parole as a convicted felon. In July 2025, Hall was transferred from a correctional institution to a residential re-entry center in Boston to serve the remainder of his confined sentence. As part of the reentry program, Hall was employed as a “part-time vehicle cleaner.” At approximately 11 p.m. on Sept. 7, 2025, when Hall returned to the residential re-entry center from work, staff conducted a breathalyzer test as part of their standard security screening. Hall tested positive, refused a subsequent breathalyzer test and refused to submit to a urinalysis test. After his refusals, Hall was allowed to go to his living quarters. At approximately 11:56 p.m., Hall returned to the front desk and walked out of the front door. Hall did not return to the residential re-entry center and was considered an active escape from federal custody until his apprehension. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Acting U.S. Marshal for the District of Massachusetts Dennis Matulewicz made the announcement. Valuable assistance was provided by the Massachusetts State Police and the Boston Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney John Dawley of the Organized Crime and Gang Unit prosecuted the case. title: New Orleans Couple Indicted for Violations of the Federal Controlled Substances Act and Federal Gun Control Act
body: Press Release New Orleans Couple Indicted for Violations of the Federal Controlled Substances Act and Federal Gun Control Act Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Louisiana shane.jones@usdoj.gov NEW ORLEANS, LA – On October 15, 2026, ALFRED FLANAGIN (“FLANAGIN”), age 42, and ASHA GANPAT (“ GANPAT” ), age 46, of New Orleans, were indicted for conspiracy to distribute, and possess with intent to distribute, controlled substances and use of a communication facility in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime, in violation of Title 21, United States Code, Sections 841(a)(1), 841(b)(1)(B), 841(b)(1)(C), 841(b)(1)(D), 841(b)(1)(E), 843(b), and 846, announced United States Attorney David I. Courcelle. FLANAGIN was also indicted for possession with intent to distribute controlled substances, possession of firearms in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime, and maintaining a drug-involved premises, in violation of Title 21, United States Code Sections 841(a)(1), 841(b)(1)(B), 841(b)(1)(C), 841(b)(1)(D), 841(b)(1)(E), and 856(a)(2), and Title 18, United States Code, Section 924(c)(1)(A). According to court records, on October 2, 2026, FLANAGIN allegedly possessed with intent to distribute fifty grams or more of a mixture and substance containing methamphetamine, a quantity of a mixture and substance containing ketamine, a quantity of a mixture and substance containing ecstasy, and a quantity of marijuana. FLANAGIN is also alleged to have used and maintained a drug-involved premises on Louisiana Avenue Parkway in New Orleans, and possessed four firearms and numerous amounts of ammunition in furtherance of his drug trafficking activities. GANPAT is alleged to have conspired with FLANAGIN to distribute narcotics in the New Orleans area and used a communications device in furtherance of same. If convicted of conspiracy to distribute and possess with intent to distribute controlled substances, FLANAGIN and GANPAT face a minimum of five (5) up to forty (40) years of imprisonment, up to a $5,000,000 fine, and at least four (4) years of supervised release. If convicted of possession with intent to distribute controlled substances, FLANAGIN faces a minimum term of five (5) years up to a maximum term of forty (40) years imprisonment, a fine of up to $5,000,000, and at least four (4) years of supervised release. If convicted of possessing firearms in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime, FLANAGIN faces a minimum consecutive sentence of five (5) years up to life of imprisonment, up to a $250,000 fine, and up to 5 years of supervised release. If convicted of maintaining a drug-involved premises, FLANAGIN faces up to twenty (20) years of imprisonment, up to a $500,000 fine, and at least 3 years of supervised release. FLANAGIN and GANPAT also face payment of a $100 mandatory special assessment fee for each charged offense. U.S. Attorney Courcelle reiterated that the indictment is merely a charge and that the guilt of the defendants must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt. The case was investigated by the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, Homeland Security Investigation, and the New Orleans Police Department. It is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Mary Ellen Buntin of the Narcotics Unit. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. *        *        * Contact Shane M. title: St. Louis County Man Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison for Attempting Sexual Contact with Jefferson County Teen
body: Press Release St. Louis County Man Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison for Attempting Sexual Contact with Jefferson County Teen Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Missouri ST. LOUIS – U.S. District Judge Cristian M. Stevens on Thursday sentenced a St. Louis County man to 10 years in prison for trying to have sexual contact with a Jefferson County 14-year-old. Judge Stevens also placed Tay’vion K. Like, 25, on supervised release for life after his release from prison, saying he was concerned about a prior conviction for indecent exposure and needed to protect children in the community. Judge Stevens also ordered Like to pay restitution to the victim of $1,210. In July of 2025, Like was communicating with the teen via Snapchat. He asked for sexual contact with the victim, even after she told him that she was 14. Like claimed he was 17. Like then told her that he wanted to come to her house to engage in sexual activity. She told him not to come, and that she would call police. When she discovered that he was outside her house on July 15, 2025, she tried to get him to leave and then told her father. Her father called the Jefferson County Sheriff’s Office. Deputies caught Like near the victim’s home. Like also admitted communicating in a sexual manner with other underage girls on Snapchat. Like, of Bellefontaine Neighbors, pleaded guilty in July in U.S. District Court in St. Louis to one count of coercion and enticement of a minor. The Jefferson County Sheriff’s Office and the FBI investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Jillian Anderson prosecuted the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Department of Justice Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc . Contact Robert Patrick, Public Affairs Officer, robert.patrick@usdoj.gov. title: Beaverton Man Sentenced to Two Years and Nine Months in Federal Prison for Possession with Intent to Distribute Fentanyl
body: Press Release Beaverton Man Sentenced to Two Years and Nine Months in Federal Prison for Possession with Intent to Distribute Fentanyl Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Oregon PORTLAND, Ore.— U.S. Attorney for the District of Oregon Scott Bradford announced today that Eder Fletes Calix , 24, of Beaverton, Oregon, was sentenced to two years and nine months in federal prison, to be followed by five years of supervised release, for possessing more than 700 grams of fentanyl with intent to distribute. The sentence follows a multi-agency investigation that began in March 2025, when an Oregon State Trooper conducted a traffic stop on a vehicle driven by Fletes Calix. During the encounter, the trooper observed drug paraphernalia and cash in the vehicle. Both Fletes Calix and a co-defendant fled the scene on foot, prompting the execution of a search warrant that revealed more than 400 grams of compressed fentanyl powder inside the vehicle. Over the following months, the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) continued the investigation and observed multiple drug transactions involving Fletes Calix and his co-defendant. Agents seized additional quantities of fentanyl from buyers during two separate stops in May and June 2025. On July 2, 2025, federal agents arrested Fletes Calix and executed multiple search warrants, including at a Beaverton residence where he had been renting a room. Agents recovered approximately $22,000 in cash, drug packaging materials, digital scales, and additional quantities of fentanyl. In total, investigators seized approximately 767.9 grams of fentanyl powder from the defendants’ vehicle, residence, and related transactions. During a post-arrest interview, Fletes Calix admitted he knew the substance was fentanyl and acknowledged that he and his co-defendant were selling it. Fletes Calix pleaded guilty to one count of possession with intent to distribute 400 grams or more of fentanyl, a Schedule II controlled substance. In determining the sentence, the Court considered the severity of the offense, the volume of fentanyl involved, and Fletes Calix’s lack of criminal history. The case was investigated by the DEA and the Oregon State Police. It was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Jessica Keefer and Kate Rochat. body: Press Release Former Missouri Middle School Principal Indicted on Child Pornography Charge Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Missouri ST. LOUIS – The former assistant principal of a Missouri middle school appeared in court this week to answer a child pornography charge. Daniel Ott, 41, was indicted in U.S. District Court in St. Louis on October 14 with one count of receiving child pornography. Juan C. Valencia, 43, was indicted the same day with one count of distribution of child pornography. Ott appeared in court and pleaded not guilty Monday. Valencia appeared in court and pleaded not guilty Thursday. The indictment accuses Ott of receiving files containing child sexual abuse material (CSAM) between Sept. 1, 2024, and Sept. 3, 2026. Valencia’s indictment accuses him of distributing CSAM, including the same two files, during the same period. A motion seeking to have Ott held in jail until trial says that he engaged in numerous conversations on Telegram during which he spoke about his attraction to minor girls, including some of the female students who attended his school. A motion seeking to hold Valencia in jail says he distributed CSAM to a middle school principal via Telegram. Both charges carry a potential penalty of five to 20 years in prison. Charges set forth in an indictment are merely accusations and do not constitute proof of guilt.  Every defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Homeland Security Investigations and St. Charles County Cyber Crime Task Force investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Sila Karacal is prosecuting the case. title: Lauderdale County Woman Charged with Making Threats Against the President of the United States
body: Press Release Lauderdale County Woman Charged with Making Threats Against the President of the United States Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Alabama HUNTSVILLE, Ala. –  A Lauderdale County woman has been charged with making violent threats against the President of the United States through social media, announced U.S. Attorney Phillip W. Williams Jr. A two-count indictment filed in U.S. District Court charges Megan Lorraine Utz, 36, of Courtland, Alabama, with threats against the President of the United States and interstate transmission of threatening communication. According to the indictment and complaint, it is alleged that on October 5, 2026, Utz made a threatening post on Facebook regarding President Trump’s attendance at the upcoming football game between Alabama and Georgia in Tuscaloosa, Alabama on October 10, 2026.  Utz’s post stated “I’ll put a bullet through him if he dares.” On October 6, 2026, FBI agents, Secret Service agents, and the Florence Police Department located Utz in Florence, Alabama. The Florence Police Department arrested Utz pursuant to an active misdemeanor warrant for Harassing Communications issued by the Guin Police Department. “Threats of violence are taken seriously, and we are committed to protecting the safety of our nation’s leaders,” said U.S. Attorney Williams. “In an era in which our current President has faced multiple attempts on his life we will act swiftly to address threats such as those listed in this complaint. We commend our law enforcement partners for their swift action in identifying and apprehending the defendant.  This case underscores our united front built on strong partnerships and addressing threats of public safety.” “Threats of violence, whether made online or in person, are taken seriously,” said David R. Fitzgibbons, Special Agent in Charge, FBI Birmingham. “People have every right to express their views, but when that expression turns into a threat against another individual, it becomes a federal matter. We appreciate the cooperation of our law enforcement partners in bringing this case forward, and we remain committed to ensuring that threats of this nature are thoroughly investigated.” “The U.S. Secret Service works closely with our law enforcement partners to investigate threats and help ensure the safety of those we protect,” said U.S. Secret Service Special Agent in Charge Patrick Glaze. “We appreciate the collaboration and swift response of our partners in this matter.” FBI and the U.S. Secret Service investigated the case along with the Florence Police Department and the Guin Police Department.  Assistant U.S. Attorneys John M. Hundscheid and Gregory R. Dimler are prosecuting the case. An indictment follows a federal complaint where Utz was arrested for the same conduct. A federal criminal complaint is a sworn, preliminary charge filed by a prosecutor and a law enforcement officer seeking an arrest warrant. After a complaint, the federal grand jury considers the evidence and, if it finds probable cause, indicts on the formal felony charge. A complaint and an indictment are merely allegations. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. title: Illegal Alien Arrested for Identity Theft and Federal Assistance Benefit Fraud
body: Press Release Illegal Alien Arrested for Identity Theft and Federal Assistance Benefit Fraud Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts Defendant allegedly used stolen identity to receive over $11,000 in SNAP benefits BOSTON – A Dominican national unlawfully residing in Dorchester, Mass. has been arrested and charged for allegedly using a stolen identity to fraudulently obtain Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits, previously known as food stamps. Juana Milagros Peña Peña, 37, was charged by criminal complaint with one count each of theft of government money, aggravated identity theft and SNAP fraud. Peña was arrested at her home on Oct. 19, 2026 and released on conditions following an initial appearance in federal court in Boston. According to the criminal complaint, Peña – a citizen of the Dominican Republic, who has been unlawfully residing in the United States since at least 2016 – fraudulently used the identity of a U.S. citizen to apply for and receive over $11,000 in SNAP benefits dating back to 2021. The victim, whose birth certificate and Social Security number Peña has fraudulently passed off as her own, reported to authorities that the theft of her identity has negatively affected her credit and has required her to utilize a special PIN when filing her taxes. The charge of SNAP fraud provides for a sentence of up to 20 years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. The charge of theft of government money provides for a sentence of up to 10 years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. The charge of aggravated identity theft provides for a mandatory two-year prison sentence to run consecutively to any other sentence imposed, one year of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. The defendant is subject to deportation upon completion of any sentence imposed.  Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes that govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Jeff Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England made the announcement. Valuable assistance was provided by the U.S. Department of Agriculture, Office of Inspector General; the Social Security Administration, Office of the Inspector General; and the Massachusetts State Police. Assistant U.S. Attorney John Potapchuk of the Major Crimes Unit is prosecuting the case. On March 26, 2026 , United States Attorney Leah B. Foley announced the creation of the Benefit & Voter Fraud Team, a district-wide initiative established in response to the rampant fraud being uncovered across Massachusetts. Members of the public are encouraged to report suspected benefit fraud in Massachusetts by calling 1-855-SCAM-MA-1 (855-722-6621). On April 7, 2026, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division . The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The details contained in the charging document are allegations. The defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in the court of law. title: Two Felons Sentenced for Illegal Possession of Firearms Following Investigation Prompted by YouTube and Instagram Videos
body: Press Release Two Felons Sentenced for Illegal Possession of Firearms Following Investigation Prompted by YouTube and Instagram Videos Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia WASHINGTON – Travis Foster, 25, and Reginald Monroe, 23, both previously convicted felons residing in the District of Columbia, were sentenced today in U.S. District Court for unlawfully possessing firearms that authorities recovered following an investigation prompted by videos and livestreams posted to YouTube and Instagram, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. “They flaunted guns for the cameras, brandished weapons in music videos, and carried an arsenal of deadly firepower into our community,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Now they’re going to prison. Let this be a warning: if you are a convicted felon who continues to arm yourself and put the public at risk, you will face prison time.” Foster pleaded guilty on July 24 before U.S. District Judge Loren L. AliKhan to unlawful possession of a firearm by a felon and unlawful possession with intent to distribute marijuana. In addition to the 57‑month prison term, Judge AliKhan ordered Foster to serve three years of supervised release. Monroe pleaded guilty on July 23 before Judge AliKhan to unlawful possession of a firearm by a felon and unlawful possession of a machine gun. In addition to the 46‑month prison term, Judge AliKhan ordered Monroe to serve three years of supervised release. A frame grab from a video posted by a co-defendant to social media. YouTube videos and Instagram live streams prompted the investigation. Investigators recognized the displayed weapons as real firearms. According to court documents, law enforcement began monitoring social media in 2023 after observing Foster and associates appearing in high‑resolution music videos and online posts with firearms equipped with extended magazines. Investigators recognized the displayed weapons as real firearms and noted the presence of micro draco pistols capable of firing rifle rounds, dramatically increasing the risk posed to the public by the firearms. According to court documents, on Oct. 19, 2023, officers tracked Foster, Monroe and others from a dinner gathering to a nightclub in NW Washington. Surveillance ultimately led law enforcement to a nearby parking garage, where officers recovered 842 suspected fentanyl pills and multiple firearms from a stolen Audi Q7, along with six more firearms from a Chrysler 300. Prescription paperwork inside a backpack found in the Chrysler 300 tied Foster to some of the recovered guns. Monroe was captured on surveillance footage exiting the Chrysler, and DNA evidence later linked him to a Glock 23 .40 caliber pistol recovered from the Audi and a Glock 32 .357 caliber pistol recovered from the Chrysler 300. Investigators later recovered Instagram voice messages in which Foster referred to the recovered firearms as his and discussed replacing them after the seizure. Additional posts showed Foster marketing marijuana for sale and possessing distribution level quantities. Law enforcement later executed a search warrant at Foster’s residence where they recovered a loaded pistol with an extended magazine, more than one pound of marijuana, and a money counter. According to court documents, Monroe’s possession of firearms was part of a longer pattern of armed criminal conduct, including prior convictions for armed robbery and unlawful firearm possession. He possessed two pistols modified to function as machine guns, each equipped with a 22‑round magazine. These weapons were carried while Monroe traveled with associates who had an arsenal of additional firearms, including micro draco pistols capable of firing rifle rounds. This case marks Foster’s second conviction involving the illegal possession of a firearm. Foster previously pleaded guilty to an October 2019 armed robbery of a car was sentenced to 96 months imprisonment. Three months after he was released on July 14, 2023, he committed the instant offense. Monroe’s conviction in this case marks his fourth for illegally possessing a firearm in just six years. Monroe also is awaiting sentencing in a Superior Court case in connection with an armed robbery. The investigation was conducted by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, Washington Field Office; the FBI Washington Field Office; and the Metropolitan Police Department. The matter was prosecuted under the Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful initiative by Assistant U.S. Attorney Benjamin Helfand. Make D.C. The bag of rifle bullets officers recovered from the backpack also including Foster’s prescription. Inside the Audi Q7, officers recovered 842 suspected fentanyl pills and three firearms in the glove box. Monroe’s DNA linked him to the Glock 23 .40 caliber pistol equipped with a machine gun conversion device that investigators recovered from the stolen Audi. In an image posted to social media, Foster is photographed with a Glock-style extended magazine protruding from his waistband. title: New Orleans Man Indicted for Violating the Federal Controlled Substances Act
body: Press Release New Orleans Man Indicted for Violating the Federal Controlled Substances Act Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Louisiana shane.jones@usdoj.gov NEW ORLEANS, LA – On October 16, 2026, HAROLD BANKS ("BANKS"), age 48, of New Orleans, was indicted on two counts of distribution of controlled substances, in violation of Title 21, United States Code, Sections 841(a)(1), 841(b)(1)(B), and 841(b)(1)(C), announced United States Attorney David I. Courcelle. Count Two alleges that on September 21, 2026, BANKS did knowingly and intentionally distribute twenty-eight grams or more of a mixture and substance containing a detectable amount of cocaine base, in violation of Title 21, United States Code, Sections 841(a)(1) and (b)(1)(B). If convicted of Count One, BANKS faces up to twenty (20) years of imprisonment, up to a $1,000,000 fine, at least three (3) years of supervised release, and a $100 mandatory special assessment fee. If convicted of Count Two, BANKS faces a mandatory minimum of five (5) years up to forty (40) years of imprisonment, up to a $5,000,000 fine, at least four (4) years of supervised release, and a $100 mandatory special assessment fee. U.S. Attorney Courcelle reiterated that the indictment is merely a charge and that the guilt of the defendant must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt. The case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives.  It is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Troy L. Bell of the Violent Crime Unit. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. *        *        * Contact Shane M. title: Oklahoma Man Guilty of Conspiracy, False Distress Signals, and False Statements
body: Press Release Oklahoma Man Guilty of Conspiracy, False Distress Signals, and False Statements Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Louisiana shane.jones@usdoj.gov NEW ORLEANS , LOUISIANA – MELVIN EMDE ("EMDE") , age 44, resident of LeFlore County, Oklahoma, pled guilty on October 14, 2026, to conspiracy to commit a federal offense against or defraud the United States or an agency thereof, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Section 371, and communication of a false distress message to the United States Coast Guard, in violation of Title 14, United States Code, Section 521(c), announced United States Attorney David I. Courcelle. According to court documents, on or about August 7, 2023, MELVIN , and others, planned to fake MELVIN’s death to avoid prosecution in North Carolina for a pending sex crime involving a minor. They purchased fishing gear and brought kayaks to the banks of the Mississippi River in St. Charles Parish. MELVIN removed his ankle monitor from his pending case in North Carolina. A co-conspirator then made a false distress call to the U.S. Coast Guard, causing a search and rescue operation. MELVIN was later apprehended in Georgia using an alias. At sentencing, MELVIN faces maximum penalties of up to 5 years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000, up to 3 years of supervised release, and a mandatory special assessment fee of $100 for the conspiracy charge. For the charge of communicating a false distress message to the Coast Guard, MELVIN faces between 5 and 10 years in prison, up to 3 years of supervised release, a fine of up to $250,000, and a $100 mandatory special assessment fee. Sentencing has been scheduled for January 20, 2027. U.S. Attorney Courcelle praised the work of the United States Coast Guard – Coast Guard Investigative Service and the St. Charles Parish Sheriff’s Office in investigating this matter.  Assistant United States Attorney Spiro G. Latsis of the General Crimes Unit oversees the prosecution. *   *   * Contact Shane M. body: Press Release Uvalde Man Sentenced to 2 Years in Federal Prison for Assaulting Border Patrol Agent at Checkpoint Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Texas DEL RIO, Texas – A Uvalde man was sentenced to 24 months in prison for assaulting a United States Border Patrol agent, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas. According to court documents, on Jan. 6, Maximiliano Arellano, 25, underwent a routine immigration checkpoint inspection at the Uvalde Border Patrol Immigration Checkpoint. Arellano was referred to a secondary inspection due to positive detection by the service canine. At secondary inspection, Arellano became agitated, repeatedly called Border Patrol agents racial slurs, and refused to comply with the agents’ commands. Arellano eventually approached an agent in an aggressive manner at which time U.S. Border Patrol agents placed Arellano against his vehicle to de-escalate the situation. Arellano resisted, pushed off of the vehicle, and threw his body into another agent. Arellano struck the agent’s chest and knocked him off balance. Arellano was ultimately restrained with the use of a taser. Arellano pleaded guilty to one count of assaulting, resisting or impeding certain officers or employees on June 30. The U.S. Border Patrol investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Carli Tuttle prosecuted the case. ### Contact USATXW.MediaInquiry@usdoj.gov Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Violent Crime Component USAO - Texas, Western

title: Rapid City Woman Sentenced to 10 Years in Federal Prison  for Her Participation in a Drug Distribution Conspiracy
body: Press Release Rapid City Woman Sentenced to 10 Years in Federal Prison  for Her Participation in a Drug Distribution Conspiracy Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of South Dakota RAPID CITY - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that U.S. District Court Judge Camela C. Theeler has sentenced a Rapid City, South Dakota, woman convicted of Conspiracy to Distribute a Controlled Substance.  The sentencing took place on October 20, 2026. Jaimie High Horse, 36, was sentenced to 10 years in federal prison, followed by five years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund. High Horse was indicted for Conspiracy to Distribute a Controlled Substance by a federal grand jury in April 2026.  She pleaded guilty on July 21, 2026. High Horse, along with 12 co-defendants, was involved in a conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine throughout South Dakota, including Rapid City.  High Horse was personally involved in the distribution of 500 grams or more of methamphetamine.  She was arrested in April 2026 after a high-speed pursuit involving an officer with the Oglala Sioux Tribe Department of Public Safety. This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.  Operation Take Back America streamlines efforts and resources from the Department’s Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Forces (OCDETFs) and Project Safe Neighborhood (PSN).  Through PSN, the District of South Dakota seeks to bring together all levels of law enforcement and the communities they serve to reduce gun violence and make our neighborhoods safer for everyone. This case was investigated by the South Dakota and Colorado Drug Enforcement Administration offices, the Bureau of Indian Affairs Division of Drug Enforcement, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Department of Homeland Security, the South Dakota Division of Criminal Investigation, the South Dakota Highway Patrol, the Pennington County Sheriff’s Office, the Rapid City Police Department, the Oglala Sioux Tribe Department of Public Safety, the Western Colorado Drug Task Force, the Arvada, Colorado Police Department, and the Wyoming Division of Criminal Investigation.  Assistant U.S. Attorney Benjamin Patterson prosecuted the case. High Horse was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service. Contact usasd.press@usdoj.gov Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Operation Take Back America Component USAO - South Dakota

title: Fort Bend County tax assessor-collector charged in wire fraud scheme
body: Press Release Fort Bend County tax assessor-collector charged in wire fraud scheme Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Texas HOUSTON – A federal grand jury has returned an indictment against three individuals for their alleged roles in a scheme to defraud Fort Bend County through fraudulent payroll practices. The elected tax assessor-collector of Fort Bend County—Carmen Patrice Turner, 65, Richmond—faces charges involving conspiracy, theft concerning federal program funds, and wire fraud. Also indicted are Shemerrylyn Regina Fields, 47, of Rosharon, and Victor Calvin Ewing, 69, of Houston, whom Turner allegedly hired as part of the scheme. Turner and Fields are expected to make their initial appearances before U.S. Magistrate Judge Peter Bray today in Houston. Law enforcement arrested Ewing in Chicago, Illinois, where he is expected to make his initial appearance. According to the indictment, Turner orchestrated a scheme from approximately September 2023 through September 2025 to use county payroll funds to pay individuals for work they did not perform. Turner allegedly hired Fields and another individual as deputy tax clerks but directed them to provide care for her elderly mother during regular county work hours. According to the charges, Turner instructed them to clock in and out remotely through the county’s telephone timekeeping system while falsely reporting they were performing their official duties. The indictment further alleges Turner hired Ewing as a full-time department coordinator despite knowing he already worked full-time for a company in Chicago, Illinois, and would not perform the duties of the county position. Ewing allegedly received a county salary while continuing his employment in Chicago. According to the indictment, he also agreed to transfer a portion of his county payroll deposits to Turner. In one instance, Ewing allegedly transferred money to Turner through Cash App after receiving a county payroll payment. Turner, Fields, and Ewing allegedly used false timesheets, concealed their actual work activities, and maintained access to county computer systems to create the appearance of legitimate employment. According to the indictment, Turner also used Ewing’s credentials to access WebDealer, a system county tax offices and Texas Department of Motor Vehicles use to process vehicle registrations, while Ewing was working in Chicago. The charges allege that in one of those “transactions,” Turner erroneously approved a vehicle cost of $295,836.92, instead of $29,583.92, causing the dealership a significant error in the assessed sales tax, which is automatically withdrawn from the dealership’s bank account. “Carmen Turner has been strutting around Fort Bend County with the title The Honorable for years. Nothing could be more dis- honorable—or illegal—than her and her conspirators’ public corruption,” said U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz. “The people of the Southern District of Texas have my commitment to do everything we can to do justice and make it right. Taxpayers deserve so much better.” “Public service is a privilege, not a right to break the law,” said Special Agent in Charge Jason Hudson of FBI – Houston Field Office. “When a public official violates the law, they violate the trust of the citizens they swore to serve and protect. As a public servant myself, my hope is that today’s federal indictments and arrests are a step towards restoring that trust. If you have information about public corruption, no matter the official, the office they hold, or the loss amount, please report it.” “Through collaborative effort, justice prevails,” said Lieutenant Erik Burse of Texas Department of Public Safety. If convicted, all three face up to 20 years for each of wire fraud count. They could also receive a maximum of 10 years for theft concerning federal program funds and another five years for conspiracy. Each of the charges also carries a potential fine of up to $250,000. FBI and Texas Rangers conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Carolyn Ferko and Rodolfo Ramirez are prosecuting the case. An indictment is a formal accusation of criminal conduct, not evidence. A defendant is presumed innocent unless convicted through due process of law. Updated October 22, 2026 Component USAO - Texas, Southern

title: Previously Convicted Felon Pleads Guilty to Illegal Possession of a Loaded Glock 27
body: Press Release Previously Convicted Felon Pleads Guilty to Illegal Possession of a Loaded Glock 27 Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia Last Month, Defendant Was Found Guilty by a Jury in a Similar Case WASHINGTON – Pres Braddy, 34, a previously convicted felon residing in the District, pleaded guilty today in U.S. District Court in connection with his illegal possession of a loaded Glock 27 .40 caliber pistol, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. Braddy pleaded guilty before Judge Christopher R. Cooper to one count of unlawful possession of a firearm by a felon. Judge Cooper scheduled sentencing for Jan. 5, 2027. According to court document, on Aug. 30, 2025, at about 11:42 p.m., members of the Metropolitan Police Department, along with other law enforcement partners, were patrolling a parking lot on the 2300 block of 11th Street NW, at the Garfield Terrace apartments. Braddy was seen on surveillance video wearing a black crossbody satchel on his person while in a group of about a dozen people. As the officers arrived, Braddy separated himself from the group, removed the satchel, and walked back toward the group. An officer approached the satchel, touched it, and felt an object consistent with a firearm. When police opened the satchel, officers recovered a Glock 27 .40 caliber pistol, loaded with one round of .40 caliber ammunition in the chamber and 15 additional rounds in the 15-round magazine. The satchel also contained 17 rounds of .40 caliber ammunition. Braddy is prohibited from having any gun because he previously had been convicted of unlawful possession of a firearm and sentenced in September 2017 to 18 months in prison. On Sept. 10, 2026, Braddy was convicted at trial for unlawful possession of a firearm by a prohibited person in connection with having a Glock 23 Gen 5 pistol. Police recovered the Glock 23 following a pursuit of a stolen Jeep in which Braddy had been a passenger. Sentencing for that offense also is scheduled for January 5. Both cases were prosecuted under the Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful Again Initiative by Assistant U.S. Attorneys David Liss, Travis Wolf, and Alexander Cook of the Federal Major Crimes Unit. The initiative targets violent crime by prioritizing federal prosecution of armed repeat offenders and removing illegal firearms from District neighborhoods. 25cr301 25cr218 Follow us on X , Instagram , and YouTube Or at https://www.justice.gov/usao-dc Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - District of Columbia

title: Cartel Commander Charged with International Cocaine and Methamphetamine Trafficking Conspiracy and Firearm Offenses
body: Press Release Cartel Commander Charged with International Cocaine and Methamphetamine Trafficking Conspiracy and Firearm Offenses Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs A federal grand jury in the District of Columbia returned an indictment today charging Ivan Cazarin Molina, 42, a Mexican national, with conspiracy to distribute cocaine and methamphetamine for importation into the United States and possessing a firearm in furtherance of the drug trafficking offense. According to court documents, Cazarin Molina, also known as “Tanque,” was a regional commander for the Cartel de Jalisco Nueva Generacion (CJNG) in Veracruz, Mexico. On Feb. 20, 2025, the U.S. Secretary of State designated the CJNG as a foreign terrorist organization. “Today’s indictment of Ivan Cazarin Molina, a regional leader of the CJNG, sends a clear message that the Department of Justice will find all leaders and commanders of drug cartels and transnational criminal organizations and prosecute them for their destruction of our communities through drug trafficking and violence,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Today’s charges demonstrate the Justice Department’s commitment toward the total elimination of drug cartels and transnational criminal organizations. Thanks to the hard work of our DEA partners and the Criminal Division prosecutors, these cartel leaders will be exposed and their organizations dismantled.” “For two decades, Ivan Cazarin Molina allegedly helped fuel CJNG’s trafficking operations using intimidation and violence to protect its criminal enterprise,” said Administrator Terrance Cole of the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). “The era of impunity for cartel leaders is over. DEA, working though the homeland security task force and alongside our international partners, will fight narco-terrorists wherever they operate – following every lead, severing every supply line, dismantling every organization, and bringing those responsible to justice.” Cazarin Molina is charged with conspiracy to manufacture and distribute five kilograms or more of cocaine and 500 grams or more of methamphetamine for importation into the United States from 2005 through 2025, and using, carrying, brandishing, and discharging a firearm, in relation to the drug trafficking conspiracy. If convicted, Cazarin Molina faces a minimum penalty of 40 years in prison and a maximum penalty of two consecutive life prison terms. Cazarin Molina was arrested on Oct. 5 by Mexican law enforcement authorities in Jalisco, Mexico. The DEA’s Special Operations Division Bilateral Investigations Unit Los Angeles is investigating the case. Chief Kaitlin Sahni of the Narcotic and Dangerous Drug Unit (NDDU) and Trial Attorneys Maryann McGuire, Lernik Begian, and Douglas Meisel of the Criminal Division’s Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section (MNF) are prosecuting the case. MNF’s mission is to take the profit out of crime, eliminate drug cartels, and protect the U.S. financial system. MNF pursues criminal prosecutions and criminal and civil asset recovery actions involving: financial facilitators who launder profits for criminals; financial institutions and their officers and employees whose actions threaten the U.S. financial system and financial institutions; international money launderers who support transnational organized crime; and the top command and control of international drug trafficking organizations. MNF’s Narcotic and Dangerous Drug Unit investigates and prosecutes the top command and control elements of international drug cartels, drug trafficking organizations and related transnational criminal organizations. This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of U.S. law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
