title: Massachusetts Man Convicted of Abusive Sexual Contact of a Minor Aboard Flight to Boston
body: Press Release Massachusetts Man Convicted of Abusive Sexual Contact of a Minor Aboard Flight to Boston Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts Defendant worked his hand in between the seat directly in front of him, where a minor victim was seated and touched the minor victim’s buttocks BOSTON – A Newton, Mass. man was convicted on Oct. 16, 2026 following a three-day jury trial, of making repeated sexual contact with a 17-year-old female passenger (minor victim) seated directly in front of him onboard a flight from Puerto Rico to Boston in August 2024. Jonathan Alan Lefman, 48, was convicted of one count of abusive sexual contact while in the special aircraft jurisdiction of the United States. U.S. District Court Judge Julia E. Kobick scheduled sentencing for Jan. 12, 2027. Lefman was arrested and charged by criminal complaint in February 2025 and later indicted by a federal grand jury in March 2025 . “The defendant repeatedly sexually abused a minor who was simply trying to travel safely aboard a commercial flight,” said United States Attorney Leah B. Foley. “No one should have to fear being sexually assaulted, whether in the air or on the ground. Today’s verdict holds the defendant accountable for his disturbing conduct and sends a clear message that those who prey on vulnerable passengers will face justice.” “This verdict delivers justice for a young teen who showed remarkable courage following an appalling act. No one should ever be subjected to such harmful and predatory conduct—least of all in a confined, public space where she was entitled to feel safe,” said Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Boston Division. “The FBI is fully committed to protecting children and ensuring those who exploit or abuse them, like Mr. Lefman, are brought to justice.” On Aug. 30, 2024, Lefman was a passenger onboard a JetBlue flight flying from San Juan, Puerto Rico to Boston with his wife and four children. On multiple occasions during the flight and while on the ground waiting to deplane in Boston, Lefman engaged in abusive sexual contact with the minor victim. Specifically, Lefman worked his hand in between the area between the back and bottom of the seat directly in front of him, where the minor victim was seated, and touched the minor victim’s buttocks without her permission. On at least one occasion when he did so, the minor victim saw Lefman’s reflection leaning between the seats in the seatback monitor in front of her. On the last occasion when he touched or attempted to touch her buttocks, the minor victim was able to use her cell phone camera to take a video of Lefman’s fingers protruding between the back and bottom of the minor victim’s seat. Upon exiting the aircraft, while still on the jet bridge, the minor victim took a video of Lefman as he got off the aircraft. After deplaning, the minor victim’s adult female family member who had been traveling in a different row reported Lefman’s conduct to a JetBlue supervisor and confronted Lefman, showing the video of his fingers to support her statement. The charge of abusive sexual contact while in the special aircraft jurisdiction of the United States provides for a sentence of up to two years in prison, five years to a lifetime of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. U.S. Attorney Foley, FBI SAC Docks and Colonel Geoffrey D. Noble, Superintendent of the Massachusetts State Police made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by Boston Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Elianna J. Nuzum and Julissa Walsh of the Criminal Division are prosecuting the case. Updated October 22, 2026 Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: Foreign-Owned Industrial Manufacturing Company to Pay $1.5 Million to Settle False Claims Act Allegations Related to Paycheck Protection Program Loan
body: Press Release Foreign-Owned Industrial Manufacturing Company to Pay $1.5 Million to Settle False Claims Act Allegations Related to Paycheck Protection Program Loan Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Michigan DETROIT – United States Attorney Jerome F. Gorgon Jr. announced today that 3CON Corporation, a company located in Wixom, Michigan that designs and manufactures automated production systems for the automotive and life sciences industries, has agreed to pay $1,500,439.50 to settle allegations that it violated the False Claims Act by making false statements to the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) to obtain a Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loan for which 3CON was ineligible. Congress created the PPP in March 2020 to provide emergency financial assistance to American businesses suffering from the economic effects of the COVID-19 pandemic. Under the PPP, eligible small businesses could receive forgivable loans guaranteed by the SBA. Regulations provided various eligibility requirements for the PPP, including limitations on the number of employees and restrictions for foreign-owned companies.When applying for PPP loans, borrowers were required to certify the truthfulness and accuracy of all information provided in their loan applications. In January 2021, 3CON obtained a second draw PPP loan for $828,498. At the time of its loan application, 3CON shared common ownership with 3CON Anlagenbau GmbH, an Austrian Company. The United States alleged that 3CON falsely certified that it was eligible for the second draw loan and loan forgiveness, even though, together with its foreign affiliates, it had more than 300 employees, in violation of the PPP rules in effect at the time 3CON obtained the funds. This civil settlement resolved a sealed lawsuit originally filed under the qui tam or whistleblower provisions of the False Claims Act, which permit private parties to file suit on behalf of the United States for false claims and share in a portion of the government’s recovery. The qui tam lawsuit has been unsealed and is captioned U.S. ex rel. Verity Investigations, LLC v. 3CON Corporation , Case No. 2:25-cv-13896. The whistleblower will receive 10% of the settlement amount. This matter was handled by Assistant U.S. Attorney Bradley H. Darling from the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Michigan, with assistance from the SBA’s Office of General Counsel. Individuals with information about allegations of fraud involving COVID-19 are encouraged to report it by calling the Department of Justice’s National Center for Disaster Fraud (NCDF) Hotline at 866-720-5721 or via the NCDF Web Complaint Form at: https://www.justice.gov/disaster-fraud/ncdf-disaster-complaint-form The claims resolved by the settlement are allegations only; there has been no determination of liability. title: White Earth Man Sentenced to 10 Years’ Imprisonment for Possession and Intent to Distribute 900 Grams of Methamphetamine
body: Press Release White Earth Man Sentenced to 10 Years’ Imprisonment for Possession and Intent to Distribute 900 Grams of Methamphetamine Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Minnesota ST. PAUL – United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen announced that Dominic Ray LaFriniere, 51, of White Earth, was sentenced to 120 months in prison for conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine and cocaine. He was sentenced before U.S. District Judge Jeffrey M. Bryan on October 22, 2026. According to court documents, White Earth Tribal Police Department and other law enforcement agencies began investigating LaFriniere’s controlled substance distribution activities in 2022. The investigation included a controlled purchase of methamphetamine from LaFriniere and a search of his home. The investigation became dormant due to the defendant’s incarceration with the Minnesota Department of Corrections. The investigation resumed in January 2024 when law enforcement arrested LaFriniere for possessing 13 grams of methamphetamine. Law enforcement tracked the defendant and observed him traveling to Minneapolis in April 2024. White Earth Tribal Police Department officers stopped LaFriniere as he returned to the White Earth Indian Reservation from Minneapolis and seized his truck. Investigators searched the truck and found 900 grams of methamphetamine hidden inside a hollowed-out log and 60 grams of cocaine hidden inside of a rolled-up carpet. “The defendant chose to traffic methamphetamine and profit off addiction. My office is committed to stopping the flow of drugs into our communities,” said United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen. This case was the result of an investigation by the White Earth Tribal Police Department, Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension, with assistance from other law enforcement partners. Assistant United States Attorney Syngen Kanassatega prosecuted the case. Contact usamn.pressoffice@usdoj.gov Updated October 22, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Indian Country Law and Justice Component USAO - Minnesota

title: Federal Crackdown: 11 charged in North Texas for firearms trafficking, meth distribution and machine gun offenses
body: Press Release Federal Crackdown: 11 charged in North Texas for firearms trafficking, meth distribution and machine gun offenses Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas ABILENE, Texas – United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced today that federal charges have been filed against eleven individuals for various firearms and drug trafficking offenses following a Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives-led investigation and violent crimes reduction initiative in Abilene. All defendants are in federal custody and made their initial appearances today before U.S. Magistrate Judge John R. Parker. “Today, we delivered a decisive blow against the criminal networks that threaten Abilene and the broader Taylor County community through the trafficking of illegal firearms and the distribution of dangerous narcotics,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “As Abilene continues to grow, protecting the safety and stability of this city remains one of my highest priorities. Let this serve as a clear warning: In unwavering partnership with our federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies, my office will relentlessly pursue and dismantle these organizations. We will not allow our streets to be undermined by gangs, firearm traffickers, and drug dealers, particularly when these crimes fuel the brutal operations of cartel driven crime.” “Those who traffic firearms to criminals, arm cartel-connected networks, and push meth into our communities are fueling violent crime,” ATF Dallas Special Agent in Charge Brian Garner. “ATF and our partners are disrupting these operations, targeting the people behind them, and holding them accountable. We will not stop pursuing those who threaten public safety.” Firearms Trafficking and Related Offenses Seven individuals face charges related to firearms trafficking, including sales to prohibited persons and conspiracy to transfer firearms for use in felony and drug trafficking crimes, some with alleged ties to Mexican cartels: Larry Don Knight, Kenneth Dwayne Tittle and Dylan Tyler Todd are charged in a criminal complaint with conspiracy and attempt to transfer firearms for use in felony and drug trafficking crimes, possession of firearms by convicted felons, attempted sale of firearms to prohibited persons, and distribution and possession with intent to distribute a controlled substance (methamphetamine). According to court documents, these individuals allegedly trafficked firearms and methamphetamine in the Abilene area, with some firearms intended for Mexican cartels. Defendants Tittle and Todd, both convicted felons, are also charged with selling firearms to a known prohibited person. Knight is additionally charged with methamphetamine distribution. Randall Kent Whitaker and Brandi Michelle Whitaker are charged with conspiracy to transfer a firearm for use in a felony and drug trafficking crimes, and attempted sale or transfer of a firearm to a prohibited person. The complaint alleges that the duo trafficked firearms in Abilene, including sales to a known felon, with the understanding that the firearms were bound for Mexican cartels. Whitaker is a convicted felon. Josiah Haynesworth is charged with sale or transfer of a firearm to a prohibited person and trafficking in firearms. Court documents allege Haynesworth knowingly sold a firearm to a convicted felon in Abilene. Justine Aten Harris is charged with possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. According to court documents, Harris allegedly sold multiple firearms, including a Springfield Armory .45 pistol and a 12-gauge shotgun, to a confidential informant in September 2026. Methamphetamine Trafficking Three individuals are facing federal charges for their alleged roles in a methamphetamine trafficking conspiracy: Coby Dale Foust, Jesseca Denah Foust and Christal Louise Rule are charged with conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine and possession with intent to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine. According to the complaint, these defendants allegedly trafficked significant quantities of methamphetamine in the greater Abilene, Anson, and Albany areas of Texas. Illegal Machine Gun Possession One individual is charged with illegal possession of a machine gun: Aiden Ochoa is charged with illegal possession of a machine gun. The complaint alleges that Mr. Ochoa possessed a handgun equipped with an illegal machine gun conversion device, commonly known as a "Glock switch," in Abilene. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives Dallas Division and the Abilene Police Department conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Matthew L. Tusing and Jordan Magee from the Abilene Division are prosecuting the cases. A criminal complaint is merely an allegation, and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law. Contact Public Affairs Division U.S. Attorney’s Office Northern District of Texas USATXN.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 22, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Texas, Northern

title: Montco Man, 20, Pleads Guilty to 2024 Carjacking in Which He Shot and Seriously Wounded the Victim
body: Press Release Montco Man, 20, Pleads Guilty to 2024 Carjacking in Which He Shot and Seriously Wounded the Victim Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Pennsylvania PHILADELPHIA – United States Attorney David Metcalf announced that Niyaz Burgess, 20, of Elkins Park, Pennsylvania, entered a plea of guilty today before United States District Judge Kai N. Scott to carjacking and using, carrying, and discharging a firearm during and in relation to a crime of violence. The defendant was charged by indictment in August of last year. As detailed in court filings and statements, on July 14, 2024, shortly before three in the morning, Burgess carjacked and shot a man on the 6600 block of Limekiln Pike in Philadelphia, driving away in the victim’s vehicle. The victim suffered two gunshot wounds to the abdomen and one to the arm, resulting in significant internal injuries. On July 15, 2024, around 4:30 a.m., Pennsylvania State Troopers found the victim’s crashed and abandoned car on I-95 South in Tinicum Township. They secured the vehicle and transferred it to the custody of the Philadelphia Police Department. Forensic testing subsequently revealed Burgess’s fingerprints and palm print on the stolen vehicle. The defendant is scheduled to be sentenced on February 15 and faces a maximum possible term of life imprisonment, five years of supervised release, and a fine of $500,000, with a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years in prison. This case was investigated by the FBI Philadelphia Violent Crimes Task Force and the Philadelphia Police Department, with assistance from the Pennsylvania State Police, and is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Sandra Urban. title: Chicago Man Sentenced to 31 Years in Prison for Sexually Exploiting a Minor
body: Press Release Chicago Man Sentenced to 31 Years in Prison for Sexually Exploiting a Minor Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts Defendant coerced minor to engage in sexually explicit acts which he demanded be photographed or videotaped BOSTON – A Chicago man was sentenced yesterday in federal court in Boston for sexually exploiting a 14-year-old minor victim from Massachusetts. Joshua Rogers, 31, was sentenced by U.S. District Court Judge Richard G. Stearns to 21 years in prison, to be followed by five years of supervised release. In June 2026 , Rogers pleaded guilty to one count of sexual exploitation of children. Roger was arrested in December 2025 in Chicago. In July 2025, law enforcement was notified of an individual purporting to be a 17-year-old boy named ‘John’ –later identified as Rogers – engaging in sexually explicit communications with a 14-year-old female minor victim on Snapchat. A review of cell phone data revealed numerous communications from Rogers in which he coerced the minor to engage in sexually explicit acts, many of which he demanded be documented by photo or video. In his communications, Rogers also discussed kidnapping the minor or the minor running away. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Boston Division; and Chief Jennifer Paster of the Brookline Police Department made the announcement. Valuable assistance was provided by the FBI’s Chicago Field Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Luke A. Goldworm, Project Safe Childhood Coordinator and a member of the Major Crimes Unit prosecuted the case. The case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood. In 2006, the Department of Justice created Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative designed to protect children from exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the DOJ’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children, as well as identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.projectsafechildhood.gov . Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: Four Men Charged with Pandemic Relief Fraud
body: Press Release Four Men Charged with Pandemic Relief Fraud Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts One defendant allegedly spent pandemic relief funds at casino BOSTON – Four individuals have been charged for allegedly defrauding the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) and Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) program by submitting fraudulent applications. The following individuals have been indicted on one count each of wire fraud: Jonathan Arroyo, 43, of Boston; Daquan Dooley, 37, of Attleboro; Demetrous Thomas, 36, of Acushnet; and Gianni Williams Johnson, 28, of Boston. Arroyo, Dooley and Thomas were arrested and appeared in federal court in Boston. Williams Johnson is currently detained on an unrelated matter in Suffolk Superior Court and will appear in federal court in Boston on a later date. According to the charging documents, Arroyo, Thomas and Williams Johnson allegedly submitted fraudulent PPP applications on behalf of themselves, claiming that they owned businesses that suffered economic harm because of the COVID-19 pandemic. They each submitted fraudulent tax return information to justify their applications. They were each awarded forgivable PPP loans in the amount of over $20,000. In fact, it is alleged that none of these individuals owned businesses and their fraudulent tax return information was never filed with the IRS. It is alleged that bank records show that none of these individuals used the loans for payroll expenses. According to the charging documents, Dooley also allegedly submitted a fraudulent EIDL application on behalf of himself, claiming that he owned a business that suffered economic harm because of the COVID-19 pandemic. Dooley claimed that he would use the loan for business expenses, such as payroll and rent. After Dooley’s application, he was given a $10,000 EIDL advance, which was a grant provided under the EIDL program that did not have to be repaid. Bank records show that Dooley allegedly spent thousands of dollars of the pandemic relief funds at a casino and none of it on business expenses. The charge of wire fraud provides for a sentence of up to 20 years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of $250,000, or twice the gross gain or loss from the scheme, whichever is greater. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Jeffrey Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England; Justin Page, Acting Inspector in Charge of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Boston Division; and Anthony P. D’Esposito, Inspector General, Department of Labor, Office of Inspector General made the announcement. Assistant U.S. Attorney Philip C. Cheng of the Criminal Division is prosecuting the case. On March 26, 2026 , United States Attorney Leah B. Foley announced the creation of the Benefit & Voter Fraud Team, a district-wide initiative established in response to the rampant fraud being uncovered across Massachusetts. Members of the public are encouraged to report suspected benefit fraud in Massachusetts by calling 1-855-SCAM-MA-1 (855-722-6621). On April 7, 2026, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division . The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The details contained in the charging document are allegations. The defendants are presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in the court of law. Updated October 22, 2026 Topics Fraud COVID-Related Fraud Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: Justice Department Opens Investigation into Alleged Firearm Permitting Abuses in Two Connecticut Municipalities
body: Press Release Justice Department Opens Investigation into Alleged Firearm Permitting Abuses in Two Connecticut Municipalities Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Today, the Justice Department opened an investigation into Middletown and Waterbury , Connecticut, to determine whether they unnecessarily delay the issuance of firearm permits to their residents. The Second Amendment protects the right of law-abiding citizens to keep and bear firearms — including the right to carry firearms. The investigation will focus on the Middletown and Waterbury police departments’ permitting systems. “All law-abiding Americans have a constitutional right to bear arms for self‑defense,” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “This right is not a luxury reserved for a privileged few, but a fundamental liberty for all, including the residents of Middletown and Waterbury, Connecticut.” The Supreme Court’s 2022 seminal ruling in New York State Rifle and Pistol Association v. Bruen , recognized that the right to keep and bear arms applies with equal force inside and outside the home. In Bruen , the Supreme Court warned against “lengthy wait times in processing license applications” that effectively “deny ordinary citizens their right to public carry.” The Middletown and Waterbury police departments may be unreasonably denying otherwise qualified applicants a CCW permit and forcing them to undergo a potentially years-long appeal process to exercise this fundamental right. The Civil Rights Division’s Second Amendment Section enforces the Second Amendment. If you believe your right to keep and bear arms is being infringed, please submit an online complaint through www.justice.gov/crt/second-amendment-section . Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Civil Rights Component Civil Rights Division Press Release Number: 26-1252

title: Arizona Man Sentenced to 38 Months in Prison for Threatening to Kill President Trump and Former Vice President Harris
body: Press Release Arizona Man Sentenced to 38 Months in Prison for Threatening to Kill President Trump and Former Vice President Harris Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Arizona PHOENIX, Ariz. – Rene Ortiz, 56, of Casa Grande, Arizona, was sentenced on Oct. 20, 2026, by Senior U.S. District Judge Stephen M. McNamee to 38 months in prison. Ortiz was convicted by a federal jury on June 8, 2026, of two felony violations of Making Threats Against Successors to the Presidency and one felony violation of Making Threats Against Former Presidents. On Nov. 5, 2024—Election Day—Ortiz delivered to the federal courthouse in Phoenix a written threat to “execute the newly elected [President of the United States] by firing an M-16A2 service rifle with a magazine of 6 rounds,” directed at both candidates, former Vice President Kamala Harris and President Donald Trump. After the election, on Nov. 25, 2024, Ortiz delivered a second threat to shoot “the incoming fraudulent elected [President of the United States] … at the inauguration on January 20th, 2025,” to the federal courthouse in Tucson. When interviewed by the U.S. Secret Service about the threats, Ortiz repeated his intent to make the threats; he was subsequently arrested on Jan. 17, 2025, ahead of the Presidential Inauguration. The United States Secret Service conducted the investigation with assistance from the United States Marshals Service. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Amy Chang and Abbie Broughton, District of Arizona, Phoenix, handled the prosecution. title: New Jersey Real Estate Investor and Online Influencer Admits to Committing Multi-Million Dollar Investment Fraud Scheme, Laundering Drug Proceeds, and Bribing a New Jersey Politician
body: Press Release New Jersey Real Estate Investor and Online Influencer Admits to Committing Multi-Million Dollar Investment Fraud Scheme, Laundering Drug Proceeds, and Bribing a New Jersey Politician Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Jersey NEWARK, N.J. – Cesar Humberto Pina, a/k/a “Flipping NJ,” of Franklin Lakes, New Jersey, pleaded guilty to committing a multi-million dollar real estate investment fraud scheme, laundering money for drug traffickers, and bribing a New Jersey politician, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced. Pina, 48, pleaded guilty today before the Honorable Madeline Cox Arleo in Newark to a four-count Superseding Information charging him with one count of wire fraud, one count of money laundering conspiracy, one count of bribery of an agent of a program receiving federal funds, and one count of travel act bribery. He is scheduled to be sentenced on March 10, 2027. “Cesar Pina admitted to misappropriating millions of dollars meant for real estate investments, laundering cash for narcotics traffickers, and bribing a politician in furtherance of real estate projects. It is hard to imagine a more varied spate of criminal activity, which robbed investors of their life savings, helped facilitate drug trafficking, and undermined confidence in our elected officials.  As this prosecution demonstrates, this Office will continue to work with our law enforcement partners to root out and prosecute complex schemes of all types.” - U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer “This case demonstrates how drug trafficking can intersect with financial crime and corruption, allowing criminals to exploit legitimate businesses and undermine public trust for personal gain,” said DEA New Jersey Field Division Special Agent in Charge Towanda R. Thorne-James. “We will follow the money, dismantle the financial networks that fuel drug trafficking, and hold accountable everyone who helps these criminals profit from their illegal activities. Through strong enforcement and close coordination with our law enforcement partners, we will ensure those who facilitate the drug trade are brought to justice.” “Postal Inspectors, working alongside our law enforcement partners, remain committed to investigating complex financial fraud schemes that victimize innocent investors and result in devasting financial losses,” said Inspector in Charge Christopher Nielsen of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service. “Financial fraud schemes such as these can devastate victims and their hard-earned savings. Those who use the U.S. Mail to facilitate fraudulent schemes to exploit the public for personal financial gain will be held accountable for their actions.” “Pina lured in victims and exploited their trust by using his online influencer persona. Not only did he steal millions of dollars from investors, but he also laundered money for drug traffickers and bribed a politician along the way,” said FBI Newark Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy. “Complex schemes like this demand strong, coordinated partnerships, and FBI Newark will tirelessly work alongside our federal, state, and local counterparts to protect investors and hold accountable those who abuse the public trust.” “Pina turned promises of real estate profits into a vehicle for fraud, while laundering drug proceeds and paying bribes to advance his own interests,” said Jenifer L. Piovesan, Special Agent in Charge of IRS Criminal Investigation’s Newark Field Office. “Behind these financial transactions are real victims—investors whose trust was betrayed and communities harmed by drug trafficking and corruption. IRS Criminal Investigation and our law enforcement partners will continue to follow the money, unravel complex financial schemes, and hold accountable those who profit at the public’s expense.” According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court: Pina partnered with a celebrity disc jockey and radio personality to conduct real estate seminars around the country. Through these seminars, self-promotional efforts, and other marketing strategies, Pina developed a significant social media following. Starting in at least 2017, Pina began accepting investments from individual investors for the alleged purchase, remodel, and sale of specific real estate properties in New Jersey and other states. To induce investors, Pina often promised 30% or higher returns on investments within 4 to 5 months. But instead of using investors’ funds as promised, Pina commingled and misappropriated investors’ money, including by using new investor funds to pay off prior investors in a Ponzi-like scheme and spending investor funds on unauthorized business and personal expenditures. Pina fraudulently obtained and misappropriated millions of dollars through this scheme. Pina also conspired to launder illicit funds, including from the sale of controlled substances, for various individuals he knew were engaged in narcotics trafficking and other criminal activities. In addition, Pina bribed a local official of Paterson, New Jersey in connection with real estate-related projects in Paterson. For example, Pina provided cash and other bribes to the official in exchange for official action, assistance, and influence in connection with Pina’s “Old School 5” development project, which had pending applications before the Paterson Zoning Board of Adjustment. The charge of wire fraud carries a maximum penalty of twenty years in prison and a fine of $250,000, or twice the gross amount of any pecuniary gain that any persons derived from the offense or of any pecuniary loss sustained by any victims of the offense, whichever is greatest. The charge of money laundering conspiracy carries a maximum penalty of twenty years in prison and a fine of $500,000 or twice the value of the property involved in the transaction, whichever is greater. The charge of bribery concerning programs receiving federal funds carries a maximum penalty of ten years in prison and a fine of $250,000, or twice the gross amount of any pecuniary gain that any persons derived from the offense or of any pecuniary loss sustained by any victims of the offense, whichever is greatest. The charge of the use of facilities in interstate commerce to facilitate unlawful activity under state law, namely bribery, carries a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a fine of $250,000, or twice the gross amount of any pecuniary gain that any persons derived from the offense or of any pecuniary loss sustained by any victims of the offense, whichever is greatest. U.S. Attorney Frazer credited special agents of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Jersey, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Matthew Maltese; special agents and task force officers of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Towanda R. Thorne-James in Newark; postal inspectors of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service in Newark, under the direction of Christopher A. Nielsen, Philadelphia Division; special agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy in Newark; and special agents and task force officers of the Internal Revenue Service – Criminal Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Jenifer L. Piovesan in Newark with the investigation leading to the charges. He also thanked the Franklin Lakes Police Department for its assistance in the investigation. The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Carolyn Silane, Chief of the Economic Crimes Unit; Edeli Rivera, Co-Chief of the General Crimes Unit; Aaron Webman, Chief of the Cybercrimes Unit; and Marko Pesce, Deputy Chief of the Criminal Division in Newark. ### Defense counsel: Gerald Krovatin, Esq., Newark, NJ pina.supersedinginformation.pdf Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Financial Fraud Component USAO - New Jersey Press Release Number: 26-231

title: Missouri Governor and U.S. Attorneys Announce Operation Show-Me the Money to Combat Benefits Fraud
body: Press Release Missouri Governor and U.S. Attorneys Announce Operation Show-Me the Money to Combat Benefits Fraud Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Missouri JEFFERSON CITY, Mo. – R. Matthew Price, U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Missouri, joined Missouri Governor Mike Kehoe, Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway, and Tom Albus, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Missouri, to announce Operation Show-Me the Money , an unprecedented partnership between the State of Missouri and the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) to aggressively identify, investigate, and prosecute fraud involving taxpayer-funded benefit programs. Operation Show-Me the Money will focus on state programs that distribute federal funds to entities and individuals, bringing together state and federal resources to better identify potential fraud, strengthen oversight, and ensure taxpayer dollars are being used for their intended purpose. "Missouri is no place for fraud, and those who think they can cheat the system and steal from hardworking taxpayers are going to be held accountable," said Governor Kehoe. "From day one, my administration has made it a priority to crack down on criminals and protect taxpayer dollars. Through Operation Show-Me the Money, we're bringing the full force of state and federal law enforcement together to send a clear message: If you're stealing from Missouri taxpayers, we're coming after you." “By combining federal investigative and prosecutorial resources with the state’s knowledge and oversight of its benefit programs, we can detect fraud sooner, build stronger cases, and hold offenders accountable,” said U.S. Attorney Price. “Hardworking Missouri taxpayers deserve better, and we are committed to protecting the integrity of these programs, following the money, and using every available federal law enforcement tool to bring those who commit fraud to justice.” Operation Show-Me the Money is a collaborative effort between the Kehoe Administration, the Missouri Attorney General's Office, and the DOJ, expanding existing partnerships for cross-departmental data sharing to help identify suspicious activity and pursue prosecution. The initiative will bring together dedicated staff from the Missouri Attorney General's Medicaid Fraud Control Unit and the DOJ to strengthen coordination and investigative efforts. “Missouri will not be a safe haven for anyone who steals from taxpayers or exploits public programs," said Attorney General Hanaway. "We have won many major victories against consumer, contractor, and Medicaid fraud, but our work is not finished. We thank Governor Mike Kehoe and U.S. Attorneys, Tom and Matt, for their leadership as we work together to root out fraud and protect taxpayer dollars across our state.” “This operation will provide better access to data and information on these benefit programs and better communication between our agencies, helping us ensure that tax dollars won’t be siphoned away from these valuable programs by fraudsters,” said U.S. Attorney Albus. “I look forward to working with our state and federal partners on this valuable new initiative.” The operation will utilize a three-pronged approach, first drawing on referrals from existing state agency investigations and tips from frontline program staff. Second, investigators will conduct targeted reviews of individual benefit programs, beginning with the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), to identify suspicious activity and vulnerabilities. The third component will use data across multiple state agencies and programs to detect patterns of potential fraud that might otherwise go unnoticed. By examining information across systems, investigators can identify emerging trends and determine where further inquiry is warranted. In addition to pursuing fraud, the operation will help identify weaknesses in existing programs and opportunities to strengthen oversight. Findings may inform future administrative changes, program improvements, or legislative solutions to better safeguard taxpayer dollars and prevent fraud before it occurs. Operation Show-Me the Money builds on ongoing state and federal efforts to crack down on fraud and protect taxpayer dollars. U.S. Attorney Price recently joined Vice President JD Vance in signing the Pledge to Protect Americans from Fraud , reinforcing Missouri's commitment to holding fraudsters accountable. For more information on federal efforts to combat fraud, visit justice.gov/fraud . Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Benefit Fraud Component USAO - Missouri, Western

title: Former High School Teacher Sentenced to Federal Prison for Possession of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Former High School Teacher Sentenced to Federal Prison for Possession of Child Pornography Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Texas WACO, Texas – A former Belton High School teacher was sentenced to 78 months in prison for possession of child pornography, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas. According to court documents, on Sept. 22, 2024, Pietro Victor Giustino, 40, sent Bitcoin to a vendor in exchange for child sexual abuse material. On June 4, 2025, the FBI executed a federal search warrant at Giustino’s residence in Belton and discovered devices and media containing thousands of images of child pornography, including prepubescent minors. Giustino was arrested in July 2025. He pleaded guilty in March to one count of possession of visual depictions of sexual activities by minors. On Wednesday, U.S. District Judge Christopher Wolfe sentenced Giustino to 78 months in federal prison followed by five years of supervised release. Judge Wolfe also ordered a $5,000 Victims of Trafficking Act assessment along with an Amy, Vicky, and Andy Child Pornography Assessment Act assessment of $10,000. The FBI investigated the case with assistance from the Belton Police Department and with cooperation from the Belton Independent School District. Assistant U.S. Attorney Greg Gloff prosecuted the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC . ### Contact USATXW.MediaInquiry@usdoj.gov Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Texas, Western

title: Monroe Man Sentenced to 30 Years in Federal Prison for Drug Trafficking and Firearms Offenses
body: Press Release Monroe Man Sentenced to 30 Years in Federal Prison for Drug Trafficking and Firearms Offenses Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Louisiana Defendant was also ordered to forfeit to the United States a Texas Shooter Supply AR, a Diamondback Arms rifle, a Romarm pistol, a D Technik pistol, a Glock pistol, and ammunition MONROE – On October 21, 2026, United States Chief District Judge Terry A. Doughty sentenced Demorion “Duck” Baker 30, of Monroe, to 30 years in federal prison for multiple counts of Possession with Intent to Distribute Controlled Substances including Cocaine, Alprazolam, Marijuana, and Methamphetamine, and for Possession of Firearms in Furtherance of Drug Trafficking.  His sentence will be followed by five years of supervised release. Baker was also ordered to forfeit to the United States a Texas Shooter Supply AR, a Diamondback Arms rifle, a Romarm pistol, a D‑Technik pistol, a Glock pistol, and ammunition. (Two of the weapons depicted below.) ATF Baker was previously convicted on May 27, 2026, after a two-day trial before Judge Doughty. The jury deliberated for only an hour before rendering the guilty verdicts. According to evidence presented at trial, this case began when a separate Monroe‑area individual was found in possession of more than five pounds of methamphetamine and identified Baker as the supplier. Acting on this information, law enforcement executed a search warrant at a vacant residence identified as Baker’s stash house. Inside, agents discovered approximately one kilogram of cocaine, one kilogram of methamphetamine, more than one thousand counterfeit ecstasy tablets, eighty‑five pounds of marijuana, four assault‑style firearms, and 860 rounds of ammunition. Investigators linked Baker to this residence through mail addressed to him, a laptop with a specific username, and an iPhone containing communications between Baker and his brother.  Further, Baker’s DNA was found on three of the four firearms. Agents later obtained an arrest warrant for Baker and searched another residence he frequented. Baker was arrested there in possession of approximately 500 grams of cocaine and a handgun. DEA U.S. Attorney Zachary A. Keller for the Western District of Louisiana made the announcement. The Drug Enforcement Administration, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, the Monroe Police Department, Ouachita Parish Sheriff’s Office, West Monroe Police Department, Metro Narcotics Unit, and the Louisiana State Police investigated this case. It was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Samuel S. Crichton and Cheyenne Y. Wilson, with assistance from Paralegal Specialist Emily Favrot. Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Western District of Louisiana at www.lawd.uscourts.gov or at https://www.lawd.uscourts.gov/cmecf-pacer, under Case Number 24‑cr‑00269. ### CONTACT: Public Affairs (337) 262-6704 Cara.Alexander@usdoj.gov www.justice.gov/usao-wdla Updated October 22, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) USAO - Louisiana, Western

title: Little Rock Man Sentenced to 15 Years in Federal Prison for Being a Felon in Possession of a Firearm
body: Press Release Little Rock Man Sentenced to 15 Years in Federal Prison for Being a Felon in Possession of a Firearm Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Arkansas Ms. Paulette Chappelle, Public Affairs Officer Paulette.Chappelle@usdoj.gov LITTLE ROCK—Andre Lavon Harris, who previously received a 30-year state sentence for first-degree murder, will spend the next 180 months in federal prison for being a felon in possession of a firearm. Jonathan D. Ross, United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Arkansas, which was handed down on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, by United States District Judge Lee P. Rudofsky. A federal grand jury indicted Harris, 47, of Little Rock, in a three-count Indictment for being a felon in possession of a firearm, possession with intent to distribute fentanyl, and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. On July 6, 2026, Harris pleaded guilty to being a felon in possession of a firearm. Judge Rudofsky also sentenced Harris to three years’ supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system. On September 5, 2023, an agent with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), working with a confidential source (CS), learned that Harris was a multi-ounce distributor of methamphetamine and fentanyl pills in Saline and Pulaski Counties. The CS advised agents that Harris wore an ankle monitor, drove a black Chevrolet Tahoe, and carried a firearm. Through their investigation, agents confirmed Harris was a convicted felon who was on parole and had a search waiver on file. On November 15, 2023, agents conducted a traffic stop on Harris to execute a parole search. During the search of Harris’ vehicle, agents located a loaded Taurus, model G3C, 9mm semi-automatic firearm on the floorboard of the driver’s side that Harris stated he got off “the street.” Agents also located in the center console’s cupholder a pill bottle containing 2.2 grams of crack cocaine, eight pills containing fentanyl, and another nine pills containing methamphetamine. Harris’ criminal history includes felony convictions for first-degree murder on July 23, 1999, possession of firearms by certain persons, and battery, second degree. This case was investigated by the DEA with assistance from the Little Rock Police Department. This case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Edward Walker of the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Arkansas. # # # Additional information about the office of the United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Arkansas, is available online at https://www.justice.gov/edar X (formerly known as Twitter): @USAO_EDAR Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Arkansas, Eastern

title: Ammunition Thefts from Sporting Goods Stores Land Oklahoma City Felon in Federal Prison for More Than Three Years
body: Press Release Ammunition Thefts from Sporting Goods Stores Land Oklahoma City Felon in Federal Prison for More Than Three Years Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Oklahoma OKLAHOMA CITY – ROBERT ALEXANDER PITTS , 39, of Oklahoma City, has been sentenced to serve 37 months in federal prison for possession of ammunition after a previous felony conviction and possession of stolen ammunition, announced U.S. Attorney Robert J. Troester. According to public records, in the fall of 2025, Pitts stole ammunition on multiple occasions from Bass Pro and Cabela’s stores in Oklahoma City. Pitts concealed boxes of ammunition in his pants pockets, hoodie pockets, waistbands, and elsewhere. In all, Pitts stole 2000 rounds of ammunition. Public records further reflect that Pitts has previous felony convictions in Oklahoma County District Court that include: attempted larceny of merchandise in case number CF-2013-2650; larceny of merchandise from a retailer and false declaration of ownership to a pawnbroker in case number CF-2015-5544; possession of cocaine and marijuana in case number CF-2015-6365; and felon in possession of a firearm in case number CF-2020-426. Federal law prohibits the possession of ammunition by convicted felons. On December 16, 2025, a federal grand jury charged Pitts with being a felon in possession of ammunition and possession of stolen ammunition. Pitts pleaded guilty on April 13, 2026, and admitted that he knowingly possessed ammunition he had stolen and that he possessed the ammunition despite his previous felony convictions. At a sentencing hearing on October 22, 2026, U.S. District Judge Bernard M. Jones II sentenced Pitts to serve 37 months in federal prison, followed by three years of supervised release. In announcing his sentence, Judge Jones noted Pitts’ criminal history and the need to promote respect for the law. This case is the result of an investigation by the Oklahoma City Police Department and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives. Assistant U.S. Attorney David Nichols, Jr., prosecuted the case. Reference is made to public filings for additional information. Updated October 22, 2026 Component USAO - Oklahoma, Western

title: Worcester Man Charged with Possession with Intent to Distribute Fentanyl
body: Press Release Worcester Man Charged with Possession with Intent to Distribute Fentanyl Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts BOSTON – A Worcester man has been arrested and charged with possessing multiple kilograms of fentanyl intended for distribution. Junior Tejada Hernandez, 28, whose immigration status is unknown at this time, was charged with one count of possession with intent to distribute controlled substances. Hernandez was arrested yesterday and will appear in federal court in Worcester later today. According to the charging documents, during a search of Hernandez’s one-bedroom apartment yesterday, more than three kilograms of fentanyl was recovered in the bedroom. Drug paraphernalia was also located inside of a suitcase in the bedroom closet which contained cutting agents, baggies, a sifting device, a blender used to mix controlled substances and other dilutants, scissors and other materials. The charge of possession with intent to distribute fentanyl provides for a sentence of up to 20 years in prison, at least three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $1 million. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Jarod A. Forget, Special Agent in Charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration, New England Field Division; Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Boston Division; Thomas Demeo, Special Agent in Charge of the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation, Boston Field Office; and Colonel Geoffrey D. Noble, Superintendent of the Massachusetts State Police made the announcement. Valuable assistance was provided by the Leominster, Fitchburg, Clinton, Worcester, Gardner, Lunenberg and Webster Police Departments and the Worcester County Sheriff’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Zachary Stendig of the Worcester Branch Office is prosecuting the case. This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Boston is comprised of agents and officers from HSI, FBI, DEA, ATF, USMS, IRS-CI, USPIS, DOL-OIG, DSS and CBP as well as several state and local law enforcement agencies, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Massachusetts. The details contained in the charging document are allegations. The defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in the court of law. title: Maryland Sex Offender Indicted on Failure to Register Charges
body: Press Release Maryland Sex Offender Indicted on Failure to Register Charges Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Maryland Baltimore, Maryland – The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Maryland announced, today, that a Maryland man is facing indictment for a sex-offender registration crime. Paul Revell, 42, of Pikesville, is charged with failure to register as a sex offender. Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the indictment with Clinton J. Fuchs, U.S. Marshal for the District of Maryland (USMS), and Chief Robert McCullough, Baltimore County Police Department (BCPD). According to the indictment, from July 16, 2026, through August 14, 2026, Revell, who is a convicted sex offender, knowingly failed to update a registration as is required by the Sex Offender Registration Notification Act under Federal law. If convicted, Revell faces a maximum of 10 years in federal prison for failure to register as a sex offender. Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. A federal district court judge determines sentencing after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. This case is part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse.  Led by the United States Attorney’s Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims.  For more information about Project Safe Childhood, visit justice.gov/psc .  For more information about Internet safety education, visit justice.gov/psc and click on the “Resources” tab on the left of the page. U.S. Attorney Hayes commended USMS and BCPD for their work in the investigation. Ms. Hayes also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorney Maryam Zhuravitsky who is prosecuting the federal case. For more information about the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office, its priorities, and resources available to help the community, visit justice.gov/usao-md . # # # Contact Kevin Nash USAMD.Press@usdoj.gov 410-209-4946 Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Components USAO - Maryland U.S. Marshals Service

title: Child predator sentenced to more than 27 years in federal prison for sexual exploitation of a minor
body: Press Release Child predator sentenced to more than 27 years in federal prison for sexual exploitation of a minor Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas FORT WORTH, Texas — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced a Fort Worth man, who has a previous conviction for sexual offenses against a child, was sentenced to 327 months in federal prison for sexually exploiting a minor on Sept. 29. Travis Jerrad McQuiston Reed, 34, pleaded guilty in April to one count of sexual exploitation of a child. “The federal government has no tolerance for anyone who preys on children, and today’s sentence reflects that reality,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “Anyone who believes they can exploit a child in North Texas and escape accountability is gravely mistaken. In this District, federal law enforcement will find you, we will prosecute you and you will face a sentence measured in decades as the defendant is in this case. I am grateful to our partners at CBP and HSI for their swift work that stopped Reed from continuing to harm children.” “The steadfast vigilance of our CBP officers at the Port of Galveston directly interrupted a dangerous threat and set a comprehensive federal investigation into motion,” said Acting Director of Field Operations Leslie Fleming-Luczkowski. “Thanks to the seamless collaboration between our frontline personnel, Homeland Security Investigations, and the U.S. Attorney’s Office, a predator has been brought to justice with a significant federal sentence. We remain unwavering in our commitment to protecting the most vulnerable and dismantling child exploitation networks” According to court documents, on or about Sept. 7, 2025, Reed enticed a minor victim to engage in sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing visual depictions. U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers encountered Reed as he re-entered the United States at the Port of Galveston, Texas, on Nov. 2, 2025. During a lawful inspection of his iPhone, officers discovered nude images of children and referred the device for forensic analysis. The subsequent review confirmed that Reed produced the child sexual abuse material in Fort Worth using the same device. Court documents also show that Reed had a prior felony conviction for indecency with a child in Tarrant County, which subjected him to enhanced penalties. Reed has also agreed to pay restitution, mandatory assessments and will be required to register as a sex offender upon release. U.S. Customs and Border Protection and Homeland Security Investigations Dallas conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Aisha Saleem from the Fort Worth Division prosecuted the case. Contact Public Affairs Division U.S. Attorney’s Office Northern District of Texas USATXN.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Texas, Northern

title: U.S. Attorney’s Office for Northern Ohio Joins DOJ Fraud Division and USDA in Uncovering Nearly $42M in SNAP Benefit Fraud
body: Press Release U.S. Attorney’s Office for Northern Ohio Joins DOJ Fraud Division and USDA in Uncovering Nearly $42M in SNAP Benefit Fraud Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Ohio 13 U.S. Attorney’s Offices joined the Fraud Division in bringing enforcement actions against alleged fraudsters CLEVELAND – The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Ohio announced several enforcement actions as part of a nationwide effort led by the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) targeting suspected fraudulent activity in the Supplemental Nutritional Assistance Program (SNAP). SNAP is a federal benefits program funded by the USDA and administered by the State of Ohio. The Northern District of Ohio (NDOH) was a key participant in this surge effort. Between Sept. 1 and Oct. 21, 2026, the Fraud Division and 13 U.S. Attorney’s Offices across the country participated in the Department’s first National USDA Benefits and Program Fraud Enforcement Surge. This coordinated effort resulted in actions against more than 40 defendants whose alleged or proven schemes caused nearly $45 million in intended losses to the federal government. Nearly $42 million of that amount involved fraud against SNAP benefits, which provide monthly food assistance to low-income individuals and families. “You cannot exchange food program benefits for cash, illegal drugs, or anything else - it is a violation of federal law,” said U.S. Attorney David M. Toepfer for the Northern District of Ohio. “My office will aggressively protect the integrity of taxpayer-funded programs to assist those truly in need. During some of these investigations, we also found evidence of federal housing or drug trafficking violations. Together with our investigative partners, we will find and prosecute those who attempt to manipulate federal programs for their own benefit.” “These benefits are a critical lifeline for eligible families, not a source of profit for those willing to exploit the program,” said Lewis Porcella, Special Agent in Charge of the U.S. Secret Service Cleveland Field Office. “Secret Service investigators will work relentlessly with our law enforcement partners to uncover fraud and hold accountable anyone who steals resources intended to help vulnerable Americans put food on the table.” NDOH Notable Cases • United States v. Sqar Qahtan, Mohsin Mohsin, Baligh Naji, Mariah Hatcher, Ahmed Al Hamami, and Almotawakil Nassr (Complaints) – approximately $1,000,000 in intended loss On Oct. 6, 2026, Sqar Qahtan, 31, Baligh Naji, 34, Ahmed Al Hamami, 36, all citizens of Yemen residing in Euclid, Ohio, along with Mohsin Mohsin, 28, of Syracuse, New York; Mariah Hatcher, 30, of Euclid, Ohio, and Almotawakil Nassr, 29, of Detroit, Michigan, were charged in criminal complaints with SNAP Benefits Fraud, Wire Fraud, and Conspiracy to Commit Wire Fraud. SNAP benefits are more commonly known as “food stamps.” For approximately two years, the defendants allegedly operated a conspiracy to exchange Ohio SNAP benefit cards for cash, marijuana, and other non-SNAP items while employed at a gas station convenience store in Euclid, Ohio. Identified members of the conspiracy obtained at least $64,000 in SNAP benefits, with the members of the conspiracy likely to have engaged in at least approximately $1 million in fraud. If convicted, each defendant faces per count: SNAP Benefits Fraud – five years in prison; Wire Fraud – 20 years in prison; and Conspiracy to Commit Wire Fraud – 20 years in prison. The investigation was conducted by the U.S. Department of Agriculture-Office of the Inspector General, U.S. Secret Service-Money Laundering Task Force, Ohio Investigative Unit, FBI, Homeland Security Investigations, and the Euclid Police Department. Assistant United States Attorney Erica Barnhill leads the prosecution for the Northern District of Ohio. • United States v. Glenda K. Jordan (Indictment) – approximately $162,580 in intended loss On Sept. 9, 2026, Glenda K. Jordan, 63, of Painesville, Ohio, was charged with three counts of Bank Fraud, Conspiracy to Commit Bank Fraud, Theft of Government Property, and Supplemental Security Income Fraud-Knowing Concealment. For more than a decade, Jordan allegedly engaged in a scheme to mislead government agencies to fraudulently obtain SNAP benefits, HUD-funded housing benefits, and Supplemental Security Income benefits. On numerous official government documents, she lied about—and concealed—her marriage, her husband's income, and her true residence. In one instance, Jordan concealed her scheme by reporting her sister-in-law as her ‘live-in aide’ when in fact, her sister-in-law used Jordan’s subsidized unit as her primary home. Meanwhile, Jordan resided at a different location with her husband. If convicted, she faces prison sentences of up to 30 years per Bank Fraud count; 30 years for Conspiracy to Commit Bank Fraud; 10 years for Theft of Government Property; and five years for Supplemental Security Income Fraud-Knowing Concealment. The investigation was conducted by the U.S. Department of Agriculture-Office of the Inspector General, Social Security Administration-Office of the Inspector General, and the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development-Office of the Inspector General. Special Assistant United States Attorney Jason White is leading the prosecution for the Northern District of Ohio. • United States v. Myron Cage and Raymond Stevens (Complaints) – approximately $4,070 in intended loss On Sept. 30, 2026, Myron Cage, 43, of Garfield Heights, and Dwayne Stevens, 34, of Mayfield Heights, were charged with SNAP Benefits Fraud as part of a related drug trafficking operation. Between February and August 2022, Cage and Stevens allegedly obtained SNAP benefits that they received as payment, or partial payment, for crack cocaine at a corner store in Cleveland that Cage owned and operated. During search warrants executed at their residences, agents also seized more than 500 grams of packaged cocaine. If convicted, they each face up to five years in prison for SNAP Benefits Fraud offenses, and up to 40 years in prison on related drug charges. The investigation was conducted by the U.S. Department of Agriculture-Office of the Inspector General, the DEA, and the FBI Assistant United States Attorneys Robert F. Corts , Marc D. Bullard , and Samuel V. Lioi are leading the prosecution for the Northern District of Ohio. For a list of similar enforcement actions across the country, please visit justice.gov/opa/pr/dojs-fraud-division-department-agriculture-and-usda-oig-uncover-nearly-42m-snap-benefit . On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division . The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud—a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance—to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. A complaint, or indictment, are merely allegations. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Contact Jessica Salas Novak Jessica.Salas.Novak@usdoj.gov Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Fraud Components National Fraud Enforcement Division USAO - Ohio, Northern

SNAP is a federal benefits program funded by the USDA and administered by the State of Ohio. The Northern District of Ohio was a key participant in this surge effort.

title: Arizona man sentenced to 3 years in prison for smuggling meth into Montana
body: Press Release Arizona man sentenced to 3 years in prison for smuggling meth into Montana Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Montana BILLINGS – A Phoenix man who smuggled meth from Arizona to Billings was sentenced today to three years and one month in prison, followed by four years of supervised release, First Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark Steger Smith said. Sebastian Kessamer Gilder, Jr., 28, pleaded guilty in June 2025 to possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine. U.S. District Judge Kathleen S. Lane presided. The government alleged in court documents that Gilder came to the attention of law enforcement in 2021 when the Eastern Montana High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area Taskforce was in the midst of investigating a Sonora, Mexico-based drug smuggling ring known locally as “The Village.” The Village smuggled drugs from Mexico into Phoenix and then used couriers to move them into Montana by bus, personal vehicles, and the U.S. Postal Service. The shipments usually were coordinated by individuals in Hermosillo and Nogales, Sonora, Mexico. Gilder, who lived in Phoenix, was recruited by the Village to transport illicit drugs to Billings. Investigators were aware of his movements and arranged a drug buy using an undercover agent on Jan. 13, 2021. The agent successfully bought a pound of methamphetamine off Gilder, which eventually led to his arrest. This operation is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Montana comprises agents and officers from various law enforcement agencies with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Montana. The U.S. Attorney’s Office prosecuted this case. The Eastern Montana High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area Taskforce conducted the investigation. title: Former Suffolk County Corrections Officer Sentenced for COVID Unemployment and Loan Fraud
body: Press Release Former Suffolk County Corrections Officer Sentenced for COVID Unemployment and Loan Fraud Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts BOSTON – A former Suffolk County Corrections Officer was sentenced yesterday in federal court in Boston for COVID unemployment and loan fraud. Jasmine Murphy, 39, of Cambridge, Mass. was sentenced by U.S. District Court Judge Richard G. Stearns to time served (one day in prison) and two years of supervised release. The defendant was also ordered to pay $19,868 in restitution to the Department of Unemployment Assistance and $17,708 restitution to the Small Business Administration. In April 2026 , Murphy pleaded guilty to seven counts of wire fraud and one count of false statements to a financial institution. Murphy was charged in December 2024 . Murphy had been a corrections officer with the Suffolk County Sherriff’s Department from January 2022 to December 2024. Murphy fraudulently applied for pandemic unemployment and small business loan benefits while working for a workforce services company. While employed by that company, Murphy collected approximately $37,576 in unemployment benefits and small business loan funds. In Murphy’s PUA application, Murphy made fraudulent representations about her employment status and thereafter falsely claimed, on a weekly basis, that she did not work and did not receive any income during the prior week. In Murphy’s PPP loan application, Murphy submitted false statements to SBA-approved lenders, including the income and/or payroll of her purported small businesses, in order to obtain her loan. Murphy also made false representations on forms submitted to request that her PPP loan be forgiven. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Kelly M.  Lawson, Special Agent in Charge, U.S. Department of Labor, Office of Inspector General; and Inspector General Joseph V. Cuffari, Ph.D., U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Office of Inspector General, made the announcement. Assistant U.S. Attorney Dustin Chao, Chief of the Public Corruption & Special Prosecutions Unit, prosecuted the case. title: We are working with Voltus to build a 1-gigawatt virtual power plant.
body: We are working with Voltus to build a 1-gigawatt virtual power plant. Oct 22, 2026 Today, Google and Voltus announced an expanded agreement to build a 1-gigawatt (GW) virtual power plant across the PJM grid region, which serves 67 million people across 13 states and Washington, D.C. Voltus aggregates flexible capacity from local businesses and homes — like smart thermostats, batteries, and industrial assets — into a Google-funded virtual power plant. During peak demand, these assets temporarily reduce energy use to support grid reliability. In return, participating customers receive direct economic benefits, including bill savings and cash payments. Building on a 100-megawatt agreement from earlier this year, this 10-fold expansion represents one of the largest known distributed capacity portfolios deployed by a hyperscaler to date. This initiative reflects Google’s commitment to actively bring new capacity to local grids while strengthening regional reliability and affordability.

title: Leading European Financial Services Organizations Embrace Open Models to Build Proprietary Intelligence
body: Leading European Financial Services Organizations Embrace Open Models to Build Proprietary Intelligence From transaction foundation models to sovereign cloud deployments, leading financial institutions across Europe are scaling intelligent technologies with advanced computing. October 21, 2026 by Jason Renders 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! At GTC Berlin, banks, payment companies and financial data providers are showing what production-scale intelligence looks like — built on NVIDIA accelerated computing, powered by open weight models and running on their own infrastructure. Revolut is rebuilding its technology stack on a single foundation model PRAGMA , powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing. Using the NVIDIA cuDF toolkit and Dynamo-Triton software on NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs , Revolut is scaling PRAGMA in production, servicing an initial 80 million customers and engineered to scale 3x. “Revolut processes billions of transactions — the opportunity was always there, but the question was whether foundation models could operate at that scale and across domains. PRAGMA answers that,” said Pavel Nesterov, head of AI at Revolut. “Built in collaboration with NVIDIA, it’s the clearest proof yet that the gap between a research breakthrough and a production banking system can be closed.” Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Training on Accelerated Infrastructure Starling Bank , the first bank to train an agentic model on U.K. sovereign cloud infrastructure, has developed “Starling Intelligence” — the intelligence layer that underpins its AI capability — on Civo’s U.K. cloud using the bank’s own transaction data. Lloyds Banking Group built ATUM , a transaction foundation model that converts billions of banking transactions into reusable intelligence — accelerated with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs and improving efficiency across bank-wide use cases. SBS launched a banking sovereign intelligence platform so banks can run generative and agentic models without their data leaving their own walls. Open Models at a Fraction of the Cost Open weight models give European financial institutions proprietary intelligence built on data they own, at costs they control. NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform is the engine running beneath them. Neobank bunq’s agentic assistant Finn now runs on open weight models. Powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, deploying on Nebius matches the quality of leading closed models at 60% of the cost per answer. NatWest is building technology designed to recognize the full range of British accents, dialects and financial terminology, developed with NVIDIA’s speech models, including Nemotron 3.5 ASR. Modulr is building specialized models for distinct parts of payment operations, based on the NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B open model. Santander is an early adopter of the new NVIDIA Kumo family of open weight foundation models for structured financial data, using them to build specialized intelligence for core banking workloads. Accelerated Computing Transforms Financial Research LSEG is working with NVIDIA to help financial institutions analyze large volumes of historical tick data up to 10x faster with the Polars GPU engine , accelerated by NVIDIA cuDF on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs. RavenPack built a dataset generation pipeline on Bigdata.com that takes a plain-language research hypothesis and returns a labeled, backtest-ready dataset — running on a fine-tuned NVIDIA Nemotron model. Investors can use these datasets to identify, analyze and visualize market trends. Speeding Data Pipelines to Improve Fraud Detection RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs and NVIDIA cuDF help accelerate data processing across multi-terabyte-scale, siloed, regulated sources, compressing the time from data to decision for fraud and other scenarios. HSBC provides near-real-time client insights that support customer processes and on-demand decision-making while minimizing risk and fraud, powered by 5x faster data processing on Starburst Enterprise’s GPU Engine . Stripe , a global provider of programmable financial services, sees 42x faster data pipelines and 92% cost savings for its Stripe Radar fraud-detection platform with NVIDIA GPU-accelerated Ray Data in offline testing. This enables Stripe Radar’s machine learning pipelines to continuously optimize model training and improve fraud detection. Learn more about NVIDIA accelerated computing in financial services . See notice regarding software product information.
