title: NVIDIA Cosmos Opens New Tools to Train, Evaluate and Deploy World Models
body: NVIDIA Cosmos Opens New Tools to Train, Evaluate and Deploy World Models New tools joining NVIDIA Cosmos are helping accelerate data pipelines, train, evaluate and optimize world models more efficiently, and improve accuracy at lower cost. October 21, 2026 by Pranjali Joshi 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! To help developers rapidly build world models , which help physical AI systems understand and simulate the real world, NVIDIA has expanded the Cosmos platform with new training tools, simulation checkpoints and Cosmos Data Factory blueprints. Ranking top five on six different open models leaderboards, the NVIDIA Cosmos platform gives world model builders the frontier open models — as well as data, training and optimization tools and recipes — to scale training data, adapt models, test behavior and optimize for performance before deployment. Build Better Training Data Building world models begins with multimodal, multisensory data. NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory brings together the tools and skills for labeling, curating, augmenting and evaluating data at scale for training physical AI. Cosmos Curator, a GPU-accelerated solution for curating video training datasets, has now added support for multimodal multisensory inputs and processing blocks. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Cosmos Data Factory now offers the following five cloud-native blueprints and is available through GitHub , Microsoft Azure , Nebius and CoreWeave : Autonomous Vehicle Dataset Generation: Curates and labels driving data, then adds synthetic examples of hard-to-capture scenarios to expand training coverage. Image Attribute Augmentation: Varies object appearance to improve image search. Event Video Generation: Turns still images into synthetic videos of rare or unsafe events. Defect Image Generation: Generates printed circuit board, metal and glass defect images for inspection models. Video Data Augmentation: Changes weather and lighting in existing footage while preserving scene structure. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/CDF-visual-Oct20.mp4 Cosmos Data Factory accelerates data curation, processing and synthetic data generation with agentic skills. Companies are already putting Cosmos Data Factory blueprints to work to speed their physical AI development workflows. Porsche is leading the development of a shared AV data flywheel across Volkswagen Group brands, using Cosmos Data Factory through Voxel51 on Microsoft Azure. This is expected to reduce repeated physical test drives by up to 90% and shorten development cycle times by up to 85%. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Porche-Cosmos-Data-Factory.mp4 Porsche searching and augmenting autonomous vehicle data footage in Voxel51, powered by Cosmos Data Factory. ANYbotics generated over 1,500 synthetic video clips with Cosmos Data Factory blueprints, curating real-world data and validating outputs with Encord’s platform, to train its industrial-inspection robots to recognize liquid spills and other changes between facility visits. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ANYbotics-Cosmos-Data-Factory.mp4 ANYbotic s generating anomaly clips with Encord powered by NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory. Ultralytics , a computer vision company, retrained its YOLO model with real images and targeted synthetic defects generated using Cosmos Data Factory, improving defect localization and recall. Train, Adapt and Optimize Models With training data prepared, developers may train their own architecture or start with a pretrained model. At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA extended Cosmos Framework training, optimization and deployment tools and recipes as agent skills to more open models, along with Cosmos 3, giving world model builders a faster path from experimentation to deployment. Developers and agents can now adapt open models like GR00T , Alpamayo , QWEN, Pi0.5 and other compatible Hugging Face models through fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, optimize the model with distillation and quantization, and deploy with high-performing inference. Cosmos Framework is an open, modular framework of model training and optimization tools and skills to accelerate world model development. To develop a world model specialized for egocentric manipulation, robotics research lab MicroAGI post-trained Cosmos 3 on videos of humans manipulating objects and distilled its 32-billion-parameter reasoner down to an 8-billion-parameter Nano model with no loss in accuracy. Developers can label data and post-train Cosmos 3 on Roboflow for their specific environments and tasks, then deploy those models to RoboFlow hosted or on-premises NVIDIA GPUs to bring video reasoning into factories and warehouses. Test Policies and Run Models Faster Alongside these tools, NVIDIA continues advancing foundational technology through its work on Cosmos models. New Cosmos 3 Nano model variants for simulation enable developers to test autonomous policies in repeatable, hard-to-capture, multiview multisensor scenarios. Accompanying code allows developers to adapt the models to train and evaluate their own policies for autonomous vehicles and bimanual robots in interactive simulations before real-world testing. Multiview and multisensory video data generation for evaluating policies in closed loop simulation. Developers can deploy core Cosmos models using updated NVIDIA Cosmos 3 NIM microservices, which deliver up to 2x faster inference with no quality loss in validated configurations, while continuous video analysis enables sub-second alerts. For vision AI developers, the new NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) 3.3 , built on Cosmos NIM microservices, turns one prompt into an efficient video AI application and helps teams monitor 40% more video streams with the same GPU. ADNOC uses Fogsphere’s MistIQ agentic platform , built with Cosmos and the NVIDIA Metropolis VSS Blueprint , to detect safety hazards in real time across 65 sites. For rare events, Fogsphere also uses the Cosmos Data Factory to generate synthetic training data, improving detection without needing to physically stage dangerous situations. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ADNOC-Cosmos.mp4 The Cosmos platform is fully modular and open. Developers can use Cosmos Data Factory to generate training datasets, Cosmos Framework to train and adapt world models, then deploy supported Cosmos models through NIM microservices . title: How Companies Are Using NVIDIA DSX to Break the Power Bottleneck
body: How Companies Are Using NVIDIA DSX to Break the Power Bottleneck Companies around the world are using the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run AI factories as one system and unlock infrastructure development. October 21, 2026 by Vladimir Troy 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Companies around the world are building on the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run the grid and the AI factory as one system, from the substation to the rack. Their adoption of the platform responds to an acute problem. Power is now the biggest bottleneck in infrastructure. More than $300 billion in equipment is backlogged, and over 200 gigawatts of projects are waiting in U.S. interconnection queues. One root cause of the bottleneck is siloed systems. The grid, the facility and the compute inside have long been designed independently from one another, creating the conditions for delays, risk and stranded capacity. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements To help address this, NVIDIA DSX brings these systems together: NVIDIA DSX Sim and SimReady assets from leading energy manufacturers let engineers simulate the grid, substation and AI factory together, validating generators, switchgear, power systems and cooling before breaking ground. NVIDIA DSX Flex syncs AI factory demand with grid conditions and onsite generation, turning AI factories from static loads into flexible grid assets. NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS and DSX Exchange squeeze more compute from every watt and securely share signals across compute, networking, energy, cooling and operations. GE Vernova is deploying its grid-to-facility and rack power expertise to complement NVIDIA DSX systems, enabling customers to transform power constraints into competitive advantages while maximizing compute and token output, sustainability and grid reliability. Hitachi Energy ’s battery energy storage system has qualified as NVIDIA DSX Ready ,  helping customers identify power infrastructure that meets applicable NVIDIA DSX reference architecture design requirements for resilient, reliable and scalable AI factories. Schneider Electric , together with AVEVA and ETAP, is advancing NVIDIA DSX with validated NVIDIA Vera Rubin power and cooling reference architectures and an NVIDIA Omniverse -powered AI factory digital twin. Combining AVEVA ’s engineering software expertise with NVIDIA SimReady assets, OpenUSD and Omniverse enables connecting simulations, real-time operational data and AI-driven optimization across AVEVA, Schneider Electric and third-party solutions. Together, these capabilities help organizations design, simulate, operate and optimize data centers across their lifecycle, improving energy efficiency and workload performance while accelerating time to token. Siemens Energy is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA by developing a reference design for resilient, scalable and grid-aware power infrastructure across power generation, transmission and distribution. This design is aligned with the requirements of the NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin AI factory design. title: NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations
body: NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations October 21, 2026 by Mavi Nafria 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a digital twin. Frontier Results With Open Models Retail leaders and technology companies across Europe are using NVIDIA-accelerated open and frontier models to advance agentic commerce, digital product discovery and retail R&D. Shopify post-trains open models to reach frontier-level accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Its engineers use the NVIDIA Megatron Bridge library for faster fine-tuning and NVIDIA NeMo RL for reinforcement learning. Shopify has post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for the GraphQL subagent integrated into Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant for merchants. The subagent retrieves store data for several Sidekick features, including Sidekick Pulse, which researches a merchant’s store and recommends ways to improve it. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements On Shopify’s internal benchmark, the post-trained model surpasses a leading frontier model in accuracy while cutting serving costs by 90% and delivering responses 7x faster. Beyond Sidekick, NVIDIA CCluster vLLM inference optimization software helped Shopify achieve 4.5x faster performance and up to 12x lower inference cost across five additional use cases: catalog enrichment, merchant assistant, e-commerce shopping simulation, product taxonomy classification, and merchant and buyer recommendations. Zooplus , Europe’s leading online pet retailer, with Infosys and NVIDIA technologies rebuilt its product discovery stack for the agentic era. A production ready prototype deployed inside Zooplus ’ Amazon Web Services (AWS) environment achieved 86% search accuracy using the NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever library for semantic search and the NVIDIA Blueprint for retail catalog enrichment for generated, search-ready product attributes. Photoroom results from its deployment with Vestiaire Collective , where its Image Editing API now standardizes every primary image,  about 40,000 a day across 70 countries, at the point of listing. Listings processed by Photoroom sold at a 5% higher rate of liquidity, with 3% to 7% more unique views per product page . The pipeline runs on NVIDIA GPUs with TensorRT and Triton Inference Server, and NVIDIA Dynamo Snapshot can help users quickly respond to demand spikes. Omi launched ProductDrop, a workflow that anchors every generated image to an approved digital twin, letting brands scale creative output across entire catalogs without introducing product errors . L’Oréal is using this approach, combining Omi ’s digital twins with generated brand environments within its CreAItech program. Omi runs TRELLIS 3D asset generation on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, speeding up inference by 10x and reducing pipeline latency by 4x. In addition, L’Oréal is accelerating the discovery of the best ingredient combinations, moving from months of experimentation to hours of computational screening, with the integration of NVIDIA ALCHEMI into its research workflow. L’Oréal is also testing this approach with CurieOS, Orbital Industries ‘ operating system for science and engineering, using OrbMol-v2, its open source molecular simulation model. Integrated with the NVIDIA ALCHEMI Toolkit and powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, OrbMol-v2 is five times faster than comparable models and delivers 21% lower error than the next-best model of its kind. This AI-based workflow enables researchers to identify the most promising ingredient combinations for solubilizing UV filters and optimizing performance before committing to laboratory testing. Mirakl , a software company for intelligent commerce, runs open models on NVIDIA GPUs, both on its own infrastructure and through European cloud providers like Scaleway . This keeps its technology sovereign, avoids vendor lock-in and delivers the speed and scale its customers expect . Mirakl ’s Catalog Transformer pairs fine-tuned open models with proprietary services and has onboarded more than 70 million products, turning messy vendor data into accurate, well-organized catalogs. Physical Intelligence Enables Training in Simulation NVIDIA physical AI, digital twins and open models help simulate retail environments, automate warehouse operations and deliver virtual try-on experiences for European retailers and fashion brands. Otto Group advanced its autonomous warehouse under human supervision initiative — built with Reply on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and running on Google Cloud — to the group’s largest fulfillment center in Haldensleben, Germany. New capabilities let logistics teams design, test and optimize warehouse operations entirely in simulation before any physical implementation . ALLSIDES launched its 3D Digital Twin Factory: an automated pipeline that transforms physical objects into SimReady 3D digital twins in minutes, capturing sub-millimeter geometric accuracy, measured physical properties and fully relightable materials that maintain accuracy under any lighting condition. Those digital twins serve as the foundation for simulating entire store layouts in 3D, as well as for tracking products reliably throughout the shopping journey and at checkout regardless of ambient light. Built on NVIDIA CUDA, OptiX and TensorRT, the platform already serves brands including adidas , Amazon , Nike , Zalando and Zara . CATCHES achieved production results from its RealFit deployment with AMIRI of conversion up 55%, add-to-cart up 80% and gross sales up 56% , all after seasonal adjustment against like-for-like styles. The company launched PredictiveFit, extending physics-based virtual try-on to retailers, as well as CASI, a personal fashion agent that shops, styles and sizes for customers over WhatsApp, powered by open weight models including NVIDIA Nemotron 3, built on NVIDIA Omniverse and the Newton Physics Engine. Explore New NVIDIA Retail Blueprints at the Nebius Booth At GTC Berlin, Nebius is showcasing three NVIDIA Blueprints for retail , all available in early access and running on Nebius infrastructure, accelerated by NVIDIA: Agent Harness for Employee Productivity : An agentic assistant that consolidates scheduling, task management, inventory alerts and operational insights for store managers. Inventory Simulation and Optimization: A blueprint that can help retailers reduce overstock and stockouts by modeling demand scenarios, testing replenishment strategies and optimizing stock levels before users need to commit in the real world. Agentic Finetuning Flywheel: A self-improving loop that uses agentic workflows to continuously generate training data, fine-tune open source models and feed real-world performance back into the next training cycle. Request early access to the blueprints and learn more about NVIDIA technologies for retail and consumer packaged goods . See notice regarding software product information. title: Pioneers Across Europe Deploy NVIDIA Earth-2 Open Models to Power Real-World Weather and Climate Prediction
body: Pioneers Across Europe Deploy NVIDIA Earth-2 Open Models to Power Real-World Weather and Climate Prediction October 21, 2026 by Niall Robinson 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Weather forecasts shape more than daily plans; timely weather information is crucial for energy producers, insurers and transport operators to plan around changing conditions. A global forecast can show a storm taking shape, but decisions about solar farms, shipping routes or insured property depend on what happens locally. NVIDIA Earth-2 gives developers and researchers a family of open AI models and tools they can customize with their own data. Running on NVIDIA computing, these technologies support global weather prediction, detailed regional forecasts and environmental research. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements StormScope EU is the latest model to join Earth-2 — a regional version of the StormScope model for short-term forecasting, trained over Europe weather and climate data. It uses EUMETSAT satellite observations to predict evolving cloud conditions across 16 Meteosat channels at 10-minute intervals. At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is showcasing a live StormScope EU pipeline in an interactive weather demo built in partnership with Earthmover . The demo uses Earth2Studio to run forecasts and Earthmover’s data platform to manage and serve the real-time results, which are updated as soon as new satellite observations come in, every 10 minutes. Earthmover serves these results as map tiles, letting visitors explore predictions across Europe without downloading entire datasets. Developers can combine Earth-2 models in workflows tailored to regional needs, using StormScope for short-term forecasting and CorrDiff to add local detail to coarser weather data. Developers can also pick up these model architectures and train them for new environmental applications such as air-quality modeling. The open source NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo framework provides training and customization tools so teams can build applications that incorporate proprietary data and domain expertise to meet regional needs. Organizations building on Earth-2 capabilities include: AXA is using NVIDIA Earth-2’s FourCastNet 3 to study regional cyclone risk beyond the historical record across more than 1,000 simulated seasons, generating insights that can inform risk assessments and help customers target prevention efforts. Vaisala Xweather is combining Earth-2 with its proprietary observations , lightning data and forecasting expertise to enhance its weather intelligence platforms for government, energy, maritime, transportation and insurance customers. Its work includes adapting StormScope with lightning data to advance short-term forecasting lead time and make these warnings accessible through Vaisala Xweather’s software-as-a-service offerings and AI-assistant integrations. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Vaisala-Xweather-Nvidia-StormScope.mp4 Video courtesy of Vaisala Xweather. University of Manchester researchers adapted the Earth-2 CorrDiff model for U.K. air-quality modeling. It trained the model on the NVIDIA-powered Isambard-AI supercomputer and ran it locally on NVIDIA DGX Spark systems, bringing environmental modeling from a national supercomputer to the desktop. TotalEnergies is exploring NVIDIA Earth-2 for solar-energy forecasting, evaluating StormScope-based solar-radiation nowcasts at two photovoltaic sites and developing models to provide weather information at subhourly intervals. The work explores how more detailed forecasts could help anticipate changes in solar-power generation. Space42 developed SARDiff4Height using CorrDiff and NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo. The research estimates surface heights from a single radar image and produces uncertainty maps, helping analysts understand where estimates need closer scrutiny. Explore NVIDIA Earth-2 open models and tools , and explore with Earth2Studio’s forecasting examples . Read AXA’s hurricane-risk case study and Manchester’s air-quality story to learn how teams are adapting weather AI to specialized challenges. title: NVIDIA Open Models Power a New Wave of European Public Sector Projects
body: NVIDIA Open Models Power a New Wave of European Public Sector Projects Across Europe, open models help governments provide essential public services while keeping sensitive data on organizations’ own infrastructure. October 21, 2026 by Eva-Maria Hempe 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Governments need modern solutions to serve the public while keeping sensitive information under their control. Open models provide a path forward, letting governments evaluate them, adapt them to local languages and public services, run them on infrastructure they control, apply their own safeguards and keep sensitive data within controlled environments. Some open models go further, with the datasets they were trained on published so governments can verify if training data was licensed, biased or compliant. NVIDIA partners and European governments are teaming to bring  advanced models to boost the efficiency of public administration while retaining control of data and infrastructure. Several are also building editions of the NVIDIA Nemotron-Personas collection , the partner-grounded datasets behind NeMo User Sim , NVIDIA’s open source library for population-scale user simulation that dynamically evaluates and trains models and agents in local languages. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements European Commission: Scaling Governed AI Applications Berlin-based software company deepset is expanding its Haystack Enterprise Platform , the foundation of AI@EC, the European Commission’s shared platform for building and running AI applications on commission-managed infrastructure. The update connects agent development, execution, optimization and governance for all customers, adding capabilities to compare operating costs, evaluate answer quality and trace problems. NVIDIA Triton Inference Server supports the shared services used to find and rank relevant information. The expansion builds on operating requirements demonstrated by deployments such as AI@EC, where reusable components, role-based access, audit trails and guardrails support applications including document summarization, knowledge management and multilingual policy analysis. Poland: Advanced Computing for Healthcare and Employment Deloitte is helping Poland build agentic systems for healthcare and employment services using open models. Poland’s eHealth Centre is building its Intelligent Services Platform for medical imaging with NVIDIA DGX BasePOD and the MONAI framework. The tool will help physicians analyze X-rays, CT scans and MRI images, detect abnormalities and prioritize urgent cases, reducing the time patients wait for results. With Deloitte’s support, Poland’s Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Policy is developing an agentic factory on NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure. Designed to support more than 400 labor offices, it will run models including PLLuM, GPT OSS and Inkling for document search, summarization and digital assistants, helping staff more efficiently assist job seekers. NVIDIA is also working with SpeakLeash in Poland and the University of Ljubljana in Slovenia on country-specific additions to its synthetic personas program, with localized datasets planned to follow. UK: Data for Locally Relevant Advanced Modeling London-based Locai Labs released Nemotron-Personas-UK , a dataset of 1 million synthetic personas reflecting the U.K.’s demographic and geographic diversity while reducing privacy risk. Potential uses include healthcare evaluation and bias testing across age groups, education levels and rural and urban populations. For developers building public-service models, it offers a way to test whether models work consistently across different communities. Germany: Digital Assistants and AI for Classified Work In Germany, Materna is introducing Sinfonie, an on-premises platform combining generative AI, voice interaction and 3D avatars, with NVIDIA Audio2Face available for animation. Built on a project for a German state administration, it helps employees access institutional knowledge through spoken questions while keeping data on their organization’s infrastructure. For organizations handling classified information, secunet, NVIDIA, Red Hat and deepset are going a step further. The four companies are developing a sovereign cloud offering built on secunet’s proven SINA Cloud foundation, which includes security components that have been authorized for use with classified information. The planned offering combines four components: NVIDIA accelerated computing and NVIDIA Nemotron open models; Red Hat OpenShift AI for deploying and managing AI workloads; deepset’s Haystack AI agent orchestration; and infrastructure operated by secunet in German data centers. To support local development, the Sovereign Open Source Foundation Models research initiative (Soofi) is developing a family of AI models for German industry and the public sector. That includes Nemotron-Personas-Germany, an open dataset of 1 million records, each with six synthetic personas, grounded in the 2022 census across all 16 federal states and 400 districts. Created with NVIDIA NeMo Data Designer without real people’s private data, the dataset helps developers test whether public-service models work consistently across regions, age groups and communities. Like the U.K. edition, it can be used with NeMo User Sim so developers can evaluate and train models against simulated users based on synthetic German personas. France: Advanced Open Models in the Public Sector Workspace CANUT, France’s public purchasing body for digital services, selected LINAGORA and Docaposte to provide a sovereign collaborative workspace built on Twake.ai. More than 2,500 eligible organizations, including municipalities, schools and healthcare institutions, can access the framework without running their own tender. The workspace offers public employees email, document sharing and collaboration tools, with NVIDIA technology supporting speech transcription and infrastructure hosted in France. Région Occitanie is the preferred partner for scaling deployment. Greece: A Local Agentic Ecosystem Greek AI and energy company KIEFER is developing an agentic factory built on NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD with DGX GB200 alongside Sophea open weight models and Greek-language tools for knowledge retrieval, speech and digital assistants. These capabilities stand to make institutional information easier to find and use for Greek-speaking public sector teams, while giving organizations control over where agents run and how data is handled. Codefest: Building the Next Applications In an effort to support public sector organizations in integrating agentic AI in Europe and beyond, NVIDIA Open Models Codefest brings together startups, software providers and labs across the region to turn open models into locally controlled solutions for public sector challenges, including medical reasoning, AI tutoring and model governance. The top five teams are Pleias , Zehnlab.ai , Disseqt , Algoritmica GmbH and ABA Technology . Deutsche Telekom and T-Systems have provided the compute infrastructure for teams to train and deploy large language models. Several are also building editions of the NVIDIA Nemotron-Personas collection , the partner-grounded datasets behind NeMo User Sim , NVIDIA’s open source library for population-scale user simulation that dynamically evaluates and trains models and agents in local languages. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements European Commission: Scaling Governed AI Applications Berlin-based software company deepset is expanding its Haystack Enterprise Platform , the foundation of AI@EC, the European Commission’s shared platform for building and running AI applications on commission-managed infrastructure. The update connects agent development, execution, optimization and governance for all customers, adding capabilities to compare operating costs, evaluate answer quality and trace problems. NVIDIA Triton Inference Server supports the shared services used to find and rank relevant information. The expansion builds on operating requirements demonstrated by deployments such as AI@EC, where reusable components, role-based access, audit trails and guardrails support applications including document summarization, knowledge management and multilingual policy analysis. Poland: Advanced Computing for Healthcare and Employment Deloitte is helping Poland build agentic systems for healthcare and employment services using open models. Poland’s eHealth Centre is building its Intelligent Services Platform for medical imaging with NVIDIA DGX BasePOD and the MONAI framework. The tool will help physicians analyze X-rays, CT scans and MRI images, detect abnormalities and prioritize urgent cases, reducing the time patients wait for results. With Deloitte’s support, Poland’s Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Policy is developing an agentic factory on NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure. Designed to support more than 400 labor offices, it will run models including PLLuM, GPT OSS and Inkling for document search, summarization and digital assistants, helping staff more efficiently assist job seekers. NVIDIA is also working with SpeakLeash in Poland and the University of Ljubljana in Slovenia on country-specific additions to its synthetic personas program, with localized datasets planned to follow. UK: Data for Locally Relevant Advanced Modeling London-based Locai Labs released Nemotron-Personas-UK , a dataset of 1 million synthetic personas reflecting the U.K.’s demographic and geographic diversity while reducing privacy risk. Potential uses include healthcare evaluation and bias testing across age groups, education levels and rural and urban populations. For developers building public-service models, it offers a way to test whether models work consistently across different communities. Germany: Digital Assistants and AI for Classified Work In Germany, Materna is introducing Sinfonie, an on-premises platform combining generative AI, voice interaction and 3D avatars, with NVIDIA Audio2Face available for animation. Built on a project for a German state administration, it helps employees access institutional knowledge through spoken questions while keeping data on their organization’s infrastructure. For organizations handling classified information, secunet, NVIDIA, Red Hat and deepset are going a step further. The four companies are developing a sovereign cloud offering built on secunet’s proven SINA Cloud foundation, which includes security components that have been authorized for use with classified information. The planned offering combines four components: NVIDIA accelerated computing and NVIDIA Nemotron open models; Red Hat OpenShift AI for deploying and managing AI workloads; deepset’s Haystack AI agent orchestration; and infrastructure operated by secunet in German data centers. To support local development, the Sovereign Open Source Foundation Models research initiative (Soofi) is developing a family of AI models for German industry and the public sector. That includes Nemotron-Personas-Germany, an open dataset of 1 million records, each with six synthetic personas, grounded in the 2022 census across all 16 federal states and 400 districts. Created with NVIDIA NeMo Data Designer without real people’s private data, the dataset helps developers test whether public-service models work consistently across regions, age groups and communities. Like the U.K. edition, it can be used with NeMo User Sim so developers can evaluate and train models against simulated users based on synthetic German personas. France: Advanced Open Models in the Public Sector Workspace CANUT, France’s public purchasing body for digital services, selected LINAGORA and Docaposte to provide a sovereign collaborative workspace built on Twake.ai. More than 2,500 eligible organizations, including municipalities, schools and healthcare institutions, can access the framework without running their own tender. The workspace offers public employees email, document sharing and collaboration tools, with NVIDIA technology supporting speech transcription and infrastructure hosted in France. Région Occitanie is the preferred partner for scaling deployment. Greece: A Local Agentic Ecosystem Greek AI and energy company KIEFER is developing an agentic factory built on NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD with DGX GB200 alongside Sophea open weight models and Greek-language tools for knowledge retrieval, speech and digital assistants. These capabilities stand to make institutional information easier to find and use for Greek-speaking public sector teams, while giving organizations control over where agents run and how data is handled. Codefest: Building the Next Applications In an effort to support public sector organizations in integrating agentic AI in Europe and beyond, NVIDIA Open Models Codefest brings together startups, software providers and labs across the region to turn open models into locally controlled solutions for public sector challenges, including medical reasoning, AI tutoring and model governance. The top five teams are Pleias , Zehnlab.ai , Disseqt , Algoritmica GmbH and ABA Technology . Deutsche Telekom and T-Systems have provided the compute infrastructure for teams to train and deploy large language models. title: October 22, 2026 - FDA Launches New Program to Advance Neuroscience Medical Product Development
body: FDA News Release FDA Launches New Program to Advance Neuroscience Medical Product Development Neuroscience Advancement and Innovation Nexus to coordinate agency action on brain and nervous system conditions, with inaugural focus on Alzheimer's prevention For Immediate Release: October 22, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today announced the launch of the Neuroscience Advancement and Innovation Nexus (NAIN) , a new agency program aligned with the Trump Administration’s efforts to accelerate medical innovation and deliver breakthrough treatments. NAIN is designed to advance the science, tools, and regulatory approaches needed to support the development of medical products for conditions affecting the brain and nervous system. NAIN’s inaugural initiative, the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator , will focus on advancing medical products that help delay or prevent Alzheimer's disease. Both efforts support the National Alzheimer’s Project Act (NAPA), the federal government's comprehensive roadmap for coordinated action on Alzheimer's and related dementias. "The launch of NAIN reflects FDA's commitment — in support of the Trump Administration’s drive to transform health care innovation — to making sure our regulatory science and cross-center collaboration keep pace with the rapid advances happening in neuroscience," said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. "Through NAIN and the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator, we are bringing the full breadth of FDA's expertise to bear on one of the most urgent public health challenges of our time.” Developing medical products for neuroscience indications is associated with complex scientific and clinical challenges, including limited understanding of underlying biology, variable disease presentation, and difficulties in demonstrating meaningful clinical benefit, particularly for conditions that develop over many years. Advances in biomarkers, digital health technologies, and other medical product development tools, however, offer important opportunities to address these challenges. NAIN will bring together scientific and regulatory expertise from the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, and Center for Devices and Radiological Health to address scientific and regulatory questions that benefit from coordinated consideration across drugs, biologics, and devices. NAIN will encompass conditions that affect the brain and nervous system broadly, including neurologic and psychiatric disorders, substance use disorders, and pain. NAIN will also support robust engagement with patients, industry, academia and other stakeholders to advance these efforts. As its first initiative, NAIN is launching the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator . This inaugural initiative will draw on perspectives from across the FDA and engage patients and caregivers, researchers, industry, public-private partnerships and other government agencies. The initiative will explore innovative approaches to advancing clinical trials for Alzheimer’s disease prevention and early-intervention drug development with emphasis on trial populations, stage-appropriate endpoints, and evidentiary approaches for demonstrating prevention or delay of cognitive decline due to Alzheimer’s disease. The FDA has long been committed to supporting the development of safe and effective medical products that address diseases and conditions of the brain and nervous system. Through NAIN and the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator, the agency is taking a proactive, coordinated approach to accelerating progress, bringing together its scientific and regulatory expertise, engaging the broader research and development community, and working in concert with federal partners to meet the scale of this public health challenge. Media: FDA Request for Comment 202-690-6343 Consumer: 888-INFO-FDA The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products. ###

title: Operation Economic Outcast Targets Iran’s Shadow Fleet Networks
body: October 21, 2026 Law Firms, Shipping Agents, and Vessels Helped Conceal and Transport Iranian Commodities WASHINGTON —Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury sanctioned Panama- and Greece-based law firm Karnakis and Karnakis , which has supported illicit Iranian shipping activity for years, indirectly aiding Tehran’s ability to generate revenue to fund its military, weapons, and nuclear programs.  Throughout Operation Economic Outcast, Treasury has continued to coordinate with counterparts in Europe and around the world to sever the Iranian regime’s remaining economic lifelines. “Whether you are conducting illegal oil transfers at sea or sitting in the corner office of a law firm, if you are supporting the Iranian regime, we will find you and sanction you,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “Iran’s facilitators must make a choice: Either you are with us or against us. We know who you are, we know what you’re doing, and we will continue to take action.” Treasury today also sanctioned Singapore- and UAE-based shipping agents that directly aid Iranian shadow fleet operations.  Today’s actions strike not only the legal and maritime facilitators that sustain Iran's sanctions-evasion networks, but also a fleet of cargo vessels that has helped generate substantial revenue for the Iranian regime. The designations imposed today are being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the Iranian petroleum and petrochemical sectors, among other key sectors of the Iranian economy. FinCEN is acting in close coordination with European partners, including in Greece, and leveraging existing legal authorities, such as its first issuance of an administrative subpoena pursuant to 31 U.S.C. § 5318(k) of the Bank Secrecy Act, to advance its investigation into a Greek bank’s potential ties to Iran and its proxies. Additionally, FinCEN has issued multiple requests for information concerning banks’ relationships with OFAC-designated Iranian financial institutions. OPERATION ECONOMIC OUTCAST IS ISOLATING THE IRANIAN REGIME Announced by Secretary Bessent on August 24, 2026 and dubbed Economic D-Day, Operation Economic Outcast is severing the remaining economic lifelines that sustain the Iranian regime. Treasury has mapped the networks, facilitators, and financial channels that Iran uses to smuggle oil, evade sanctions, and fund terror.  Working with partners across the U.S. government, the European Union, United Kingdom, Gulf partners, and others, Treasury is targeting any source of the regime’s illicit revenue, as well as its sanctions evasion schemes to move funds. Operation Economic Outcast significantly expanded sanctions risk for those who continue to choose to do business with Iran.  Treasury warned that any entity facilitating money laundering or sanctions evasion on behalf of Iran risks being cut off from the U.S. financial system.  Operation Economic Outcast also expanded sanctions exposure for non-U.S. persons who continue doing business with the Iranian regime and will accelerate the pace of U.S. enforcement. More information on Operation Economic Outcast is available here . LAW FIRM ESTABLISHING SHADOW FLEET ARCHITECTURE Through Operation Economic Outcast, Treasury is targeting law firms and corporate service providers that establish shell and front companies for persons trading in sanctioned Iranian products, an essential service needed for any such malign actor to evade sanctions or regulatory compliance.  Panama- and Greece-based law firm Karnakis and Karnakis has for years leveraged its legal practice to register shipping companies that own shadow fleet vessels responsible for shipping hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of Iranian steel, petroleum, and petrochemicals, among other goods.  The firm previously set up the companies Skyros Maritime and Trading S.A. , Corfu Maritime and Trading S.A. , and Elias Shipping and Trading Group S.A. , among others, all of which OFAC has previously designated for their ownership of vessels active in the trade of Iranian petroleum and petroleum products. Elias Shipping and Trading SA, the owner of the RAMONA 1 (IMO: 9233222), served as a front company for the Al-Qatirji Company, a Syrian firm responsible for selling millions of barrels of Iranian oil for the benefit of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF) and Houthis.  The Al-Qatirji Company at the time of its designation was one of the main financial channels for the IRGC-QF, enabling the terrorist group to generate and access hundreds of millions of dollars a year in revenue gained from the sale of Iranian oil. Karnakis and Karnakis played a particularly critical role in establishing the corporate architecture for the shipping empire of Iranian liquified petroleum gas (LPG) magnate Seyed Asadoollah Emamjomeh (Emamjomeh), which is collectively responsible for shipping hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of Iranian LPG and crude oil.  Karnakis and Karnakis served as the corporate agent for many of Emamjomeh’s firms, including several that were ultimately designated for their role in shipping Iranian petroleum products. Karnakis and Karnakis was founded, and is currently owned, by dual Panamanian-Greek nationals Sofianos Karnakis Kosmas and Konstantinos Karnakis Kosmas , with Panamanian-Greek national Ioanis Karnakis Kosmas and Panamanian national Pedro Ortega Jones serving as employees of the law firm.  Karnakis and Karnakis employees, including Panamanian national Roberto Ortega Jones , act as directors and officers of many of the companies they register in order to obfuscate the true beneficial owners of these companies. Karnakis and Karnakis is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petroleum and petrochemical sectors of the Iranian economy.  Sofianos Karnakis Kosmas, Konstantinos Karnakis Kosmas, Pedro Ortega Jones, Roberto Ortega Jones, and Ioanis Karnakis Kosmas are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Karnakis and Karnakis. CARGO FLEET VESSELS Iran relies on seemingly legitimate cargo vessels to move Iranian petrochemicals and other products, including steel.  Panama- and Greece-based Roxette Maritime Shipping and Trading S.A. (Roxette), for which Karnakis and Karnakis serves as the corporate agent, is the operator and ship manager of the Panama-flagged vessels ANEMOS (IMO 9205952), GLORIS (IMO 9449510), and PRIDE (IMO 9487407), all of which have shipped various cargos of Iranian-origin goods within the past year, including petrochemicals and steel products.  In addition, Roxette is the ship manager and operator of the Panama-flagged cargo vessels DESTINY (IMO 9385491), FLAMINGO 1 (IMO 9474199), HARMONY (IMO 9449522), and PRINCE (IMO 9548316). Roxette Maritime Shipping and Trading S.A. is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petrochemical sector of the Iranian economy.  ANEMOS, GLORIS, PRIDE, DESTINY, FLAMINGO 1, HARMONY, and PRINCE are being identified pursuant to E.O. 13902 as blocked property in which Roxette Maritime Shipping and Trading S.A. has an interest. SHIPPING AGENTS AIDING SHADOW FLEET Shipping agents play a critical role in shadow fleet operations by aiding the transit of illicit Iranian cargo through ports, including oil, petroleum, and other commodities.  Treasury is taking action against two shipping agents that have helped Iran transport its products to buyers around the world. Amigoz Singapore PTE. Ltd. (Amigoz) is a Singapore-based full-range shipping agency that provides port agency services.  Amigoz acted as the agent for a shipment of light crude oil overseen by Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars Company, which oversees a network of front companies that supports the allocation of billions of dollars’ worth of commodities to Iranian military entities.  As of 2026, Amigoz has been associated with a range of dark fleet actors, including some affiliated with the shipping empire of Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani , and provided bunkering services to the Iranian shadow fleet vessel ZIXUAN (IMO 9317298). Whales Shipping Line LLC (Whales), a Dubai-based maritime and logistics company, acted as the shipping agent for Sparrow Trading FZE, a sanctioned Dubai-based front company that organized the purchase of tens of millions of dollars’ worth of Iranian petrochemicals in coordination with Persian Gulf Petrochemical Industry Commercial Co.  Whales has also conducted business worth hundreds of thousands of dollars with Amigoz.  Whales is the registered owner of two UAE-flagged small support vessels: WHALES DIAMOND (IMO 9375032) and WHALES PEARL (IMO 9483114). Amigoz Singapore PTE. Ltd. is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petroleum sector of the Iranian economy.  Whales Shipping Line LLC is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Amigoz Singapore PTE. Ltd.  WHALES DIAMOND and WHALES PEARL are being identified as blocked property in which Whales Shipping Line LLC has an interest. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities with designated or otherwise blocked persons. Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions.  OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.  For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List . Click here for more information on the persons designated today . ###

title: Recreating the lost studios of women sculptors with Prune Nourry
body: Recreating the lost studios of women sculptors with Prune Nourry Oct 21, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link We partnered with artist Prune Nourry on a documentary film that uses Google AI to recreate the workspaces of 19th-century sculptors, bringing their legacies back into focus. Prune Nourry Artist Amit Sood VP, Google Arts & Culture Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Listen to article [[duration]] minutes This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X Read AI-generated summary Artist Prune Nourry and Google Arts & Culture are honoring 18 overlooked female sculptors in the new "Visionaries" exhibition at the Petit Palais in Paris. The project uses generative artificial intelligence to recreate the artists' lost studios and highlight how women were historically erased from the art world. You can visit the exhibition from October 20, 2026, through January 30, 2027, or watch the accompanying documentary online. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. "Recreating the lost studios of women sculptors" celebrates forgotten female artists in Paris. Artist Prune Nourry honors 18 historical sculptors with new monumental plaster portraits. Researchers used archival letters and photos to uncover these women's hidden creative lives. Google’s AI brings these lost studios to life through immersive 3D models. Visit the "Visionaries" exhibition in Paris to see these women’s stories restored. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. History often forgot the talented women who worked as sculptors in Paris long ago. Artist Prune Nourry is now using AI to recreate their lost studios and bring their stories back to life. These digital models let you walk through their workspaces and see how they lived. It’s a cool way to show how these women were unfairly left out of history books. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer Throughout the late 19th and early 20th centuries, talented female sculptors lived and worked across Paris. Despite social constraints and limited access to artistic training, these pioneers made their mark in a predominantly male art world. Yet for a long time, women appeared in art history primarily as models or muses, while their roles as active artists were pushed into the background. On October 20, a new exhibition titled "Visionaries" opens at the Petit Palais in Paris, coinciding with Art Basel Paris. The exhibition presents monumental plaster portraits sculpted by Prune Nourry, celebrating 18 historical female sculptors and their creative legacies. To expand on their lives, Prune and Google Arts & Culture collaborated with film director Vincent Lorca on a 10-minute documentary. The project builds on a year of research during which three art historians gathered letters, journals, and photographic portraits of women sculptors who lived and worked in Paris. Because few historical photos of their actual workspaces exist, Lynn Cherny, creative technologist-in-residence at the Google Arts & Culture Lab used Google’s generative AI and image editing models to bring to life the studios of sculptors like Nancy Elizabeth Prophet, Jane Poupelet, and Camille Claudel. Using a custom tool built with Google Gemini, the team created 3D models from archival photos to animate camera paths, allowing viewers to move virtually through the historical studios. In another sequence conceived by Prune and Lorca, AI image editing is used to make the female students slowly fade from an archival photograph of Antoine Bourdelle’s studio, leaving only the men. The effect visually demonstrates how these talented women vanished from history. "Visionaries" runs at the Petit Palais from October 20, 2026, through January 30, 2027, alongside the film installation in the museum galleries and a behind-the-scenes trailer online on Google Arts & Culture . To discover more stories of trailblazing women who have shaped global culture, explore more Google Arts & Culture initiatives, such as Surfacing Women in Smithsonian History with the Smithsonian, Road to Equality , Women in India: Unheard Stories , and the Artemisia Gentileschi retrospective . Waze is bringing the connoisseur of happy chaos to your passenger seat for the arrival of The Cat in the Hat, only in theatres November 6. Voiced by comedy icon Bill Hader, the Cat is on a brand-new mission: delivering pure delight to drivers everywhere. Expect turn-by-turn directions packed with Seussian rhymes, unshakeable optimism, and playful sound effects turning everyday traffic into THE. BEST. DRIVE. EVER! Along with the Cat’s voice navigation, you can express yourself with the “Delightful” Mood (his iconic red-and-white stovepipe hat) or the mischievous “Impulsive” Mood (Thing 1). Complete the ride by swapping your navigation arrow for the Cat’s fantastical hero vehicle: the jet-powered Magical Couch. This experience is available globally in English. Open Waze and tap the banner in your menu or activate it now.

title: Bringing the Spark to Europe: Local Intelligence Powers Next Wave of Agents
body: Bringing the Spark to Europe: Local Intelligence Powers Next Wave of Agents At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is highlighting secure, local systems across RTX Spark, DGX Spark and DGX Station systems to accelerate coding, engineering, robotics and AI factory development. October 21, 2026 by Gerardo Delgado 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is showcasing its full lineup of local AI hardware. RTX Spark , which launched last week , powers personal agents on Windows PCs; DGX Spark supports developers building and scaling applications on Linux; and DGX Station serves enterprise teams running frontier workloads on Linux, with a Windows version arriving in December. Announcements include: Underdog Desktop Agent now available for RTX Spark DGX Spark 64GB available on Friday, Oct. 23 NVIDIA Sync to support eight DGX Sparks and add Model Launcher this month October DGX Spark software update adds Wi-Fi Assistant and updates DGX Spark Skills DGX Station improves manageability with seven new integrations DGX Station for Windows launches in December with support for many manufacturing apps and agent harnesses Three new open source reference workflows for robotics on DGX Station NVIDIA Cloud Functions is coming in early access to DGX Station Recursive Flint, a new local coding model, is now available for NVIDIA local hardware Day-0 support for new Nemotron, GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax and FLUX.3 AI models New accelerations for llama.cpp and vLLM inference engines and a new collection of checkpoints optimized for local AI hardware. Learn more about these local AI announcements below, and check out the demos and sessions at GTC Berlin . Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements RTX Spark Brings Personal Agents to the Windows PC RTX Spark is a new beginning for the PC — running personal agents, accelerated content creation and 1440p 100 frames-per-second gaming with up to 128GB of unified memory and 1 petaflop of AI compute. Here’s what early reviewers are saying about the platform since its October 16 release: “A dream machine for serious creators … ” — CGMag “Designed for the future of AI … ” — The Verge “An extremely capable, surprisingly portable and efficient machine … ” — PCMag Underdog , a new desktop agent app built for fully local, private AI, is also bringing its experience to RTX Spark. Powered by its Husky model-specific inference engine, Underdog runs models entirely on device, so personal agents can get work done without user data ever leaving the PC. Underdog is available now for download . To better enable developers and enthusiasts to build and customize local agents, many RTX Spark laptops come with an unlocked bootloader. During the GTC keynote, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang showed off how AI agents running on RTX Spark can be used to train Hugging Face’s Microduck robot using NVIDIA Isaac Lab, Hermes Agent and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B. ASUS , Dell Technologies , HP , Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI laptops are available today, with Acer coming soon. Learn more about RTX Spark , and get started with the latest RTX Spark playbooks . DGX Spark Gives Developers Room to Build New DGX Spark 64GB systems — that can run models including Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B 24GB, Qwen3.8 27B and Gemma 4 26B-A4B — start rolling out from partners on Friday, Oct. 23. When workloads require more capacity, developers can connect multiple DGX Spark systems via built-in NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking and NVIDIA Sync Cluster Assistant . This allows users to run advanced coding models like Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, DeepSeek v4 Flash 0731 and GLM 5.3 Flash. Now, DGX Spark supports clusters of up to eight units in manual configuration, enabling larger models, longer contexts, concurrent agents and distributed development. Ideal for small teams sharing a single cluster as a backend, with each developer running concurrent sessions against the same model, it delivers 1TB of unified memory — enough to run frontier-class models like GLM 5.3. Get started with the DGX Spark cluster playbook . NVIDIA Sync Model Launcher will also be available later this month. It simplifies access to local AI on a single DGX Spark or a cluster. With a few clicks, Model Launcher downloads a model and container suited to the configuration and connects the model to OpenCode. It automatically loads DGX Spark Skills for troubleshooting, device maintenance, access to official documentation and other workflow guidance. The October DGX Spark software update brings a new Wi-Fi Assistant that lets users switch networks when DGX Spark is running in appliance mode. Plus, DGX Spark Skills provide workflow-focused guidance in troubleshooting and device maintenance directly into NVIDIA Sync via OpenCode. DGX Spark systems are available directly from Acer , ASUS , Dell Technologies , GIGABYTE , HP , Lenovo, MSI and NVIDIA. DGX Station Puts Frontier Intelligence at the Desk For larger teams, DGX Station offers 748GB of coherent memory and up to 20 petaflops of AI performance, enabling developers to run advanced models like GLM 5.3 and serve 30+ users at speeds comparable to those provided by cloud models. Adding scale, NVIDIA Sync now supports DGX Station, simplifying connections between two Linux-based systems. Introducing Recursive Flint — A New Local Coding Model Optimized for RTX Spark Today, frontier AI lab Recursive Superintelligence released Recursive Flint , a local LLM built for fast, accurate coding. A 40-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 2.5 billion active parameters, Recursive Flint delivers fast inference and performs well in agentic coding benchmarks like S WE-Bench Pro v2, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-bench verified. It automates the full research loop: proposes ideas, implements them, runs experiments to validate ideas and uses the results to decide what to try next — creating specialized kernels that boosted Flint’s generation speed on RTX Spark by 55% without changing the model’s weights. title: Google Cloud and NVIDIA Announce General Availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin Infrastructure
body: Google Cloud and NVIDIA Announce General Availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin Infrastructure Google Cloud A5X instances, accelerated by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, support European innovators with next-generation agentic and reinforcement learning infrastructure. October 21, 2026 by Uttara Kumar 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! General availability of the instances is coming next month, with planned expansion of availability to Europe — bringing an integrated platform for training, inference and large-scale reinforcement learning to cloud customers. A5X instances bring together NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, Google Cloud Virgo Network and Google Cloud’s fourth-generation advanced liquid-cooling technology for demanding agentic inference and reinforcement learning workloads at scale. Google Cloud plans to scale its Vera Rubin-based infrastructure to as many as 960,000 Rubin GPUs across multiple sites. Ineffable Intelligence , a London-based technology company founded by AlphaGo creator David Silver, was the first customer to access A5X. Ineffable is using the platform to advance large-scale reinforcement learning and shape “superlearner” systems that learn continuously from experience. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Learning through interaction requires a continuous cycle of generating experience, evaluating outcomes and updating models, requiring infrastructure that can support the entire process at scale. A5X brings Vera Rubin into Google Cloud’s AI Hypercomputer as an integrated system, combining compute, networking and storage to support experience-driven learning at scale. “We’re building superlearners that continually improve through their own experience,” said David Silver, founder and CEO of Ineffable Intelligence. “That demands both substantial compute and a tight connection between generating experience and training on it, so each improvement in the agent can quickly shape its next experience. Vera Rubin’s combination of compute performance and high-bandwidth connectivity, between the Vera CPU and Rubin GPUs and between the Rubin GPUs within the rack, allow us to push the scale and ambition of our reinforcement learning research further.” WPP , a London-based marketing and communications company, has also demonstrated its creative agent reference architecture on NVIDIA Vera Rubin-based A5X instances using NVIDIA Nemotron models and NVIDIA OpenShell, part of the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for safe AI agents. The agents turn conversational requests into multistep creative workflows, such as video generation, upscaling and restyling, with human approval before execution. OpenShell provides governed sandboxes for agent execution, helping control access to sensitive brand assets and creative tools. In WPP’s initial tests, workloads that typically required a multi-node cluster ran on a single A5X instance. As organizations deploy agentic systems, they need to protect the proprietary models and sensitive data that power these systems — even when running on infrastructure they don’t own. Google Cloud will be among the first cloud providers to offer NVIDIA Confidential Computing at rack scale on bare metal instances such as A4X Max instances powered by NVIDIA GB300 NVL72. Additionally, Google Cloud is making Confidential Computing generally available on G4 VMs powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, offering a flexible platform for confidential inference and fine-tuning. Customers including Vertebrae , Polaris Cloud and Confidential Core AI are using Confidential G4 for conversational privacy, verifiable agent execution and policy-governed enterprise intelligence. To support energy-efficient deployment at scale, Google Cloud and NVIDIA are exploring NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS capabilities for Vera Rubin-based infrastructure to help optimize performance per watt and expand capacity within available data-center power budgets. Learn more about NVIDIA Vera Rubin and Google Cloud A5X instances. title: NVIDIA Cloud Partners Scale Across Europe — Sovereign, Open and Built for Safe AI Agents
body: NVIDIA Cloud Partners Scale Across Europe — Sovereign, Open and Built for Safe AI Agents Growing ecosystem of AI clouds across Europe, Nordics, Africa and Central Asia build full-stack NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin AI factories as AI-native companies drive demand for sovereign compute, training, inference and post-training services. October 21, 2026 by Stuart Pitts 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Sovereign: AI Clouds Building European AI Infrastructure Europe is home to world-class research, engineering talent, industrial expertise, data, the next generation of models and applications that requires large-scale computing close to where that knowledge resides. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow. As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence. Nscale is using the NVIDIA DSX Platform to coordinate power allocation with workload requirements. In tests using NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems, Nscale demonstrated that NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS enabled 37% more GPUs and nearly 50% higher aggregate inference throughput within the same provisioned power budget. Nscale also plans to deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure for frontier-model training and production workloads to support leading model and application builders using its full-stack, vertically integrated platform with expansion across five European markets. Crusoe is developing Spark, its liquid-cooled modular AI factories designed for the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, to bring Crusoe Cloud capacity closer to users for low-latency AI inference. Crusoe Cloud serves leading model and application builders across EMEA, including Base44, Gradium, LTX and Wonderful. Aleria, Cassava Technologies , Firebird , G42 , Radiant, SWI Compute and Vultr are also developing and expanding NVIDIA-powered AI infrastructure across Europe, the Nordics, Africa and Central Asia. Regional capacity from AI clouds combines the full-stack NVIDIA DSX AI Factory platform , including NVIDIA Vera Rubin, NVIDIA BlueField and NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking, giving customers greater choice and control over where workloads and data reside while advancing sovereign computing services and economic growth. Open: Models and Libraries, From Training to Inference Across the ecosystem, AI clouds are expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure and services for developers to build applications with open models and libraries. This new capacity supports model training, fine-tuning for specialized tasks and inference at scale, including applications deployed at the edge. For production inference, Nebius has adopted NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX, using Spectrum-X Ethernet networking to integrate it with Vera Rubin NVL72 on Nebius Token Factory. The combination will bring faster token generation to latency-sensitive applications and agentic systems through the platform’s managed serverless and dedicated endpoints and familiar application programming interfaces. For robotics and physical AI, Nebius offers a purpose-built AI cloud solution that includes its full-stack Physical AI Workbench. Robotics companies including Rhoda AI , RoboForce and Sereact are building on the platform. The company also launched three NVIDIA retail agent blueprints — covering inventory, store operations, and fine-tuning —- into early access on Nebius infrastructure. Nebius is expanding its cloud services widely across the continent with its Physical AI Living Lab, and in Germany as a computer supplier for the Next Frontier Challenge of SPRIND, the Federal Agency for Breakthrough Innovation. Baseten has developed a specialized model for code-review routing with Nemotron 3.5 Lightning used by CodeRabbit. Through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, CodeRabbit improved routing agreement from 75.8% to 80.7% while reducing estimated inference costs by 50% for the evaluated workload. The results demonstrate how AI developers can customize NVIDIA open models for specialized tasks while improving accuracy and inference efficiency. Fireworks and Era4 are partnering to bring open models to enterprises across the U.K. and Europe. The collaboration combines Fireworks ’ model training and inference platform with direct liquid-cooled capacity powered by NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs at Era4’s Chesterfield facility, supporting plans for enterprise AI solutions in financial services, insurance and life sciences. Mistral is expanding its NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure to support model training, customization and inference. The expansion includes NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure planned for delivery in 2027. Trained on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral -operated European data centers, Mistral Large 4 is the company’s latest frontier multimodal model, advancing capabilities across coding, agentic workflows and multimodal understanding. Verda plans to deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin, continuing to promote open weight models with NVIDIA Nemotron and NVIDIA Cosmos already in production, and using the NVIDIA Dynamo open source framework for inference optimization. Safe: Secure Boundaries for AI Agents, From Silicon to Software As developers connect models to tools and business systems, they also need controls over what agents can access and do. Announced at GTC Berlin, the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture with support from AI cloud ecosystem partners. Built on the foundation of NVIDIA OpenShell secure runtime software, the architecture is designed to give organizations full-stack control to deploy AI agents with clear boundaries around what agents can access and do. NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 for model inference, NVIDIA Vera CPUs with OpenShell for agent harnesses and tool use, and NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs running NVIDIA Sentry for in-silicon enforcement. Each play a distinct role in delivering that control, working together so agents can achieve what they’re meant to do without moving beyond the boundaries people set for them. Partners including Aleria , Baseten , Cassava , CoreWeave , Crusoe , DigitalOcean , Firebird , Fireworks, Firmus , G42 , GMI Cloud , IREN , Lambda , Lightning AI, Nebius , Nscale , Radiant Verda and Vultr are supporting the OpenShell Reference Architecture to enable secure agentic deployments for their customers. Together, European AI clouds are connecting regional infrastructure investment with the work of building and deploying AI. Expanded capacity gives builders more places to run workloads. Model and inference services help them put that capacity to use. Agent controls address what applications are allowed to do as they move into production. Explore NVIDIA Cloud Partners for infrastructure and services, and the OpenShell Reference Architecture for agent deployment controls.
